ingredients: 1 tsp salt plus 1/2 tsp for the cabbage
3 tbsp Chinkiang black vinegar, to serve
steps: Mix the flour and water into a firm dough, knead 5 minutes until smooth, cover and rest 30 minutes.
Toss the cabbage with 1/2 tsp salt, leave 10 minutes, then squeeze out as much water as possible.
Stir the pork with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, ginger and 1 tsp salt in one direction until sticky, then fold in the cabbage, spring onions and sesame oil.
Roll the dough into a rope, cut into 40 pieces, roll each into a thin 8 cm round, fill with a heaped teaspoon of filling and pinch into a pleated half-moon.
Boil in a large pot of water; each time it returns to the boil add 125 ml cold water, and after the third boil (about 8 minutes) the dumplings float, puff and the pork is fully cooked.
Drain and serve hot with black vinegar mixed with a little chili oil and garlic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g Chinese chives (jiucai) or napa cabbage, finely chopped
1 tsp flour mixed into 150 ml water, for the crust
steps: Stir the hot water into the flour, knead into a soft dough and rest covered for 30 minutes.
Beat the pork with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, ginger and salt until sticky, then mix in the chives.
Roll 30 thin wrappers, fill each and pinch only the middle and ends so the dumpling stays long and open-ended.
Heat the oil in a lidded non-stick pan over medium heat, line up the dumplings and fry 2 minutes until the bottoms start to colour.
Pour in the flour-water, cover and steam 7-8 minutes until the water evaporates and the pork is cooked through, then uncover and fry 2 minutes more until the bottoms are crisp and golden.
Invert onto a plate crust-side up and serve with black vinegar and ginger slivers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g raw prawns, peeled and chopped
2 tbsp dried small shrimp (xiami) or a sheet of nori
steps: Mix the pork, prawns, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, ginger and salt, stirring in one direction until sticky.
Put a teaspoon of filling in the centre of each wrapper, fold into a triangle, then bring two corners together and seal with a dab of water.
Bring the stock to a simmer and season with salt; divide the dried shrimp, spring onions and sesame oil between 4 bowls.
Boil the wontons in a separate pot of water for 4-5 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Lift the wontons into the bowls and ladle the hot stock over to serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 ml water or stock, for the filling
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and warm water into a smooth dough, knead 8 minutes and leave covered for about 1 hour until doubled.
Beat the pork with soy sauce, oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine and ginger, add the 60 ml water a little at a time until absorbed, then mix in the spring onions and sesame oil.
Knock back the dough, divide into 16 pieces, roll each into a 10 cm round thicker in the middle, fill and pleat closed at the top.
Set each bun on a square of baking paper in a bamboo steamer and rest 20 minutes until slightly puffy.
Steam over boiling water on high heat for 15 minutes, then turn off the heat and wait 3 minutes before lifting the lid so the buns do not collapse.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, water and oil into a dough and knead 10 minutes until very smooth.
Cover and leave about 1 hour until doubled in size.
Knead out the air, roll into a log and cut into 12 pieces, or shape each into a smooth dome.
Place on baking paper in a steamer and rest 20 minutes until slightly risen.
Steam over boiling water on high heat for 15 minutes, turn off the heat and wait 3 minutes before opening; serve with stir-fries or porridge.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp Sichuan pepper powder (huajiao fen), optional
steps: Make a dough with flour, yeast, sugar and water, knead 10 minutes and leave about 1 hour until doubled.
Roll the dough into a large rectangle 5 mm thick, brush with the oil and sprinkle with salt, Sichuan pepper and spring onions.
Roll up tightly from the long side, cut into 12 pieces, stack two pieces, press a chopstick across the middle and twist the ends underneath to make a flower.
Rest the rolls on baking paper in a steamer for 20 minutes.
Steam on high heat for 15 minutes, then wait 3 minutes with the heat off before lifting the lid.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp neutral oil plus 3 tbsp for frying
1 tbsp flour for the oil paste
steps: Stir the hot water into the flour, knead into a soft dough and rest covered for 30 minutes.
Mix 3 tbsp hot oil with 1 tbsp flour, salt and five-spice to make a paste (youxu).
Divide the dough into 4, roll each thin, spread with paste, sprinkle with spring onions, roll up into a rope, coil into a snail and flatten to 5 mm.
Fry each pancake in 1 tbsp oil over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and flaky.
Scrunch the hot pancake from the sides to open the layers, cut into wedges and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g Chinese chives (jiucai), finely chopped; substitute garlic chives or spring onions
30 g dried glass noodles (fensi), soaked and chopped
1 tbsp dried small shrimp, optional (omit to keep it eggetarian)
steps: Mix the flour and hot water into a soft dough and rest covered 30 minutes.
Scramble the eggs in 1 tbsp oil until just set, chop finely and cool.
Toss the chives with the sesame oil first, then mix with the eggs, glass noodles and salt just before filling so they stay dry.
Roll 8 thin rounds, fill one half with filling, fold into a half-moon and crimp the edge.
Pan-fry in the remaining oil over medium-low heat for 4-5 minutes per side until golden and crisp; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Stir-fry the pork in 1 tbsp oil over high heat for 2 minutes until no longer pink.
Add the cabbage, carrot, mushrooms and bean sprouts, season with soy sauce and sugar and stir-fry 2 minutes, then stir in the cornstarch slurry to bind and cool completely.
Place 2 tbsp filling near one corner of each wrapper, fold in the sides, roll up tightly and seal with a little water.
Deep-fry at 170°C in batches for 4-5 minutes until golden and crisp, then drain on a rack.
Serve hot with Chinkiang vinegar or sweet chili sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp neutral oil, for the dough
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt, add the oil and liquid and stir into a soft, sticky dough without kneading hard.
Fold the dough a few times every 15 minutes over the first hour, then oil it, wrap and refrigerate overnight (8 hours) and bring to room temperature for 1 hour.
Stretch the dough into a strip 10 cm wide and 1 cm thick and cut into 2.5 cm wide strips.
Stack two strips, press a chopstick lengthwise down the centre to join them, and stretch to about 25 cm.
Deep-fry at 200°C, turning constantly, for 1-2 minutes until puffed and deep golden; serve with hot soy milk or congee.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 l water, plus water for soaking
3-4 tbsp sugar, or salt for savoury style
steps: Soak the soybeans in plenty of water overnight (8 hours) until doubled, then drain.
Blend the beans with the 1.5 l water for 2 minutes until very smooth.
Strain through a muslin cloth or nut-milk bag, squeezing out all the milk.
Bring to the boil in a large pot over medium heat, stirring often, then simmer gently for 10 minutes, skimming foam, because raw soy milk must be fully cooked.
Sweeten with sugar and serve hot with youtiao, or serve savoury (xian doujiang) with soy sauce, vinegar, chopped spring onion and chili oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tsp gypsum powder (shigao, food-grade calcium sulfate) or 1 1/2 tsp glucono-delta-lactone
60 ml cold water for the coagulant
200 ml water and 3 slices ginger, for syrup
steps: Blend the soaked beans with 1.2 l water, strain through muslin and boil the soy milk gently for 10 minutes, skimming foam.
In a large heatproof bowl, stir the gypsum and cornstarch into the 60 ml cold water.
Let the soy milk cool to about 85°C, then pour it from a height into the coagulant bowl in one go, skim the foam and do not stir.
Cover with a cloth and leave 20 minutes until it sets into a soft custard.
Simmer the brown sugar, water and ginger for 5 minutes to make syrup, then spoon the tofu pudding into bowls and pour syrup over; in the north it is served savoury with soy-mushroom gravy instead.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Wash the rice twice, drain and toss with the oil and salt.
Bring the water to a boil in a heavy pot, add the rice and return to the boil, stirring so it does not stick.
Lower the heat and simmer partly covered for 50-60 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the grains break down into a creamy porridge.
Ladle into bowls and serve with zhacai, spring onions, fermented tofu or salted duck egg on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g rock sugar (bingtang) or brown sugar
steps: Soak the red beans, peanuts, lotus seeds and black rice overnight (8 hours), then drain.
Simmer the red beans, peanuts and lotus seeds in the water for 30 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the glutinous rice, black rice, millet and mung beans and simmer gently for 45 minutes, stirring often to stop sticking.
Add the red dates, longan and rock sugar and cook 15 minutes more until thick and all the beans are tender.
Serve warm on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month (Laba Festival).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp black tea leaves or 3 tea bags (Pu-erh or red tea)
steps: Boil the eggs 8 minutes, cool in cold water, then gently tap each shell all over with a spoon to crack without peeling.
Bring the water, tea, soy sauces, spices, sugar and salt to the boil.
Add the eggs and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes.
Turn off the heat and leave the eggs in the liquid in the fridge overnight (8 hours or longer) for a marbled pattern.
Peel and serve warm or cold as a snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Lightly score each egg 3-4 times with a knife so the braise can soak in.
Bring the soy sauces, sugar, wine, spices, ginger and water to the boil.
Add the eggs and simmer gently 30 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep brown.
Rest in the liquid at least 1 hour (or overnight in the fridge) and serve halved over rice or noodles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rinse the peanuts and dry them thoroughly on a towel.
Put the peanuts and cold oil together in a wok and heat over medium-low heat, stirring constantly.
Fry 6-8 minutes until they crackle and the skins look slightly darker, then remove immediately as they keep cooking.
Drain, toss with salt (and sugar) while warm and let cool completely to crisp; serve with beer or congee.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g cold cooked jasmine rice, preferably day-old
steps: Break up the cold rice with your hands so no clumps remain.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering, pour in the eggs and stir 20 seconds until half set.
Immediately add the rice and toss continuously for 3-4 minutes, breaking the egg into small pieces, until the grains are hot and separate.
Season with salt, white pepper and soy sauce, add the spring onions and toss 30 seconds more, then serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g fresh egg noodles (chow mein noodles)
150 g chicken breast or pork, thinly sliced
1/2 small cabbage or bok choy, shredded
3 spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
steps: Blanch the noodles in boiling water for 1 minute, rinse, drain well and toss with 1 tbsp oil.
Toss the meat with cornstarch and 1 tsp soy sauce, then stir-fry in 1 tbsp oil over high heat for 2-3 minutes until cooked through and set aside.
Fry the noodles in the remaining oil, spread out, for 2 minutes until lightly crisp in spots.
Add the cabbage, bean sprouts, spring onions and the meat, pour in the sauces and toss for 2 minutes until evenly coloured and the vegetables just wilt, then serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Tomato and Egg Noodle Soup (Xihongshi Jidan Mian)

steps: Scramble the eggs in 1 tbsp hot oil until just set and remove.
Fry the spring onion whites and tomatoes in the remaining oil over medium-high heat for 4 minutes, pressing until they collapse into a sauce.
Add the water, soy sauce, sugar and salt and simmer 5 minutes.
Cook the noodles separately according to the packet, drain and divide between bowls.
Return the eggs to the soup, heat 1 minute, ladle over the noodles and top with spring onion greens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Tomato and Egg Stir-fry (Xihongshi Chao Jidan)

steps: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat, pour in the eggs and stir gently for 30 seconds until fluffy and just set, then remove.
Add the remaining oil and tomatoes, stir-fry 3 minutes until soft and juicy, adding the water, sugar and salt.
Return the eggs, toss for 30 seconds, sprinkle with spring onion and serve over steamed rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Stir-fried Eggs with Chinese Chives (Jiucai Chao Dan)

ingredients: 150 g Chinese chives (jiucai), cut into 3 cm lengths; substitute garlic chives
steps: Beat the eggs with half the salt and the Shaoxing wine.
Scramble the eggs in 2 tbsp hot oil over high heat until just set in large curds, then remove.
Stir-fry the chives in the remaining oil for 1 minute until bright green and just wilted, adding the rest of the salt.
Return the eggs, toss for 20 seconds and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 270 ml warm water or stock (1.5 times the egg volume)
steps: Beat the eggs with salt, then whisk in the warm water gently to avoid bubbles.
Strain the mixture into a shallow heatproof bowl and skim off any foam.
Cover the bowl with a plate or cling film and steam over gently boiling water on low-medium heat for 10-12 minutes until just set and still wobbly.
Drizzle with soy sauce and sesame oil, scatter with spring onion and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 700 g skin-on pork belly (wuhua rou), cut into 3 cm cubes
steps: Put the pork in cold water, bring to the boil, simmer 3 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Dry-fry the pork in a wok over medium heat for 5 minutes until some fat renders and the edges brown, then push aside.
Melt the rock sugar in the fat over low heat until amber, then toss the pork to coat.
Add ginger, spring onions, spices, wine, both soy sauces and hot water, bring to the boil, cover and simmer on low for 60-70 minutes until tender.
Uncover, raise the heat and reduce for 5-10 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy, and serve with steamed rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Sweet and Sour Pork Ribs (Tangcu Paigu)

ingredients: 700 g pork spare ribs, cut into 5 cm pieces
50 g rock sugar or 4 tbsp sugar
steps: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for 3 minutes, rinse and drain.
Fry the ribs in the oil over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the ginger, wine, soy sauces, 2 tbsp vinegar, sugar and hot water, bring to the boil, cover and simmer 35 minutes until tender.
Uncover, add the remaining vinegar and reduce over high heat, tossing, for 5-8 minutes until the sauce is sticky and coats the ribs.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve hot or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g pork loin, cut into thin strips
2 green bell peppers or long green chilies (qingjiao), cut into strips
steps: Toss the pork with half the soy sauce, the wine and the cornstarch and leave 10 minutes.
Stir-fry the pork in 2 tbsp oil over high heat for 2 minutes until it turns pale and is cooked through, then remove.
Fry the garlic and peppers in the remaining oil for 1-2 minutes until bright and slightly blistered, adding the salt.
Return the pork with the remaining soy sauce and oyster sauce, toss 30 seconds and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g firm tofu, cut into 1 cm thick triangles
100 g pork belly or pork loin, thinly sliced
4 dried wood ear mushrooms (mu'er), soaked and torn
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
steps: Shallow-fry the tofu in 3 tbsp oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden, then drain.
Stir-fry the pork in the remaining oil for 2 minutes until cooked and lightly browned, then add the doubanjiang and garlic and fry 30 seconds until the oil turns red.
Add the tofu, wood ear, soy sauce, sugar and water and simmer 4 minutes.
Add the pepper, cook 1 minute, then stir in the cornstarch slurry until glossy and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole carp or sea bass (about 800 g), cleaned and scored
steps: Pat the fish completely dry and rub with salt inside and out.
Fry the fish in hot oil over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until golden, without moving it until the skin releases.
Add ginger, garlic and spring onion whites, then pour wine and vinegar down the side of the wok, followed by soy sauces, sugar and hot water.
Simmer over medium heat for 12-15 minutes, spooning the sauce over, until the flesh flakes easily at the bone.
Lift onto a platter, reduce the sauce for 2 minutes, pour over and top with spring onion greens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Score the wings twice on each side, blanch in boiling water 2 minutes and drain.
Fry the wings in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Add ginger, star anise, wine, soy sauces and cola, bring to the boil and simmer uncovered 15-20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Raise the heat and toss for 3-5 minutes until the sauce reduces to a sticky glaze, then sprinkle with sesame seeds.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g firm tofu, cut into thin strips
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
10 g dried wood ear mushrooms, soaked and shredded
3 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 4 tbsp water
steps: Bring the stock to the boil, add the pork and stir to separate; simmer 2 minutes until cooked through.
Add the shiitake, wood ear, bamboo shoots and tofu and simmer 5 minutes.
Season with soy sauce, then stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook 1 minute until thickened.
Turn off the heat, drizzle in the egg in a thin stream while stirring gently to form ribbons.
Stir in the vinegar and white pepper, taste for sour and hot balance, finish with sesame oil and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
steps: Bring the stock to the boil with the tomato, salt and white pepper and simmer 3 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook 1 minute until lightly thickened.
Lower the heat to a gentle simmer, stir the soup in one direction and pour in the egg in a thin stream to form silky ribbons.
Turn off the heat, add sesame oil and spring onions and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Hot and Sour Shredded Potatoes (Suanla Tudou Si)

ingredients: 2 large potatoes, cut into fine matchsticks
4 dried red chilies, cut in half
2 tbsp white rice vinegar or black vinegar
steps: Soak the potato strips in cold water for 10 minutes, rinsing until the water runs clear, then drain well.
Heat the oil over medium heat and fry the Sichuan peppercorns and chilies for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add garlic.
Raise the heat to high, add the potatoes and stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add vinegar down the side of the wok, then salt and sugar, and toss 1-2 minutes more until the potatoes are just cooked but still crunchy.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g bok choy or Shanghai green (qingcai), halved
steps: Wash the bok choy well and shake dry.
Fry half the garlic in the oil over medium heat for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Raise the heat to high, add the bok choy and toss 1 minute, then add water, salt and sugar and stir-fry 1-2 minutes until the stems are tender-crisp.
Add the remaining garlic, toss 15 seconds and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g napa cabbage, stems only or mixed, cut diagonally into slices
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Mix vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, salt and cornstarch slurry in a small bowl.
Heat the oil over high heat and fry the chilies and garlic for 20 seconds.
Add the cabbage stems first and stir-fry 2 minutes, then the leaves for 1 minute until wilted but still crisp.
Pour in the sauce and toss 30 seconds until glossy, then serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Smash the cucumbers with the flat of a cleaver until they split, then cut into bite-size chunks.
Toss with salt and leave 10 minutes, then drain the liquid.
Mix garlic, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, chili oil and sesame oil.
Toss the cucumbers with the dressing and serve chilled.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Soak the wood ear in cold water for 30 minutes until fully rehydrated, then trim the hard bases and tear into pieces.
Blanch in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, then plunge into iced water and drain well.
Mix the garlic, chili, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, chili oil and sesame oil.
Toss the wood ear with the dressing and coriander and serve cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Carefully turn the tofu out onto a plate and drain any water.
Scatter the diced century eggs over and around the tofu.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil and chili oil and pour over.
Garnish with spring onion and coriander and serve cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp salt for the overnight rub
3 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns
steps: Rub the beef with salt and refrigerate overnight (8 hours), then blanch in boiling water for 5 minutes and rinse.
Fry the sweet bean sauce in a little oil for 1 minute, then add all the remaining ingredients and bring to the boil.
Add the beef, cover and simmer on low heat for 2 hours until a chopstick slides in easily.
Turn off the heat and leave the beef to cool in the liquid for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Slice thinly across the grain and serve cold with a drizzle of the braising liquid, garlic and chili oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g extra-firm tofu, cut into 3 cm cubes
120 ml Chinese baijiu or vodka, for dipping (cooking use)
steps: Arrange the dried, pressed tofu cubes apart on a clean rack in a covered box and keep at 15-20°C for 5-7 days until each cube grows a white fuzzy mold (the traditional maodoufu stage); discard any cube with black, green or pink mold or a foul smell.
Mix the salt, chili flakes, Sichuan pepper and five-spice on a plate.
Dip each cube briefly in the spirit, then roll in the spice mixture and pack into the sterilised jar.
Cover with oil, seal and leave in a cool place for 2-3 weeks until creamy and pungent, then refrigerate.
Serve small pieces with congee or steamed buns; store-bought furu is a safe and convenient substitute.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml rice vinegar (white or light rice vinegar)
steps: Peel the garlic and trim off the root ends; make sure the cloves are completely dry.
Pack into the clean, dry jar.
Pour in the vinegar (stirred with sugar if using) until the garlic is fully covered, then seal.
Keep in a cool place out of direct sun for 15-20 days until the cloves turn jade green, starting on the Laba festival, and serve with jiaozi on Chinese New Year.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 50 g Sichuan chili flakes (erjingtiao or similar), coarse
steps: Put the chili flakes, sesame seeds and salt in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the oil with the ginger and spices over low heat for 8-10 minutes until the aromatics are golden and fragrant, then strain them out.
Bring the oil to about 180°C, then pour one third over the chili and stir as it sizzles.
Let the oil cool to 140°C and pour in the rest, stir and leave to cool completely before jarring.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 24 dried bamboo leaves (zongye) and kitchen string
400 g pork belly, cut into 12 chunks
3 tbsp light soy sauce plus 2 tbsp for the rice
steps: Soak the rice overnight (8 hours), and marinate the pork with 3 tbsp light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, wine and sugar overnight in the fridge; soak the bamboo leaves in hot water for 1 hour.
Drain the rice and mix with 2 tbsp soy sauce and the salt.
Overlap two leaves, fold into a cone, add a spoon of rice, a piece of pork (and egg yolk), cover with more rice, fold the leaves over into a tetrahedron and tie tightly with string.
Submerge the zongzi in a large pot of boiling water, weigh down with a plate and simmer 2.5-3 hours, topping up with boiling water, until the rice is soft and sticky and the pork is tender.
Unwrap and serve hot for the Dragon Boat Festival (Duanwu).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g black sesame seeds, toasted and finely ground
50 g softened butter or vegetable shortening (traditionally lard)
3 slices ginger and 2 tbsp brown sugar, for the soup
steps: Mix the ground sesame, sugar and butter into a paste, chill 20 minutes and roll into 16 small balls.
Gradually stir the warm water into the rice flour and knead into a smooth, play-dough-like dough.
Divide into 16 pieces, flatten each into a cup, enclose a sesame ball and roll smooth.
Simmer the water with ginger and brown sugar for 5 minutes.
Drop in the tangyuan and simmer gently 5-6 minutes until they float and puff, then serve in the ginger syrup for the Lantern Festival.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g brown sugar (or Chinese slab sugar, pian tang)
6 dried red dates, pitted and halved
steps: Dissolve the brown sugar in the hot water and cool to warm.
Stir the syrup into the rice flour with 1 tbsp oil to make a smooth, thick batter.
Pour into an oiled 20 cm cake tin, decorate with red dates and sesame seeds.
Steam over boiling water on medium-high heat for 50-60 minutes until set and translucent, topping up the water as needed.
Cool completely, then slice; it can be eaten as is or pan-fried in the remaining oil until crisp at the edges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g sweet red bean paste (hongdou sha)
steps: Dissolve the sugar in the hot water, then mix into the flour and starch and knead into a soft dough.
Divide into 16 pieces, flatten each, fill with a teaspoon ball of bean paste and roll closed.
Dampen each ball lightly and roll in sesame seeds, pressing so they stick.
Put the balls into oil heated to 140°C and fry 6-8 minutes, pressing gently against the side of the wok with a ladle so they expand.
Raise the heat to 170°C for the last 2 minutes until golden and puffed, drain and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 30 g candied winter melon or dried apricots
steps: Soak the rice overnight (8 hours), drain and steam on a cloth for 30 minutes until tender, then mix with oil and sugar while hot.
Oil a medium heatproof bowl and arrange the dates, lotus seeds, raisins, candied fruit, goji and walnuts in a pattern in the bottom.
Press half the rice over the fruit, spread the bean paste in the centre, and cover with the remaining rice, pressing firmly.
Steam over boiling water for 30 minutes until heated through.
Invert onto a plate, drizzle with a little sugar syrup and serve warm at New Year.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the flour, baking powder and eggs into a firm dough, knead 5 minutes and rest 20 minutes.
Roll out 2 mm thick, dust with flour and cut into thin noodles 5 cm long.
Deep-fry in batches at 170°C for 1 minute until pale golden and puffed, then drain.
Boil the sugar, maltose and water over medium heat to about 118°C (soft-ball stage), then toss in the fried strips, raisins and sesame seeds until coated.
Press firmly into an oiled tin, cool 30 minutes until set and cut into squares.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 30 g small tapioca pearls or glutinous rice balls, optional
steps: Soak the beans overnight (8 hours) and drain.
Bring the beans, water and tangerine peel to the boil, then simmer covered on low heat for 75 minutes until the beans burst and turn creamy.
Add the rock sugar (and tapioca pearls) and simmer 10-15 minutes more, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and the soup thickens.
Serve warm in winter or chilled in summer.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 strip kelp (haidai) or a few lily bulb petals, optional
steps: Rinse and soak the mung beans for 2 hours.
Bring the beans and water to the boil, then simmer covered for 30 minutes until the beans split open and are soft.
Stir in the rock sugar and simmer 5 minutes until dissolved.
Cool and serve chilled as a cooling summer drink-soup.

ingredients: 15 g dried white fungus (yin'er / snow fungus)
steps: Soak the white fungus in water for 1 hour until fully expanded, trim the hard yellow base and tear into small pieces.
Simmer the fungus, red dates and lotus seeds in the water on low heat for 75 minutes until the soup turns thick and gelatinous.
Add rock sugar and goji berries and simmer 10 minutes more.
Serve warm or chilled.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar over a bowl of warm water at high speed for 8-10 minutes until pale, tripled and leaving a thick ribbon.
Sift in the flour in two additions and fold gently, then fold in the milk and oil.
Pour into a 20 cm tin lined with baking paper and tap once to release large bubbles.
Steam over rapidly boiling water for 20-25 minutes until springy and a skewer comes out clean, keeping a cloth under the lid to catch drips.
Rest 3 minutes with the heat off, then unmould and slice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp jasmine green tea leaves (or jasmine pearls)
steps: Heat the water to 80-85°C, not boiling, to avoid bitterness.
Warm the teapot with a little hot water and discard.
Add the tea, pour over the water and steep 2-3 minutes.
Pour into small cups and serve plain; the leaves can be re-steeped 2-3 more times.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g soft tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans (douchi), rinsed and chopped
3 tbsp rapeseed oil (caiziyou) or vegetable oil
3 garlic cloves and 10 g ginger, minced
2 tsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
2 stalks garlic sprouts (suanmiao) or spring onions, cut in 2 cm pieces
steps: Simmer the tofu cubes in lightly salted water for 2 minutes to firm them, then drain gently.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the minced meat until browned and crisp at the edges, about 4 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium, add the doubanjiang and fry 1 minute until the oil turns red, then add the douchi, chili flakes, garlic and ginger and fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the stock, slide in the tofu and simmer 5 minutes, nudging the tofu with the back of the ladle rather than stirring.
Add the garlic sprouts, then thicken with the cornstarch slurry in two or three additions until the sauce clings and glistens.
Serve in a bowl topped with the ground Sichuan pepper, with steamed rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g boneless chicken thigh, cut into 1.5 cm cubes
1 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp Shaoxing wine, for marinade
10 dried red chilies, snipped in half and seeds shaken out
3 spring onions (white parts), cut into 1.5 cm pieces
3 garlic cloves and 10 g ginger, thinly sliced
2 tbsp Zhenjiang black vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp light soy, 1 tsp cornstarch, 3 tbsp water (sauce)
steps: Toss the chicken with soy, Shaoxing wine and cornstarch and rest 15 minutes; mix the sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chilies and Sichuan peppercorns and fry 20 seconds until the chilies darken slightly but do not blacken.
Turn the heat to high, add the chicken and stir-fry until the pieces separate and turn white, about 3 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger and spring onion and stir-fry 1 minute until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir the sauce, pour it in and toss until it thickens and coats the meat with a glossy lychee-flavoured (sweet-sour) glaze.
Toss in the peanuts and serve immediately with steamed rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g skin-on pork belly, in one piece
3 slices ginger and 1 spring onion, for boiling
1 tsp sweet bean sauce (tianmianjiang) or hoisin
4 stalks garlic sprouts (suanmiao) or leeks, sliced diagonally
steps: Simmer the pork belly in water with ginger and spring onion for 25 minutes until a chopstick pierces it easily, then cool and chill 30 minutes so it slices neatly.
Cut the pork into thin 3 mm slices.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the pork and fry until the fat renders and the slices curl into "lamp-cup" shapes, about 5 minutes.
Push the pork aside, fry the doubanjiang in the fat for 30 seconds until red, then add douchi, sweet bean sauce and sugar and toss everything together.
Add the garlic sprouts and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes until just tender, then serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g pork loin, cut into thin matchsticks
1 tsp Shaoxing wine, 1/2 tsp salt, 2 tsp cornstarch (marinade)
2 tbsp pickled chili paste (paola jiao) or sambal oelek
50 g wood ear mushrooms, soaked and shredded
100 g winter bamboo shoots or carrot, shredded
3 garlic cloves and 15 g ginger, minced
1.5 tbsp sugar, 1.5 tbsp Zhenjiang black vinegar, 1 tbsp light soy, 1 tsp cornstarch, 3 tbsp stock (sauce)
steps: Mix the pork with wine, salt and cornstarch and set aside 10 minutes; whisk the sauce ingredients together.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the pork until it separates and turns pale, about 1 minute.
Push the pork aside, add the pickled chili paste and fry 30 seconds until the oil turns red, then add garlic and ginger and fry until fragrant.
Add the wood ear and bamboo shoots and stir-fry 2 minutes until hot and crisp-tender.
Pour in the sauce, toss until glossy and thickened, add the spring onions and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g long Chinese eggplants, cut into finger-length batons
2 tbsp pickled chili paste (paola jiao) or doubanjiang
4 garlic cloves and 15 g ginger, minced
150 ml vegetable stock and 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Toss the eggplant with salt and leave 15 minutes, then squeeze gently and pat dry.
Heat 4 tbsp oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the eggplant in batches until golden and soft, about 5 minutes, then remove.
Add the remaining oil, fry the chili paste 30 seconds until red, then add garlic and ginger and fry until fragrant.
Add stock, sugar and soy, return the eggplant and simmer 3 minutes until it absorbs the sauce.
Thicken with the cornstarch slurry, stir in the vinegar and spring onions, and serve hot with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g white fish fillets (grass carp, sea bass or tilapia), sliced 5 mm thick
1 egg white, 1 tbsp cornstarch, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp Shaoxing wine (marinade)
300 g bean sprouts or napa cabbage
4 garlic cloves and 15 g ginger, minced
20 dried red chilies, cut in sections
steps: Coat the fish slices in egg white, cornstarch, salt and wine and set aside 15 minutes.
Blanch the bean sprouts 1 minute, drain and spread in a deep serving bowl.
Heat 3 tbsp oil in a wok over medium heat, fry the doubanjiang 1 minute until red, add garlic and ginger, then pour in the stock and bring to a simmer.
Slide in the fish slices one by one and poach gently 2 to 3 minutes until opaque and flaking, then pour fish and broth over the sprouts.
Scatter the chilies and Sichuan peppercorns over the fish, heat the remaining oil until smoking, and pour it over so the spices sizzle; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g beef flank, sliced thinly across the grain
1 tbsp cornstarch, 1 tbsp light soy, 1 tbsp water (marinade)
3 garlic cloves and 10 g ginger, minced
2 tbsp Sichuan chili flakes and 1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper
steps: Massage the beef with cornstarch, soy and water until the liquid is absorbed and leave 10 minutes.
Stir-fry the celery and bean sprouts in 1 tbsp oil for 2 minutes, season lightly with salt and place in a deep bowl.
Fry the doubanjiang in 3 tbsp oil over medium heat for 1 minute, add garlic and ginger, then pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Add the beef slices, separate them with chopsticks and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until just cooked, then pour everything over the vegetables.
Sprinkle with chili flakes and Sichuan pepper, heat the remaining oil until smoking and pour it over to sizzle; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp salt and 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted together (dry cure)
30 g jasmine or black tea leaves (smoking)
50 g raw rice and 50 g brown sugar (smoking)
steps: Rub the duck inside and out with the wine and the salt-peppercorn mixture and refrigerate overnight, covered.
Steam the duck with ginger and spring onions in the cavity over high heat for 1.5 hours until tender, then pat completely dry.

Line a wok with foil, add tea, rice, sugar and orange peel, set a rack over and place the duck on it, cover tightly and heat over medium-high; once smoke appears, smoke 15 minutes, turn the duck and smoke 10 minutes more, with the kitchen well ventilated.
Heat oil to 180 C and deep-fry the duck, ladling oil over, for 5 to 8 minutes until the skin is crisp and mahogany.
Rest 10 minutes, chop into pieces and serve with lotus-leaf buns or steamed rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g lean beef (rump or flank), cut into thin strips
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and 1/2 tsp salt
3 celery stalks, cut into thin strips
1 tsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp sugar
1/2 tsp ground Sichuan pepper and 1 tsp sesame oil
steps: Mix the beef with wine and salt.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and stir-fry the beef patiently for 10 to 12 minutes until the moisture evaporates and the strips turn dark, dry and slightly chewy.
Push the beef aside, fry the doubanjiang in the oil for 1 minute until red, then toss with the beef.
Add the ginger, carrot and celery and stir-fry 2 minutes until just tender.
Season with soy and sugar, finish with Sichuan pepper and sesame oil, and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp light soy and 1 tbsp dark soy
2 tbsp pickled chili paste (paola jiao), 3 garlic cloves minced, 1 tbsp black vinegar (fish-fragrant topping)
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water and 2 chopped spring onions
steps: Blanch the knuckle in boiling water for 5 minutes, scrape the skin clean and rinse.
Place in a pot with ginger, spring onions, wine, rock sugar, soy sauces and spices, add water to cover and braise covered on low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is meltingly tender.
Lift the knuckle into a serving dish and reduce 300 ml of the braising liquid until slightly syrupy.
In a wok, fry the chili paste and garlic in 1 tbsp oil for 1 minute, add the reduced liquid and vinegar, then thicken with the slurry.
Pour the sauce over the knuckle, scatter spring onions and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp fermented tofu juice or light soy
1 tsp Shaoxing wine and 1 tsp sugar
80 g steamed-rice powder (zhengrou fen), or rice toasted with star anise and coarsely ground
2 tbsp vegetable oil and 3 tbsp water
1 tsp Sichuan chili flakes, 1/2 tsp ground Sichuan pepper, chopped coriander and garlic (topping)
steps: Mix the beef with doubanjiang, fermented tofu juice, wine, sugar, oil and water and marinate 15 minutes.
Add the rice powder and toss until every slice is coated and slightly moist.
Line small bamboo steamers with sweet potato cubes and pile the beef on top.
Steam over high heat for 25 to 30 minutes until the beef is tender and the rice coating is soft.
Top with chili flakes, Sichuan pepper, garlic and coriander and serve in the steamers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g beef tallow or vegetable oil
50 g dried chilies (erjingtiao), soaked and blitzed
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 bay leaves and 1 black cardamom
30 g fermented black beans and 30 g ginger, sliced
2 litres beef or chicken stock and 1 tbsp rock sugar
1 kg mixed dippers: thinly sliced beef and lamb, tripe, duck intestine, tofu, lotus root, potato, mushrooms, greens
dipping bowl per person: 3 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp minced garlic, chopped coriander and spring onion, pinch of salt
steps: Melt the tallow in a wok over low heat, add doubanjiang and fry 10 minutes until deep red and fragrant.
Add the blitzed chilies, ginger, black beans and whole spices and fry 5 more minutes without scorching.
Add the Sichuan peppercorns, stock and rock sugar and simmer 20 minutes to build the broth.
Transfer to a hot-pot pan on a tabletop burner and keep at a lively simmer; Chengdu style often uses a split pot with a mild mushroom broth on one side.
Diners cook dippers in the broth: thin meats 30 to 60 seconds until no pink remains, tripe and intestines until cooked through, vegetables until tender.
Dip each piece in the sesame-garlic oil before eating.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 450 g green beans, trimmed and dried well
2 tbsp Sichuan preserved mustard greens (yacai), or chopped pickled mustard
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and fry the beans, tossing, for 8 minutes until blistered, wrinkled and tender, then remove and pour off all but 1 tbsp oil.
Fry the chilies and Sichuan peppercorns in the oil for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the pork and stir-fry until cooked through and slightly crisp, about 3 minutes.
Add the yacai and garlic and stir-fry 30 seconds.
Return the beans, season with salt and sugar, toss 1 minute and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g thin green chilies or long green peppers, stems trimmed
steps: Lightly flatten each pepper with the flat of a knife.
Dry-roast the peppers in a hot wok over medium heat, pressing them with a spatula, for 5 to 6 minutes until blistered with black "tiger stripes" on both sides.
Push the peppers aside, add the oil and garlic and fry 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add soy, vinegar, sugar and salt and toss until the sauce reduces and coats the peppers; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 kg pork shoulder (about 70 percent lean, 30 percent fat), cut into small cubes
steps: Mix the pork with salt, sugar, wine, chili flakes, Sichuan pepper, five-spice and soy, and leave in the fridge 2 hours.
Stuff the mixture into the casings, tie into 15 cm links and prick all over with a needle.
Hang in a cold (below 10 C), dry, airy place for 7 to 10 days until firm, or traditionally smoke lightly over cypress branches first.
To eat, steam the sausages over high heat for 30 minutes until cooked through, cool slightly and slice thinly.
Serve as a cold platter or stir-fry the slices with garlic sprouts; keep remaining sausages refrigerated.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 kg skin-on pork belly, cut into long strips 5 cm wide
1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and crushed
steps: Rub the pork with wine, then with the mixed salt, peppercorns, five-spice and sugar, and pack into a covered container in the fridge for 5 to 7 days, turning daily.
Thread string through one end of each strip and hang in a cold, dry, airy place for 10 to 14 days until firm, or smoke over cypress or tea for flavour.
To cook, scrub the skin, soak in warm water 1 hour, then simmer for 30 to 40 minutes until cooked through.
Cool, slice thinly and serve with rice, or stir-fry with garlic sprouts or leeks.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Fuqi Feipian (Husband and Wife Lung Slices)

ingredients: 500 g beef shank and 300 g honeycomb beef tripe
4 slices ginger, 2 spring onions, 2 star anise, 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, 2 tbsp Shaoxing wine
5 tbsp Sichuan chili oil with sediment (hongyou)
small bunch coriander and 2 celery stalks, chopped
steps: Blanch the beef and tripe for 5 minutes, rinse, then simmer with ginger, spring onions, spices and wine in fresh water for 1.5 to 2 hours until tender.
Cool the meats in the stock, then slice thinly.
Mix chili oil, soy, sugar, Sichuan pepper and braising stock into a dressing.
Toss the sliced meats with the dressing, celery and coriander and top with crushed peanuts; serve at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg chicken legs, bone-in and skin-on
4 tbsp Sichuan chili oil with sediment
2 garlic cloves, crushed to a paste
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds and 2 tbsp crushed peanuts
steps: Simmer the chicken legs with ginger and spring onions in water to cover for 15 minutes, then turn off the heat and leave covered 15 minutes until the juices run clear (75 C inside).
Plunge into iced water for 10 minutes to firm the skin, drain and chop into bite-size pieces.
Mix chili oil, soy, vinegar, sugar, Sichuan pepper, garlic and 2 tbsp of the poaching liquid into a sauce.
Arrange the chicken on a plate, pour the sauce over and sprinkle with sesame seeds, peanuts and spring onion.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp Chinese sesame paste (zhimajiang) or tahini
1 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp black vinegar
steps: Poach the chicken with ginger and spring onion in barely simmering water for 15 minutes, then cover off the heat 10 minutes until cooked through.
Cool, then beat the breasts with a rolling pin to loosen the fibres and tear into thin shreds.
Thin the sesame paste with 2 tbsp warm water, then stir in chili oil, soy, vinegar, sugar and Sichuan pepper.
Pile the cucumber on a plate, top with the chicken, pour the sauce over and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp green Sichuan peppercorns (tengjiao) or red Sichuan peppercorns
2 tbsp Sichuan pepper oil (tengjiao you) or rapeseed oil
steps: Poach the chicken with ginger and spring onions for 15 minutes, then rest covered off heat 15 minutes until fully cooked; chill in iced water.
Soak the peppercorns in warm water 10 minutes, then finely chop them with the spring onion greens into a fragrant green paste.
Mix the paste with stock, soy, salt, sugar and pepper oil.
Chop the chicken into pieces, arrange on a plate and spoon the numbing green sauce over; serve cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g skin-on pork belly or leg, one piece
6 garlic cloves, pounded to a paste with a pinch of salt
3 tbsp sweet aromatic soy sauce (fuzhi jiangyou) or light soy simmered with sugar and star anise
steps: Simmer the pork with ginger and spring onion for 30 to 35 minutes until a chopstick passes through, then cool in the liquid.
Slice the pork paper-thin across the grain into wide sheets.
Mix garlic paste, sweet soy, chili oil and sesame oil.
Roll the pork slices around cucumber strips or drape them over the cucumber, pour the garlic sauce over and serve cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and 1 tsp dark soy
1 tsp sugar and 2 garlic cloves, minced
200 g bok choy or pea shoots
steps: Stir-fry the pork in 1 tbsp oil over high heat until crisp and brown, add wine, dark soy and yacai and fry 1 minute more.
Divide chili oil, soy, sesame paste, Sichuan pepper, sugar and garlic among four bowls.
Boil the noodles until just tender (about 3 minutes), blanching the greens in the same pot for the last 30 seconds.
Add 2 tbsp noodle water to each bowl, add noodles and greens, top with the pork and tell diners to toss well before eating.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g plain flour and 200 ml water and 1/2 tsp salt (thick noodles)
4 tbsp sweet aromatic soy sauce (fuzhi jiangyou), or 3 tbsp soy simmered with 2 tbsp brown sugar, star anise and cinnamon
4 garlic cloves, pounded to a paste
steps: Knead the flour, water and salt into a firm dough, rest covered 30 minutes, then roll 8 mm thick and cut into thick square-section noodles.
Boil the noodles 6 to 8 minutes until cooked through but chewy, drain and toss with a little oil.
Mix the sweet soy, chili oil, sesame paste, garlic and Sichuan pepper.
Divide the noodles into bowls, spoon over the sauce, sprinkle with sesame seeds and toss to serve warm or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp black vinegar
3 garlic cloves, crushed with 2 tbsp water (garlic water)
steps: Boil the noodles until just tender, about 2 minutes, drain and spread on a tray.
Toss with the oil and fan them while cooling so they stay springy and separate.
Mix chili oil, soy, vinegar, sugar, garlic water and Sichuan pepper.
Put bean sprouts in bowls, top with cold noodles, pour on the sauce and garnish with spring onions.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 tbsp Yibin yacai (sweet preserved mustard greens)
4 tbsp crushed roasted peanuts and 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
steps: Stir-fry the pork in 1 tbsp oil until crisp, add the yacai and fry 1 minute; set aside.
Boil the noodles until just tender, drain very thoroughly and shake off all water (the noodles should be dry enough to "burn" if lit).
Toss the hot noodles with the remaining oil, chili oil, soy and Sichuan pepper.
Divide into bowls and top with pork, yacai, peanuts, sesame seeds and spring onions; mix before eating.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g pork large intestines, thoroughly cleaned
2 tbsp flour and 2 tbsp salt (for cleaning)
300 g dried sweet potato glass noodles, soaked 1 hour
4 slices ginger, 2 star anise, 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, 2 tbsp Shaoxing wine
2 tbsp light soy and 1 tbsp black vinegar
1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper and 4 tbsp roasted soybeans or peanuts
steps: Scrub the intestines with flour and salt, rinse well, then blanch 5 minutes and rinse again.
Simmer the intestines in the stock with ginger, star anise, peppercorns and wine for 1.5 to 2 hours until tender, then slice into rings.
Put chili oil, soy, vinegar and Sichuan pepper into four bowls.
Cook the soaked glass noodles in the hot stock for 2 to 3 minutes until translucent and chewy, then ladle noodles and stock into the bowls.
Top with intestines, soybeans, coriander and spring onion.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g silken tofu pudding (douhua) or very soft silken tofu
2 tbsp Sichuan yacai or chopped zhacai
4 tbsp crushed roasted peanuts or crispy fried soybeans
steps: Warm the tofu pudding gently in a steamer for 5 minutes.
Boil the noodles until just tender and divide among bowls.
Spoon warm tofu pudding over the noodles in large soft scoops.
Drizzle with chili oil and soy, then top with yacai, peanuts, Sichuan pepper and spring onions; stir before eating.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g sweet potato or mung bean glass noodles, soaked 30 minutes
2 garlic cloves and 10 g ginger, minced
1 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp dark soy
steps: Drain the noodles and cut into roughly 15 cm lengths.
Stir-fry the pork in the oil over high heat until browned and crumbly, then add doubanjiang, garlic and ginger and fry 1 minute until red.
Add the stock and soy sauces, bring to a boil, then add the noodles.
Simmer, tossing, for 3 to 4 minutes until the noodles absorb nearly all the liquid and the pork "ants" cling to them.
Stir in the spring onions and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp grated ginger soaked in 80 ml water (ginger water)
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp white pepper
4 tbsp sweet aromatic soy sauce (fuzhi jiangyou)
4 garlic cloves, pounded to a paste
steps: Beat the pork with salt, pepper and wine, adding the ginger water a little at a time and stirring in one direction until springy and sticky.
Put a teaspoon of filling on each wrapper, fold into a half-moon and press the edges firmly to seal.
Boil the dumplings in plenty of water, adding a splash of cold water each time it returns to the boil, three times, until they float and the filling is cooked through (about 6 to 7 minutes).
Mix sweet soy, chili oil and garlic, divide among bowls and top with drained dumplings.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp grated ginger, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp Shaoxing wine
2 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp sugar
2 garlic cloves, minced and 1/2 tsp ground Sichuan pepper
steps: Mix pork, egg white, ginger, salt, wine and 3 tbsp water, stirring in one direction until sticky.
Place a small spoonful on each wrapper, fold into a triangle, then bring the two corners together and pinch to form a "folded arms" shape.
Boil the wontons 4 to 5 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Mix chili oil, soy, sugar, vinegar, garlic and Sichuan pepper in bowls, add the drained wontons and scatter spring onions.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 egg white and 1 tsp grated ginger
1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp white pepper
1.2 litres clear chicken and pork bone stock
1 tsp sesame oil and salt to taste
2 spring onions, sliced and a small handful of pea shoots
steps: Beat the pork with egg white, ginger, salt, pepper and 3 tbsp water until smooth and springy.
Fill each wrapper with a small amount and pinch into a loose bundle, Chengdu style.
Bring the stock to a simmer, season with salt and keep hot.
Boil the wontons in a separate pot for 3 to 4 minutes until they float and are cooked through, blanching the pea shoots at the end.
Ladle the hot stock into bowls, add wontons and greens and finish with sesame oil and spring onions.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 g instant yeast and 280 ml warm water
300 g minced pork with some fat
1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper and 1 tsp salt
steps: Mix flour, yeast and water into a soft dough, knead 8 minutes and rest covered 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the pork with Sichuan pepper, salt, soy and spring onions.
Divide the dough into 6, roll each into a long strip, brush with lard, spread a thin layer of filling, roll up like a snail, then flatten into a 12 cm disc and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Pan-fry in lard over medium-low heat for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden, then bake at 200 C for 10 minutes until crisp and the filling is cooked through.
Serve hot; some stalls slit them open and stuff with spicy cold-dressed meats.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg mixed skewer items: sliced beef, chicken gizzards, luncheon meat, quail eggs, tofu skin, lotus root, potato, mushrooms, kelp
150 g beef tallow or vegetable oil
40 g dried chilies, soaked and blitzed
15 g Sichuan peppercorns, 2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick
2 litres stock and 1 tbsp rock sugar
dry dip: 3 tbsp chili flakes, 1 tbsp ground Sichuan pepper, 1 tbsp ground peanuts, 1 tsp salt
steps: Thread the ingredients onto skewers, a few pieces each.
Melt the tallow, fry the doubanjiang over low heat 8 minutes, add chilies and spices and fry 3 minutes more.
Add stock and rock sugar and simmer 20 minutes to make a fiery broth.
Set the pot on a tabletop burner; diners dunk skewers until meats are cooked through (beef 1 minute, gizzards 3 to 4 minutes) and vegetables tender.
Roll in the dry dip or a sesame-oil and garlic dip; skewers are counted at the end to tally the meal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 litres pork or beef bone stock
2 tbsp hot pot base or chili oil
600 g mixed items: sliced beef, fish balls, tofu puffs, enoki, napa cabbage, lotus root, potato slices, glass noodles
2 garlic cloves, minced and chopped coriander
1 tsp sugar and salt to taste
steps: Fry the doubanjiang and hot pot base in 2 tbsp oil for 2 minutes, add peppercorns, then pour in the stock and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the denser items (lotus root, potato, fish balls) and cook 4 minutes.
Add sliced beef, tofu puffs, cabbage, enoki and noodles and cook 2 to 3 minutes until the beef is cooked and noodles soft.
Season with sugar and salt, ladle into bowls, and top with sesame paste thinned with broth, garlic and coriander.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg chicken legs, plus cooked gizzards, beef tripe or lotus root as extras
300 ml Sichuan chili oil with sediment
3 tbsp light soy sauce and 2 tbsp sugar
bamboo skewers and blanched vegetables (lotus root, potato slices, kelp, lettuce stems)
steps: Poach the chicken with ginger and spring onions for 15 minutes, then rest covered off heat 15 minutes until cooked through; chill.
Slice the chicken, extras and blanched vegetables thinly and thread onto skewers.
Mix chili oil, cold stock, soy, sugar, Sichuan pepper and sesame seeds in a large clay pot (bobo).
Stand the skewers in the pot so they soak for at least 10 minutes and serve cold; diners take skewers and pay by the stick.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 rabbit (about 1.2 kg), chopped into 1.5 cm pieces
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 1 tsp salt, 10 g ginger sliced (marinade)
60 g dried chilies, cut into short sections
30 g ginger, sliced and 4 spring onions, cut into sections
2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds and 1 tsp sesame oil
steps: Marinate the rabbit with wine, salt and ginger for 20 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat the oil in a wok to medium-high and fry the rabbit for 10 to 12 minutes until the pieces are golden, dry and cooked through.
Lower the heat, add the ginger, spring onions, chilies and peppercorns and fry 5 minutes until the chilies are dark red and crisp, not black.
Stir in sugar, sesame seeds and sesame oil, then let cool completely so the flavours infuse; serve cold as a snack with beer.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 rabbit heads, cleaned and soaked in cold water 1 hour
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and 4 slices ginger
3 tbsp Pixian doubanjiang and 2 tbsp hot pot base
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 bay leaves, 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns
2 tbsp light soy and 1 tbsp rock sugar
3 tbsp Sichuan chili oil and 1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper (finish)
steps: Blanch the rabbit heads with wine and ginger for 5 minutes and rinse.
Fry the doubanjiang and hot pot base in the oil for 2 minutes, add the spices and chilies, then add water to cover the heads, soy and rock sugar.
Simmer the heads gently for 50 to 60 minutes until tender, then leave to soak in the liquid for 30 minutes.
Lift out, toss with chili oil and ground Sichuan pepper, and eat with gloves, prising the jaw open to reach the cheek meat and brain.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g lean beef topside, in one piece
1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground
steps: Freeze the beef 1 hour, then slice paper-thin along the grain into large translucent sheets.
Rub the slices with salt, sugar, half the Sichuan pepper and wine, spread on racks and dry in a cool airy place or in an oven at 60 C for 6 to 8 hours until leathery.
Steam the dried slices over high heat for 15 minutes, then cut into squares.
Heat the oil to 150 C and fry the beef in batches for 1 to 2 minutes until crisp and translucent like lantern paper.
Toss with chili flakes, remaining Sichuan pepper, five-spice and sesame oil; cool and store airtight.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg mixed vegetables: napa cabbage stems, radish, carrot, long beans, ginger, fresh red chilies
50 ml baijiu (optional) or a splash of old pickle brine to start
steps: Dissolve the salt and rock sugar in the cooled boiled water and pour into a clean glass jar or traditional water-seal paocai crock.
Wash the vegetables, dry them completely in the sun or air for a few hours, and cut into thick pieces.
Pack the vegetables into the brine with the peppercorns, star anise and baijiu, keeping them fully submerged; seal (topping up the water moat if using a crock).
Leave at cool room temperature for 2 to 5 days until pleasantly sour, using clean dry chopsticks to remove pieces.
Serve cold as a side or chop and stir-fry with meat; discard the brine if it smells off or grows fuzzy mould.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 80 g black sesame seeds, toasted and ground
50 g softened butter or lard-free vegetable shortening
dip: 3 tbsp Chinese sesame paste mixed with 2 tbsp sugar and 1 tbsp water
steps: Mix the ground sesame, sugar and butter into a paste and chill 20 minutes, then roll into 20 small balls.
Knead the rice flour with warm water into a smooth, soft dough.
Wrap each sesame ball in a walnut-size piece of dough and roll smooth.
Boil in plenty of water for 5 to 6 minutes until they float and puff, then simmer 1 minute more.
Serve the tangyuan in a little cooking water with a dish of sweet sesame dip on the side, as at the Lai stall.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: San Da Pao (Three Cannon Rice Balls)

ingredients: 100 g roasted soybean flour (kinako) or ground toasted soybeans
steps: Steam the soaked rice on a cloth over high heat for 30 minutes until tender, then pound in a bowl into a sticky mass.
Simmer brown sugar and water for 5 minutes into a syrup.
Spread the soybean flour on a tray, pull off small balls of rice and throw them so they bounce on a board (the "three cannons" thud) and land in the soybean flour, then roll to coat.
Serve on a plate drizzled with brown sugar syrup and scattered with sesame seeds.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 15 g bingfen powder (made from shoofly/nicandra seeds) or 10 g agar powder
2 g limewater powder (if using bingfen powder) or omit for agar
120 g brown sugar and 120 ml water (syrup)
2 tbsp hawthorn flakes, raisins and roasted peanuts
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds and a few slices of watermelon or rose petals
steps: Bring the water to a boil, whisk in the bingfen powder (and limewater) or agar and boil 2 minutes until fully dissolved.
Pour into a shallow dish, cool and refrigerate 2 hours until set into a clear, wobbly jelly.
Simmer brown sugar and water 5 minutes into a dark syrup and chill.
Cut or spoon the jelly into bowls, pour over the syrup and top with hawthorn, raisins, peanuts and sesame seeds; serve icy cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g beef tallow (niuyou), the essential Chongqing fat
80 g dried chilies (facing-heaven chilies), soaked and coarsely pounded
30 g fermented black beans, 30 g ginger, 1 head garlic
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 black cardamom, 3 bay leaves, 1 tsp fennel seeds
2 litres beef stock, 2 tbsp rock sugar and 50 ml Shaoxing wine
1.2 kg dippers: beef tripe (maodu), duck intestines, goose intestines, sliced beef, luncheon meat, potato, lotus root, kelp, tofu, greens
dip per person: 3 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp minced garlic, chopped coriander, pinch of MSG or salt
steps: Melt the beef tallow in a wok over low heat, add doubanjiang and fry 10 minutes until deep red.
Add pounded chilies, ginger, garlic, black beans and whole spices and fry 5 minutes until fragrant; add the peppercorns for the last minute.
Add wine, stock and rock sugar and simmer 20 minutes; the tallow will set in leftovers, the sign of real Chongqing base.
Transfer to a nine-grid or single pot on a tabletop burner and keep boiling vigorously.
Cook dippers at the table: "seven up, eight down" for tripe (about 15 seconds of dunking), sliced beef until no pink, intestines and meats until fully cooked, vegetables until tender.
Dip in the sesame-garlic oil, which also cools each bite.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g bone-in chicken thighs, chopped into 2 cm pieces
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 1 tbsp light soy, 1 tsp salt, 10 g ginger sliced (marinade)
100 g dried chilies, cut into 2 cm sections
4 garlic cloves and 20 g ginger, sliced
steps: Marinate the chicken 15 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat the oil to 180 C and deep-fry the chicken in batches for 6 to 8 minutes until deep golden, crisp and cooked through; remove and pour off all but 3 tbsp oil.
Fry the garlic, ginger and spring onions over medium heat 1 minute, then add the chilies and peppercorns and fry 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant and the chilies turn crimson.
Return the chicken, add sugar and toss 2 minutes so the chicken picks up the oil.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve; diners hunt for chicken pieces among the mound of chilies.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Fish with Pickled Mustard Greens (Suancai Yu)

ingredients: 1 whole grass carp or sea bass (about 1 kg), filleted; head and bones reserved
1 egg white, 1 tbsp cornstarch, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine (marinade)
250 g Sichuan pickled mustard greens (suancai), rinsed and sliced
4 garlic cloves and 15 g ginger, sliced
1.2 litres boiling water or fish stock
1 tsp white pepper and 1/2 tsp sugar
10 dried chilies and 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns
steps: Slice the fillets thinly at an angle and coat with egg white, cornstarch, salt and wine; chop the head and bones.
Fry the head and bones in 2 tbsp oil 2 minutes, add ginger, garlic, pickled chilies and suancai and stir-fry 3 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the boiling water and boil hard 8 minutes until the broth turns milky and sour; season with white pepper and sugar, then strain the solids into a big bowl.
Lower the heat to a gentle simmer, slide in the fish slices and poach 2 minutes until white and cooked through, then pour fish and soup into the bowl.
Heat the remaining oil with dried chilies and peppercorns until sizzling and pour over the top; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g cooked duck blood or pork blood curd, cubed
200 g beef tripe, sliced and blanched
100 g luncheon meat or spam, sliced
200 g bean sprouts and 100 g soybean sprouts
3 tbsp Pixian doubanjiang and 2 tbsp hot pot base
15 dried chilies, 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns, 4 garlic cloves minced
steps: Blanch the bean sprouts and place in a deep bowl.
Fry the doubanjiang and hot pot base in 3 tbsp oil for 2 minutes, add garlic, then pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Add duck blood and luncheon meat and simmer 4 minutes, then add tripe and eel and simmer 3 minutes until fully cooked.
Pour everything over the sprouts, scatter with dried chilies and peppercorns, and pour over smoking-hot oil; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g mixed ingredients: sliced beef, shrimp, chicken wings, lotus root, potato, broccoli, wood ear, tofu skin
3 tbsp hot pot base or 2 tbsp doubanjiang plus 1 tbsp chili oil
4 garlic cloves and 15 g ginger, sliced
1 tbsp light soy and 1 tsp sugar
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds and chopped coriander
steps: Blanch the vegetables separately until just tender and drain well; cook chicken wings in boiling water 10 minutes until cooked through and drain.
Heat the oil in a large wok, fry chilies and peppercorns 20 seconds, then add hot pot base, garlic, ginger, onion and celery and fry 2 minutes.
Add beef and shrimp and stir-fry over high heat 2 to 3 minutes until cooked.
Add the wings and vegetables, season with soy and sugar and toss 2 minutes until everything is coated and sizzling.
Finish with sesame seeds and coriander and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole fish (grass carp, catfish or sea bass, about 1.2 kg), butterflied through the back
1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 10 g ginger sliced (marinade)
2 tbsp vegetable oil and 1 tsp cumin powder
3 tbsp Pixian doubanjiang and 2 tbsp hot pot base
15 dried chilies and 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns
4 garlic cloves, 1 onion sliced, 2 celery stalks
300 g toppings: potato slices, lotus root, tofu skin, bean sprouts, wood ear
steps: Score the fish, rub with salt, wine and ginger and marinate 15 minutes.
Brush with oil, sprinkle cumin and grill over charcoal or under a hot grill for 15 to 20 minutes, turning once, until the skin is crisp and the flesh flakes at the bone.
Meanwhile fry doubanjiang, hot pot base, chilies, peppercorns, garlic and onion in 3 tbsp oil for 3 minutes, add stock and the toppings and simmer 6 minutes until tender.
Lay the fish in a metal tray over a burner, pour the spicy sauce and toppings over and simmer 3 minutes at the table; scatter coriander.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg free-range chicken, chopped into pieces
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and 1/2 tsp salt
10 dried chilies and 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns
20 g ginger and 4 garlic cloves, sliced
600 ml spring water or filtered water
1 tsp sugar and 1 tbsp light soy
4 tbsp vegetable oil and chopped spring onions
steps: Marinate the chicken with wine and salt for 10 minutes.
Fry ginger, garlic, chilies and peppercorns in the oil 1 minute, add pickled chili paste and doubanjiang and fry until red.
Add the chicken and stir-fry over high heat 5 minutes until the skin is lightly golden.
Pour in the spring water, add soy and sugar and simmer covered 25 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Garnish with spring onions and serve with rice and clear vegetable soup, as at the Nanshan spring-side restaurants.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and 1/2 tsp salt
15 dried chilies and 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns
2 tbsp light soy and 1 tsp sugar
500 ml water and 1 bunch fresh mint or celery leaves
300 g fresh wheat noodles (to add at the end)
steps: Marinate the chicken with wine and salt for 10 minutes.
Fry the doubanjiang in the oil 1 minute until red, add pickled chilies, dried chilies, peppercorns, ginger and garlic and fry 1 minute.
Add chicken and stir-fry over high heat 5 minutes, then add soy, sugar and water and simmer covered 20 minutes until tender and cooked through.
Transfer to a large pot on a tabletop burner and serve, adding the noodles to the remaining sauce once the chicken is eaten, with mint leaves stirred in to finish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g white fish fillets, thinly sliced
1 egg white, 1 tbsp cornstarch, 1/2 tsp salt (marinade)
400 g tofu pudding (douhua) or silken tofu
10 dried chilies and 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns
6 tbsp vegetable oil and chopped coriander
steps: Coat the fish slices with egg white, cornstarch and salt.
Fry doubanjiang and pickled chilies in 3 tbsp oil 1 minute, add garlic and ginger, then pour in the stock and simmer 5 minutes.
Spoon in large scoops of tofu pudding and simmer gently 3 minutes, then slide in the fish and poach 2 minutes until opaque and cooked through.
Pour into a bowl, top with dried chilies and peppercorns, pour over smoking-hot oil and scatter coriander.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp Sichuan yacai or chopped zhacai
3 garlic cloves crushed with 2 tbsp water and 1 tsp grated ginger in 2 tbsp water
2 tbsp lard or vegetable oil and 1 tbsp sesame paste
200 g water spinach or bok choy and 2 spring onions, sliced
steps: In each bowl combine chili oil, soy, Sichuan pepper, lard, sesame paste, garlic water and ginger water.
Add 120 ml hot bone stock to each bowl.
Boil the noodles 2 to 3 minutes until springy, blanching the greens alongside for 30 seconds.
Add noodles and greens to the bowls and top with peanuts, yacai and spring onions; stir well before eating, as at a Chongqing breakfast stall.

dishes.name: Pea and Minced Pork Noodles (Wanza Mian)

ingredients: 200 g dried yellow peas (wandou), soaked overnight, or 400 g canned
1 tbsp Pixian doubanjiang and 1 tbsp sweet bean sauce
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and 1 tbsp light soy
1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper and 2 garlic cloves, crushed
200 g greens and 2 spring onions, sliced
steps: Simmer the soaked peas in water 45 to 60 minutes until soft and creamy, then salt lightly.
Stir-fry the pork in 1 tbsp oil until browned, add doubanjiang, sweet bean sauce, wine and soy and fry 5 minutes into a rich za jiang topping.
Put chili oil, Sichuan pepper, garlic and a little soy in each bowl.
Boil the noodles and greens, divide into bowls, top with a ladle of soft peas and the pork, and sprinkle with spring onions.

dishes.name: Hot and Sour Glass Noodles (Suanla Fen)

ingredients: 300 g sweet potato glass noodles, soaked 1 hour
4 tbsp Zhenjiang or Baoning black vinegar
1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper and 1/2 tsp sugar
4 tbsp crispy fried soybeans or peanuts and 2 tbsp Sichuan yacai
steps: Combine chili oil, vinegar, soy, Sichuan pepper, sugar and garlic water in four bowls.
Bring the stock to a boil and cook the soaked noodles 2 to 3 minutes until translucent and chewy.
Ladle noodles and hot stock into the bowls.
Top with crispy soybeans, yacai, coriander and spring onion and serve hot.

ingredients: 600 g fresh tofu pudding (douhua) or silken tofu
2 tbsp Pixian doubanjiang, fried in 1 tbsp oil until red
2 tbsp chopped coriander and 2 spring onions, sliced
steps: Warm the tofu pudding gently in its whey or a steamer for 5 minutes.
Mix chili oil, soy, fried doubanjiang, Sichuan pepper, coriander, spring onion and sesame into a dipping sauce, one small dish per person.
Scoop the tofu pudding into bowls with a little of its whey.
Serve with bowls of rice; diners dip pieces of tofu into the sauce and eat it with rice, a classic cheap Chongqing worker's meal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g lean pork leg, in one piece
1 tbsp honey and 1 tbsp sesame seeds
steps: Freeze the pork 1 hour, then slice paper-thin into large sheets.
Marinate the slices with salt, sugar, wine, five-spice, Sichuan pepper and soy, covered in the fridge for 4 hours.
Lay the slices flat on oiled racks and dry in a 70 C oven for 4 to 5 hours until leathery.
Brush with honey, sprinkle sesame seeds and roast at 200 C for 5 to 8 minutes until glossy, slightly charred at the edges and cooked through.
Cool, cut into squares and store airtight as a chewy snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 ml vegetable oil plus about 1 litre for deep-frying
optional flavourings: 1 tsp chili flakes and 1/2 tsp ground Sichuan pepper (spicy version)
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, 60 ml oil, baking soda and sesame seeds, then add warm water and knead into a firm, smooth dough; rest covered 30 minutes.
Divide into 30 g pieces and roll each into a 40 cm rope.
Twist each rope tightly, fold in half so it twists on itself, then fold and twist again into a short braided stick, tucking the ends.
Heat oil to 160 C and fry the twists 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until deep golden and very crisp right through.
Drain, toss spicy ones with chili and Sichuan pepper while warm, and cool completely before storing airtight.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg fresh stem mustard tubers (zhacai), or kohlrabi as a substitute
steps: Cut the tubers into quarters and air-dry on racks for 2 to 3 days until they lose about half their weight and feel pliable.
Rub with half the salt, pack into a bowl, press with a weight for 2 days, then squeeze out the brine.
Rub with the remaining salt, chili flakes, Sichuan pepper, five-spice, sugar and wine.
Pack tightly into a clean jar, seal and keep in a cool place for 2 to 4 weeks until savoury and crunchy (or buy Fuling zhacai in packets from Chinese grocers).
To serve, rinse, slice thinly, and dress with chili oil and sugar, or use in soups and noodles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g boneless pork shoulder (pork collar, "mui tau"), cut into 5 cm wide strips
1 tbsp red fermented bean curd (nam yu), mashed
steps: Mix hoisin, both soy sauces, Shaoxing wine, nam yu, five-spice and garlic; coat the pork strips and marinate covered in the fridge overnight (at least 8 hours).
Heat the oven to 200 C and set the pork on a rack over a foil-lined tray filled with 1 cm of water so the drips do not burn.
Roast 20 minutes, flip, baste with marinade and roast another 15 minutes.
Loosen the maltose with the hot water, brush it thickly over the pork and roast at 230 C for 5-8 minutes until glossy and charred at the edges and the centre reads 68 C.
Rest 10 minutes, slice across the grain and serve with steamed rice and blanched choy sum.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole goose, about 3.5 kg, cleaned (substitute a large duck)
2 tbsp chu hou sauce (or hoisin), mixed with 1 tbsp sesame paste
3 star anise and 2 slices ginger, for the cavity
steps: Rub the cavity with salt, sugar, five-spice and the chu hou paste, add star anise and ginger, and close the opening tightly with a skewer.
Pour boiling water over the skin until it tightens, then brush with maltose dissolved in vinegar and a splash of hot water.
Hang or set the goose on a rack in the fridge, uncovered, overnight so the skin dries completely.
Roast at 180 C for 60 minutes, then raise to 220 C for 20-30 minutes until the skin is deep mahogany and crisp and the thigh juices run clear (75 C).
