Rest 15 minutes, chop through the bone into pieces and serve with plum sauce and rice or rice noodles in broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg skin-on pork belly, one even slab
2 tsp salt, plus 1 tsp for the skin
300 g coarse salt, for the crust
English mustard and white sugar, to serve
steps: Blanch the belly skin-side down in boiling water 3 minutes, then dry and prick the skin all over with a sharp skewer.
Rub the meat side (not the skin) with five-spice, sugar, 2 tsp salt and Shaoxing wine; wipe the skin with vinegar and 1 tsp salt and refrigerate uncovered overnight.
Wrap foil around the sides like a box, pack coarse salt over the skin and roast at 180 C for 60 minutes.
Remove the salt crust, raise the oven to 230 C and roast 20-30 minutes until the skin blisters into crackling and the meat reaches 71 C.
Rest 15 minutes, chop into bars with a cleaver and serve with mustard and a dish of sugar for dipping.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 suckling pig, 5-6 kg, butterflied by the butcher
2 tbsp red fermented bean curd (nam yu)
3 tbsp Mei Kuei Lu Chiew rose wine (or Shaoxing wine)
4 tbsp maltose dissolved in 4 tbsp white vinegar
steamed lotus-leaf buns and hoisin, to serve
steps: Rub the cavity side with salt, sugar, five-spice, hoisin, nam yu and rose wine and marinate 2 hours.
Pour boiling water over the skin, brush with the maltose-vinegar mixture and dry in a cool, airy place or uncovered fridge overnight.
Stretch the pig flat on a rack or spit and roast at 180 C for about 2 hours, pricking any blisters, until the internal temperature at the shoulder reaches 71 C.
Raise to 230 C for the last 20-30 minutes until the skin is crisp and amber like glass.
Carve the skin into squares first, then the meat, and serve with buns, hoisin and sliced scallions.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 ml Shaoxing rice wine or Mei Kuei Lu Chiew
3 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 pieces dried tangerine peel (chenpi)
steps: Bring the soy sauces, rock sugar, wine, water, spices, ginger and scallions to a simmer in a deep pot just large enough for the chicken.
Lower the chicken in breast-side down, dip it in and out twice to fill the cavity, then simmer gently 15 minutes and turn it over.
Cover, turn off the heat and steep 30 minutes, until the thigh juices run clear (75 C at the thigh).
Lift out, brush with sesame oil for shine, rest 10 minutes and chop into pieces.
Serve with a ladle of the master sauce over rice; strain and freeze the sauce to reuse.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Bring the water, sliced ginger, scallions and salt to a boil, dip the chicken in and out three times, then submerge it.
Simmer at the barest bubble 15 minutes, cover, turn off the heat and steep 25-30 minutes until the thigh reaches 75 C.
Plunge into ice water for 10 minutes to tighten the skin into a smooth, jelly-like layer.
Mix minced ginger, scallions and salt in a heatproof bowl and pour the smoking oil over to make the ginger-scallion dip.
Chop the chicken into pieces and serve at room temperature with the dip and rice cooked in a little of the poaching stock.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 litres soy master stock (from Soy Sauce Chicken) or 500 ml light soy, 1 litre water, 2 star anise, chenpi
1 tsp salt mixed with 1/2 tsp five-spice, and lemon wedges, to serve
steps: Simmer the squab in the master stock 8 minutes, cover and steep off the heat 10 minutes.
Lift out, brush with maltose, vinegar and wine mixed together and hang or set on a rack in front of a fan for 3-4 hours until the skin is dry.
Heat oil to 170 C and ladle it repeatedly over the birds (or deep-fry) for 6-8 minutes until the skin is crisp and dark red and the meat is cooked through.
Chop each squab into quarters and serve with five-spice salt and lemon wedges, as in Shiqi, Zhongshan.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Steamed Whole Fish with Ginger and Scallion

ingredients: 1 whole sea bass or grouper, about 700 g, scaled and gutted
5 cm ginger, half sliced, half cut into fine shreds
steps: Score the fish twice on each side, lay it on ginger slices on a heatproof plate.
Steam over rapidly boiling water 8-10 minutes until the flesh by the bone flakes and the eye turns white; pour off the cloudy steaming liquid.
Warm soy, sugar and water until the sugar dissolves.
Pile shredded ginger and scallions on the fish, pour over smoking-hot peanut oil so it sizzles, then spoon the sweet soy around the fish.
Garnish with coriander and serve immediately with steamed rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Sweet and Sour Pork (Gu Lou Yuk)

ingredients: 500 g pork shoulder, cut into 3 cm chunks
1 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
1 green pepper and 1 red pepper, cut into chunks
4 tbsp ketchup, 3 tbsp white rice vinegar, 3 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp plum sauce
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
steps: Marinate the pork with soy, wine and egg yolk 20 minutes, then toss in potato starch, pressing it on until dry and shaggy.
Deep-fry at 170 C for 4 minutes until cooked through, rest 2 minutes, then refry at 190 C for 1 minute until very crisp.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp oil and stir-fry the peppers and pineapple 1 minute on high heat.
Add ketchup, vinegar, sugar and plum sauce, bring to a boil and thicken with the cornstarch slurry until glossy.
Toss the pork through the sauce for 15 seconds and serve at once with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g large shell-on shrimp, legs trimmed, deveined through the shell
1 red chilli and 1 green chilli, finely chopped
1/2 tsp ground white pepper and 1/4 tsp five-spice powder
steps: Dry-toast the salt in a wok until faintly grey, then mix with white pepper and five-spice to make jiaoyan.
Pat the shrimp very dry, dust in cornstarch and deep-fry at 190 C for 1-2 minutes until the shells are crisp and the flesh is opaque.
Pour out all but 1 tbsp oil and fry garlic, chillies and scallions 30 seconds until fragrant but not brown.
Return the shrimp, sprinkle with the spiced salt and toss on high heat 30 seconds; serve hot, shells and all.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ginger and Scallion Crab (Geung Chung Haai)

ingredients: 2 live mud crabs or Dungeness crabs, about 1.5 kg total
steps: Chill the crabs in the freezer 20 minutes to dull them, then clean, quarter and crack the claws.
Dust the cut sides with cornstarch and shallow-fry in hot oil 3-4 minutes until the shells turn red; set aside.
Fry the ginger until golden at the edges, add scallion whites and the crab, splash Shaoxing wine around the wok.
Add oyster sauce, soy, sugar and stock, cover and cook 5 minutes until the crab meat is opaque throughout.
Toss in the scallion greens, reduce the sauce to a glaze and serve with rice or e-fu noodles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Steamed Scallops with Garlic and Vermicelli

ingredients: 50 g mung bean vermicelli, soaked 15 minutes and cut short
steps: Fry half the garlic in 2 tbsp oil over low heat until golden, then stir in the raw garlic off the heat (the "golden and silver garlic").
Put a nest of vermicelli on each shell, top with a scallop and a spoon of the garlic.
Steam over high heat 5-6 minutes until the scallops are just opaque.
Warm soy, sugar and water, spoon over, scatter scallions and pour over the remaining smoking oil; serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Steamed Pork Patty with Salted Fish (Haam Yu Jing Yuk Beng)

ingredients: 30 g Cantonese salted fish (mui heung haam yu), skin removed (substitute salted anchovy fillets)
steps: Pan-fry the salted fish in a little oil 1 minute per side until fragrant, then slice thinly.
Mix the pork, water chestnuts, soy, cornstarch, sugar and water, stirring in one direction until sticky.
Spread the pork into a flat patty 2 cm thick on a shallow heatproof plate and lay the fish and ginger on top.
Steam over high heat 12-15 minutes until the juices run clear and the centre reaches 71 C; serve with plain rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg beef brisket or flank, cut into 4 cm chunks
400 g daikon radish, cut into chunks
1 tbsp red fermented bean curd (nam yu)
3 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 piece chenpi, 2 bay leaves
steps: Blanch the beef in boiling water 5 minutes, then rinse off the scum.
Fry the ginger, garlic, chu hou paste and nam yu in a little oil 1 minute until fragrant, add the beef and Shaoxing wine.
Add oyster sauce, dark soy, rock sugar, spices and water to just cover, then simmer covered on low 2 hours until tender.
Add the daikon and simmer 30 minutes more until translucent and the sauce is reduced.
Serve over rice or with rice noodles in clear beef broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml full-fat milk (Shunde uses buffalo milk)
1 tbsp finely chopped scallion, for colour
steps: Whisk the milk, egg whites, cornstarch, sugar and salt until smooth with no lumps.
Heat the oil in a wok over low-medium heat and pour in the milk mixture.
Fold gently with a spatula, scraping from the bottom, so it sets in soft white curds without browning, about 5 minutes.
Pile onto a plate, scatter toasted pine nuts and scallion, and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g sashimi-grade fish fillet (traditionally freshwater fish; use sushi-grade sea bream or yellowtail from a trusted supplier)
1 lemon leaf (or kaffir lime leaf), very finely shredded
2 tbsp toasted crushed peanuts and 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
50 g crispy fried taro or rice crackers
2 tbsp peanut oil, 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, pinch of salt
steps: Use only sashimi-grade fish kept below 4 C; pat dry and slice paper-thin against the grain.
Fan the slices over a chilled plate, and arrange the shredded onion, ginger, scallions and lemon leaf in small piles around it.
Scatter peanuts, sesame and crispy taro at the table.
Mix soy, sugar, salt and peanut oil, pour over and toss everything together just before eating.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g raw shrimp, peeled and cut into chunks
1 tsp each salt, sugar and sesame oil, plus 1/2 tsp white pepper
4 portions thin alkaline egg noodles (jook-sing style)
1.5 litres chicken and pork stock, simmered with 20 g dried flounder (daimyo fish) or 2 tbsp dried shrimp
4 stalks choy sum and garlic chives, chopped
steps: Mix shrimp, pork, salt, sugar, sesame oil and pepper until sticky; place a teaspoon on each wrapper and pinch into a tail-like wonton.
Season the hot stock with fish sauce and keep at a simmer.
Boil the wontons 3-4 minutes until they float and the shrimp is pink.
Blanch the noodles 20 seconds, rinse briefly in cold water, and blanch again 10 seconds so they stay springy.
Put a spoon of the soup in each bowl, then wontons at the bottom, noodles on top, choy sum and chives, and ladle over more broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Beef Chow Fun (Gon Chow Ngau Ho)

ingredients: 450 g fresh flat rice noodles (ho fun), separated
200 g beef flank, thinly sliced across the grain
1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp cornstarch, 1/4 tsp baking soda (for marinade)
1 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp sugar
steps: Marinate the beef with soy, cornstarch and baking soda 15 minutes.
Sear the beef in 1 tbsp very hot oil 30 seconds per side until browned, and remove.
Add the remaining oil, onion and noodles, spread them out and leave 30 seconds to char before tossing with a lifting motion to avoid breaking.
Add dark soy, light soy and sugar, then bean sprouts, scallions and beef, and toss on maximum heat 1 minute until the noodles are evenly coloured and smoky ("wok hei"). Serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Soy Sauce Pan-fried Noodles (Si Yau Wong Chow Min)

ingredients: 300 g thin fresh egg noodles (Hong Kong style pan-fried noodles)
steps: Blanch the noodles 30 seconds, drain and toss with sesame oil; let them dry 5 minutes.
Mix dark soy, light soy and sugar.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok on high, fry the noodles spread out 2 minutes until golden in patches, then toss.
Push aside, fry onion in the remaining oil 1 minute, add bean sprouts and scallion whites, then the noodles and sauce.
Toss with chopsticks 1-2 minutes until evenly brown and dry, add the scallion greens and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 Chinese liver sausage (yun cheong) or 100 g chicken thigh, sliced
2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tbsp dark soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil, 2 tbsp hot water
steps: Oil the clay pot (or a heavy cast-iron pot), add drained rice and water, bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
When the water is almost absorbed (about 8 minutes), lay the sausages and chicken on top, cover and cook on low 12-15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Drizzle 1 tbsp oil around the rim and tilt the pot over the flame for 4-5 minutes, rotating, until you hear crackling and a crust (faan jiu) forms.
Mix the soy sauces, sugar, sesame oil and hot water, pour over at the table with the choy sum and scallion, and mix well, scraping up the crust.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Salted Fish and Chicken Fried Rice (Haam Yu Gai Lap Chaau Faan)

ingredients: 600 g cold cooked jasmine rice, grains separated
30 g Cantonese salted fish, finely diced (substitute salted anchovies)
200 g chicken thigh, diced, with 1 tsp soy and 1/2 tsp cornstarch
steps: Fry the salted fish in 1 tbsp oil on medium heat 1-2 minutes until crisp and fragrant; set aside.
Stir-fry the chicken on high heat 3-4 minutes until cooked through; set aside.
Scramble the eggs in the remaining oil until half set, add rice and toss on high heat 3 minutes until hot and grains jump.
Return fish and chicken, season with soy and pepper, then add lettuce and scallions and toss 30 seconds until just wilted. Serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Lo Mai Gai (Lotus Leaf Sticky Rice)

ingredients: 2 dried lotus leaves, soaked and halved
6 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp light soy, 1 tbsp dark soy, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil
steps: Steam the drained rice on a cloth 25 minutes, then mix with 1 tbsp soy, dark soy and peanut oil.
Stir-fry chicken, sausage, mushrooms and dried shrimp with oyster sauce, sugar and sesame oil 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked; add a splash of water to make a little gravy.
On each lotus leaf, spread a layer of rice, add filling and a piece of egg yolk, cover with more rice and fold into a tight parcel.
Steam the parcels 45-60 minutes over high heat until the rice is soft and fragrant; open at the table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Century Egg and Pork Congee (Pei Daan Sau Yuk Zuk)

ingredients: 150 g jasmine rice, rinsed and mixed with 1 tsp oil and 1/2 tsp salt
2.5 litres water or light chicken stock
250 g lean pork, salted overnight with 1 tsp salt (sau yuk)
2 century eggs (pei daan), peeled and diced
1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp white pepper
steps: Bring the water to a rolling boil, add the oiled rice and ginger, and simmer, stirring now and then, 60 minutes until the grains break into a silky porridge.
Rinse the salted pork, add it whole with half the century egg and simmer 20 minutes until cooked through; lift out and shred.
Return the pork with the rest of the egg, season with salt and pepper, and simmer 5 minutes.
Serve topped with scallions and white pepper, with sliced youtiao on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g white fish fillet, thinly sliced
100 g pork skin or lean pork, thinly sliced
2 tbsp roasted peanuts and 1 handful fried rice crackers or youtiao
1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp white pepper
1 egg-net omelette strip (optional), scallions and coriander
steps: Simmer the rice in the stock 60-75 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and smooth.
Season with salt and pepper and bring back to a rolling boil.
Add pork and squid, cook 2 minutes, then add fish and ginger and cook 1 minute until opaque.
Ladle into bowls and pile on peanuts, crispy crackers, scallions and coriander, as sold from boats in Guangzhou's harbours.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g grass carp, snakehead or tilapia fillet, thinly sliced
1 tsp each light soy, cornstarch and oil for the fish
1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp white pepper
steps: Simmer the rice with chenpi in the water 60 minutes until smooth and creamy; season with salt.
Toss the fish with soy, cornstarch and oil.
Put fish slices and ginger in each bowl and ladle the boiling congee over; stir and leave 1 minute, or simmer 1 minute in the pot, until the fish is opaque.
Finish with white pepper, scallions and coriander.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 180 ml boiling water and 1 tsp lard or oil
300 g raw shrimp, peeled, half chopped and half left in chunks
1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper
1 tsp sesame oil and 1 tsp lard
steps: Mix the shrimp, bamboo, sugar, salt, pepper, cornstarch, sesame oil and lard; chill 20 minutes.
Pour boiling water over wheat and tapioca starch, stir, add lard and knead to a smooth, translucent dough; keep covered.
Roll small 10 g balls and press thin 7 cm rounds with an oiled cleaver blade.
Fill with a heaped teaspoon and pleat one side 8-10 times into a crescent.
Steam on parchment over high heat 6-7 minutes until the skins turn translucent and the shrimp is pink. Serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp light soy, 1 tsp sugar
1 tbsp cornstarch and 1 tsp sesame oil
flying fish roe or finely diced carrot, to garnish
steps: Mix the pork, shrimp, mushrooms, seasonings and cornstarch, stirring hard in one direction until springy.
Hold a wrapper in a ring of thumb and finger, add a spoon of filling and squeeze into an open-topped cylinder, flattening the top.
Dot with roe or carrot and steam over high heat 8-10 minutes until the filling is cooked through (71 C).
Serve hot with chilli oil and tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g raw shrimp, peeled, with pinch of salt and 1/2 tsp cornstarch
2 tbsp light soy, 1 tbsp dark soy, 1 tbsp sugar, 4 tbsp water (sweet soy)
steps: Whisk the flours, water and oil to a thin batter and rest 15 minutes.
Oil a shallow tray, pour in a thin layer of batter, scatter a few shrimp and scallions and steam covered over high heat 2-3 minutes until the sheet turns opaque and bubbles.
Scrape the sheet into a loose roll with a spatula and transfer to a plate; repeat with the remaining batter, stirring it each time.
Simmer the sweet soy ingredients 1 minute and pour over the rolls; serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Zha Leung (Fried Dough in Rice Roll)

ingredients: 2 fried dough sticks (youtiao), bought, each cut in half
2 tbsp light soy, 1 tbsp dark soy, 1 tbsp sugar, 4 tbsp water (sweet soy)
2 tbsp sesame paste or hoisin, loosened with water
steps: Crisp the youtiao in a 180 C oven for 5 minutes.
Whisk the flours, water and oil into a thin batter and steam thin sheets on an oiled tray 2-3 minutes until set and translucent.
Roll each hot sheet around a piece of youtiao, then cut into 3 cm pieces.
Drizzle with sweet soy and sesame paste, scatter sesame seeds and serve immediately while the youtiao is still crunchy.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g low-protein flour (bao flour or cake flour)
1 tsp instant yeast, 2 tsp baking powder
1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp hoisin, 1 tsp dark soy, 1 tbsp sugar
1 tbsp shallot oil or peanut oil
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, water and lard into a smooth soft dough and leave covered 1-1.5 hours until doubled.
Heat the shallot oil, add sauces, sugar and cornstarch water and stir until thick, then fold in the char siu and cool.
Knead the baking powder into the dough and divide into 12 pieces; roll each into a round thicker in the middle.
Fill with a spoon of filling, pleat closed and set on squares of paper.
Steam over high, rapidly boiling water 12-15 minutes until the tops burst open like smiles; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 sheets all-butter puff pastry (or Chinese flaky lard pastry)
steps: Simmer oyster sauce, hoisin, sugar and the cornstarch water until thick, stir in the char siu and chill.
Cut the pastry into 8 cm squares, place a spoon of filling on each and fold into rectangles, sealing the edges.
Brush with egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake at 200 C for 20-25 minutes until puffed, flaky and golden; serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp maltose or honey in 1 litre water
2 tbsp fermented black beans (dau si), rinsed and mashed
2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp light soy, 1 tbsp dark soy, 1 tbsp sugar
steps: Blanch the feet 5 minutes, dry well and soak in the maltose water, then dry again.
Deep-fry at 180 C, covered with a splatter guard, 8-10 minutes until golden and blistered.
Plunge into cold water and soak 1-2 hours until the skin puffs and wrinkles.
Simmer in water with star anise, ginger and half the sauces 45 minutes until tender, then drain.
Toss with black beans, garlic, remaining sauces, cornstarch and chilli and steam 15 minutes until glossy; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Steamed Spare Ribs with Black Bean (Si Zap Paai Gwat)

ingredients: 500 g pork spare ribs, chopped into 2-3 cm pieces
2 tbsp fermented black beans (dau si), rinsed and lightly crushed
steps: Soak the ribs in cold water 20 minutes to draw out blood, then pat dry.
Mix with black beans, garlic, soy, sugar, wine and cornstarch, finish with oil, and marinate 20 minutes.
Spread in a single layer on a shallow plate and steam over high heat 15-20 minutes until the meat is cooked through and no longer pink at the bone.
Garnish with chilli and scallion and serve in the steaming dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
3 tbsp dried shrimp, soaked and chopped
1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar, 1/4 tsp white pepper
2 tbsp peanut oil, plus more for frying
steps: Fry the sausage, mushrooms and dried shrimp in oil 3 minutes until fragrant.
Simmer the radish with 200 ml water 10 minutes until soft, then stir in the fried mixture and seasonings.
Whisk the rice flour with 200 ml water, pour into the radish off the heat and stir to a thick paste.
Press into an oiled 20 cm tin, steam over high heat 50-60 minutes until a chopstick comes out clean, then cool completely and chill.
Slice 1 cm thick and pan-fry in a little oil 3 minutes per side until golden; serve with chilli sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g wheat starch with 100 ml boiling water
1 tsp each salt and sugar, 1/2 tsp five-spice powder
3 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
1 tbsp oyster sauce and 1 tsp cornstarch in 3 tbsp water
steps: Steam the taro 20 minutes until soft, mash smooth while hot, then knead in the scalded wheat starch, lard, salt, sugar and five-spice; chill 30 minutes.
Stir-fry pork, shrimp and mushrooms 4 minutes until cooked, add oyster sauce and the cornstarch slurry to bind, then cool.
Wrap a spoon of filling in a 30 g piece of taro dough and shape into ovals.
Deep-fry at 180 C for 3-4 minutes until the surface puffs into a lacy golden honeycomb; drain and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Bean Curd Skin Rolls (Fu Pei Gyun)

ingredients: 2 large sheets dried bean curd skin (fu pei), cut into 15 cm squares
3 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
1 tbsp light soy, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp cornstarch
2 tbsp oyster sauce in 150 ml stock, thickened with 1 tsp cornstarch
steps: Mix the pork, shrimp, mushrooms, carrot and seasonings until sticky.
Wipe the bean curd sheets with a damp cloth to soften, spread a line of filling and roll up tightly, sealing with a little cornstarch paste.
Pan-fry the rolls 2 minutes until lightly golden, then steam 12-15 minutes until the filling is cooked through.
Cut into pieces and pour over the hot oyster sauce gravy.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 links Cantonese lap cheong (bought cured pork sausage)
steps: Rinse the sausages and lay them whole on top of the rice and water in a rice cooker or pot.
Cook the rice as usual (about 18 minutes covered on low after boiling) so the sausage steams and its fat seasons the rice.
Slice the sausages diagonally and arrange over the rice.
Drizzle with soy sauce dissolved with sugar and scatter scallion; alternatively pan-fry slices 2 minutes as a side with gai lan.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Stir-fried Gai Lan with Oyster Sauce

ingredients: 500 g gai lan (Chinese broccoli), ends trimmed (substitute broccolini)
1 tbsp peanut oil, plus 1 tsp for blanching water
1 tsp salt and 1 tsp sugar for blanching water
steps: Blanch the gai lan in boiling water with salt, sugar and oil 1-2 minutes until bright green and the stems are just tender; drain and lay on a plate.
Fry the garlic in 1 tbsp oil 20 seconds over medium heat.
Add oyster sauce, soy, sugar and water and bubble 30 seconds until glossy.
Pour the sauce over the greens and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g pork bones or pork shank
300 g lean pork, in one piece
8 red dates (hong zao) and 1 tbsp goji berries
2 dried honey dates (mut zou) and 1 piece chenpi
steps: Blanch the bones and lean pork in boiling water 5 minutes and rinse.
Put everything except the goji berries and salt into a large pot with the water and bring to a boil.
Reduce to the lowest simmer, cover and cook 3 hours until the broth is sweet and amber.
Add the goji berries for the last 10 minutes, season with salt, and serve the broth first, with the soft meat dipped in soy on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 small winter melon (about 3 kg), top cut off and seeds scooped out
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp white pepper
steps: Blanch the chicken 1 minute and drain.
Stand the melon in a heatproof bowl inside a large steamer and fill with stock, ham, mushrooms and lotus seeds.
Cover with the melon lid and steam over simmering water 2.5-3 hours until the flesh inside is translucent and soft, topping up the steamer water.
Add the chicken and shrimp for the last 20 minutes until cooked through, season, and serve at the table, scraping melon flesh into each bowl.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g sugar dissolved in 200 ml hot water, cooled
steps: Rub butter into flour, add 1 egg and cold water and bring into a short, smooth dough; chill 30 minutes.
Roll out, cut rounds and press into 12 fluted tart tins, pushing the dough slightly above the rim.
Whisk the 3 eggs gently with the cooled syrup, evaporated milk and vanilla without making foam, and strain twice.
Fill the shells to 90% and bake at 200 C for 10 minutes, then 180 C for 8-10 minutes until the custard is just set and wobbles slightly.
Cool 10 minutes and serve warm, the Hong Kong cha chaan teng way.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 salted duck egg yolks, rinsed and baked 5 minutes
1 egg yolk with 1 tsp egg white, for wash
steps: Mix golden syrup, oil and lye water, stir in the flour into a soft dough, cover and rest 1 hour.
Wrap each salted yolk in 60 g lotus paste and roll into a ball.
Flatten 20 g dough thinly, wrap around the filling and press into a floured mooncake mould.
Bake at 200 C for 5 minutes, cool 10 minutes, brush thinly with egg wash and bake 15 minutes more until deep golden.
Cool and keep in an airtight tin 2-3 days so the crust softens and turns glossy before slicing in wedges with tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 salted duck egg yolks, steamed 10 minutes and mashed
30 g milk powder and 20 g custard powder
300 g bao flour, 1 tsp instant yeast, 40 g sugar, 160 ml milk
steps: Beat the mashed yolks, butter, sugar, milk powder, custard powder and coconut milk into a paste; freeze in 12 small balls.
Knead flour, yeast, sugar and milk into a smooth dough and leave 1 hour until doubled; knead in the baking powder.
Divide into 12, wrap each frozen filling ball tightly, and set seam-down on paper squares; rest 15 minutes.
Steam over high heat 10-12 minutes; rest 2 minutes before opening the lid so they don't wrinkle. Eat carefully as the molten yolk filling is very hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml full-fat milk (buffalo milk in Shunde)
red beans in syrup, to serve (optional)
steps: Heat the milk until steaming and pour into two bowls; leave 15 minutes until a skin forms on top.
Cut a small edge of the skin, pour the milk out into a jug, leaving the skin in the bowl.
Whisk the milk with egg whites and sugar, strain and pour back slowly down the side so the skin floats up.
Cover with film and steam on low heat 12-15 minutes until set with a second skin; serve warm or chilled with red beans.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Ginger Milk Curd (Geung Zap Zong Naai)

ingredients: 300 ml full-fat milk (buffalo milk is traditional; whole cow's milk works)
steps: Squeeze the grated ginger through cloth to get 2 tbsp juice, stir it, and divide between two bowls.
Heat the milk with sugar to 75-80 C (steaming, small bubbles at the edge, not boiling).
Pour the hot milk from a height into the ginger juice in one go and do not stir.
Leave untouched 5-10 minutes until set into a soft curd that holds a spoon; eat warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp baking soda
steps: Whisk the eggs and brown sugar 5 minutes until pale and thick.
Fold in milk, then the sifted flour, raising agents and custard powder, then the melted butter.
Rest the batter covered 1 hour.
Pour into a 20 cm lined bamboo steamer or cake tin and steam over high heat 30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool slightly and cut into wedges; serve warm with tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: White Sugar Sponge Cake (Bak Tong Gou)

steps: Simmer half the water with sugar until dissolved, then pour into the rice flour while stirring; add the rest of the water and cool to lukewarm.
Stir in the yeast, cover and leave to ferment at room temperature 12-24 hours until bubbly and slightly tangy.
Pour into an oiled 20 cm tin and steam over high heat 25-30 minutes until springy and translucent white with honeycomb holes.
Cool completely before cutting into wedges; it is chewy and lightly sweet-sour.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g water chestnut flour (ma tai fen)
200 g fresh water chestnuts, peeled and diced (or canned)
250 g rock sugar or light brown sugar
steps: Mix the water chestnut flour with 500 ml water to a smooth slurry.
Boil the sugar with 500 ml water until dissolved, add the diced chestnuts and boil 1 minute.
Pour a third of the slurry into the hot syrup while stirring until it becomes a thick translucent paste, then stir in the rest.
Pour into an oiled 20 cm tin and steam over high heat 30-35 minutes until fully translucent; cool and chill.
Slice and eat cold, or pan-fry slices in oil until golden.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g plain flour, 50 g lard and 60 ml water (water dough)
100 g low-protein flour and 50 g lard (oil dough)
100 g candied winter melon, finely chopped
80 g glutinous rice flour, cooked (koh fun)
2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds and 1 tbsp desiccated coconut
30 g lard or oil and 100 ml water (for filling)
steps: Mix the filling: candied winter melon, cooked glutinous flour, sugar, sesame, coconut, lard and water into a soft sticky paste; divide into 8 balls.
Make the water dough and oil dough separately, divide each into 8, wrap each oil dough inside a water dough, then roll out and fold up twice to make flaky layers.
Wrap each filling ball in pastry, flatten to a 1 cm disc and cut two slits on top.
Brush with egg and bake at 190 C for 20-25 minutes until golden and flaky.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Sweet Potato Ginger Soup (Fan Syu Tong Sui)

ingredients: 600 g yellow or orange sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
80 g Chinese slab sugar (pin tong) or brown sugar
steps: Bring the water and ginger to a boil and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the sweet potato and simmer 15-20 minutes until tender but still holding shape.
Stir in the slab sugar until dissolved and taste for sweetness and ginger heat.
Serve hot in bowls on a cold day.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 40 g glutinous rice flour (or 3 tbsp rice soaked 2 hours)
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan over low heat 5 minutes until fragrant and starting to pop.
Blend the sesame with 500 ml water until very smooth and strain.
Simmer with the remaining water and rock sugar until dissolved.
Whisk the glutinous rice flour with a little water, stir into the pot and simmer 3-5 minutes until creamy; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 20 g dried prunella spike (xia ku cao)
steps: Rinse all the herbs briefly in cold water.
Bring the water to a boil, add the herbs, and simmer covered on low 45-60 minutes until reduced to about 1.2 litres and dark amber.
Strain, stir in rock sugar until dissolved, and drink warm or cooled; Chinese herbal shops sell ready-mixed liang cha packs as a substitute.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 goose (about 3.5 kg), cleaned; substitute 2 large ducks
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, 1 tsp five-spice powder
6 cloves garlic, smashed, plus 2 tbsp minced garlic and 4 tbsp white rice vinegar for dip
1 block firm tofu and 6 hard-boiled eggs, peeled
steps: Rub the goose inside and out with the coarse salt, leave 20 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
In a large deep pot bring the water, both soy sauces, rock sugar, galangal, spices and smashed garlic to a boil to make the lou (master braise).

Lower in the goose, ladle the liquid over it, and simmer on low heat with a lid ajar for about 100 minutes, turning and basting every 15 minutes, until a skewer slides easily into the thigh and the juices run clear.
Add the tofu and eggs for the last 30 minutes so they take on a deep brown colour.
Rest the goose 15 minutes, chop into bite-size pieces on the bone, and spoon over some reduced braising liquid.
Serve with the tofu, eggs, and a dip of minced garlic in vinegar, alongside plain rice or Teochew porridge.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g very fresh beef, mixed cuts (shank, brisket edge, flank, tenderloin), thinly sliced against the grain
300 g Teochew beef balls (homemade or bought)
200 g daikon radish, sliced into rounds
2 ears sweet corn, cut into pieces
6 tbsp shacha sauce (sha cha jiang) for dipping
steps: Bring the broth to a boil in a tabletop pot, add the daikon and corn, and simmer 15 minutes until the daikon turns translucent.
Add the beef balls and cook 5 minutes until they float and are hot through.
Each diner dips the thin beef slices into the barely simmering broth for 8 to 15 seconds for tender cuts and up to 1 minute for tougher cuts, until no longer red.
Mix shacha sauce with a little soy sauce and celery in small bowls as the dip.
Finish by cooking the kway teow in the rich broth for 2 minutes and serving it as soup with fried shallots.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 live mud crabs or flower crabs (about 1.2 kg total), scrubbed
2 tbsp Chinese red vinegar (substitute black vinegar)
steps: Chill the crabs in the freezer for 20 minutes to sedate them, then scrub well.
Place the crabs belly up on a steaming plate with the ginger slices and steam over rolling boiling water for 18 to 20 minutes until the shells are fully bright orange and the meat is opaque.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 3 hours until well chilled so the roe sets firm and sweet.
Mix the vinegar, shredded ginger and sugar into a dip.
Crack and portion the crabs and serve cold with the ginger vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 silver pomfret (about 600 g), gutted and scaled
60 g salted mustard greens (kiam chye), soaked and sliced
3 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
30 g pork fat or fatty pork, thinly sliced
steps: Score the fish twice on each side and lay it on a heatproof plate over the spring onions.
Scatter the salted vegetable, tomato, mushroom, pork fat, mashed sour plum and ginger over and around the fish, then drizzle with the soy and wine.
Steam over high heat for 10 to 12 minutes until the flesh at the thickest part flakes from the bone.
Discard the spring onions underneath and serve immediately with the tangy juices and steamed rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole fish such as golden threadfin or mackerel (about 800 g), cleaned
2 tbsp puning yellow bean sauce (puning dou jiang); substitute yellow bean paste
steps: Rub the fish inside and out with the salt and leave 10 minutes.
Steam over high heat with the ginger for 12 to 15 minutes until the flesh is opaque and flakes at the bone.
Cool to room temperature then refrigerate at least 2 hours until cold and firm.
Mash the bean sauce with the sugar and sesame oil and serve as a dip with the cold fish, alongside porridge.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g lean beef (topside or round), sinew removed and chilled
steps: Pound the chilled beef with two heavy cleavers or a meat mallet for 10 minutes, or pulse in a food processor with crushed ice, until a smooth sticky paste forms.
Mix in the salt, sugar, fish sauce, pepper, baking soda and starch, then beat with your hand, slapping the paste into the bowl, for 5 minutes while adding ice water a little at a time until springy.
Squeeze balls through your fist and scoop them with a spoon into a pot of water held just below a simmer (about 80°C).
Cook 10 to 12 minutes until they float and the centres are no longer pink, then transfer to ice water to firm up.
Serve in clear broth with celery and fried garlic, or with shacha sauce as a snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g white fish fillet such as wolf herring or Spanish mackerel, skin and bones removed
steps: Scrape the flesh from the fillets with a spoon, discarding bloodline, then chop until fine.
Add the salt and beat the paste in a bowl, gradually adding ice water, sugar, pepper and starch, and throw it against the bowl for 10 minutes until glossy and bouncy.
Shape balls by squeezing through the thumb and forefinger, dropping them into a pot of cold water.
Heat slowly to just below a simmer and cook 6 to 8 minutes until the balls float and are white throughout.
Serve in clear broth or with kway teow soup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g small fresh oysters, shucked and rinsed
3 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
2 tbsp chili sauce mixed with 1 tsp lime juice
steps: Whisk the sweet potato starch with the water into a thin slurry.
Heat the lard in a flat wok over high heat until smoking, pour in the slurry, and fry 2 minutes until it turns translucent and crisp at the edges.
Pour the beaten eggs over, break it up with the spatula and let it crisp for 2 minutes.
Add the oysters and fish sauce and toss 1 to 2 minutes until the oysters plump and are cooked through.
Plate with spring onion and coriander and serve with the chili-lime dip.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g Teochew chai poh (preserved radish), rinsed and chopped
100 g salted mustard greens (kiam chye), sliced
4 salted duck eggs or plain boiled eggs (optional sides)
100 g olive vegetable (kana chye) or fermented bean curd
steps: Bring the water to a boil, add the rice, and cook uncovered on medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the grains are soft but still whole in plenty of thin liquid.
Meanwhile fry the chopped chai poh in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden.
Ladle the watery porridge into bowls.
Serve with small plates of fried chai poh, salted vegetables, olive vegetable and eggs to eat alongside.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g minced pork, seasoned with 1 tsp soy sauce
3 tbsp thick sweet soy sauce mixed with 1 tbsp peanut sauce
steps: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch and water into a thin batter and rest 10 minutes.
Oil a flat steaming tray, pour in a thin layer of batter, and scatter some pork, prawns, chai poh and a cracked egg over.
Steam over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until the sheet is translucent and the pork and prawns are fully cooked.
Add the bean sprouts and lettuce, then scrape the sheet into a loose roll with a pastry scraper.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve hot with the sweet soy-peanut sauce poured over.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g chai poh (preserved radish), finely chopped
steps: Whisk the flours, salt and 200 ml water together, then whisk in 300 ml just-boiled water to form a thin warm batter.
Pour into oiled small metal cups and steam over high heat for 15 minutes until set with a slight dimple in the centre.
Fry the garlic and chai poh in the oil on medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, add the sugar, and cook until caramelised and fragrant.
Unmould the rice cakes, top each with a spoon of chai poh, and serve with sambal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g glutinous rice for filling, soaked 4 hours
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
2 tbsp dried shrimp, soaked and chopped
200 g glutinous rice flour and 50 g rice flour
220 ml boiling water with a few drops red food colouring
steps: Steam the soaked glutinous rice for 20 minutes until tender.
Fry the shallots, pork, mushrooms and shrimp in oil for 5 minutes until the pork is cooked, add the soy sauce, peanuts and steamed rice, and toss until coloured and dry.
Mix both flours with the hot pink water and 1 tbsp oil and knead to a smooth dough.
Wrap a portion of dough around a spoonful of filling and press into an oiled peach-shaped kueh mould, then unmould onto a square of banana leaf.
Steam over high heat for 10 to 12 minutes until the skin is glossy and soft, then brush with oil.
Serve warm, or pan-fry the next day until crisp.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g Chinese garlic chives (ku chai), finely chopped
steps: Toss the chives with salt, pepper, soy sauce and sesame oil.
Mix the rice flour and tapioca starch, pour in the boiling water and 1 tbsp oil, and knead into a smooth translucent dough.
Roll small pieces into thin rounds, fill with chives, and pleat closed.
Steam on an oiled tray over high heat for 10 to 12 minutes until the skin turns translucent.
Pan-fry in the remaining oil for 2 minutes per side until crisp, if liked, and serve with chili sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g fresh kway teow (flat rice noodles)
1 litre pork bone or chicken stock
1 tbsp crispy pork lard or fried garlic with its oil
2 tbsp chopped spring onion and Chinese celery
steps: Bring the stock to a simmer and season with the fish sauce.
Cook the fish balls and fish cake in the stock for 5 minutes, then add the pork slices and simmer 2 minutes until no longer pink.
Blanch the noodles and bean sprouts in boiling water for 30 seconds and divide between bowls.
Ladle over the stock, pork, fish balls and fish cake, and finish with lard, spring onion and celery.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 ml light soy sauce and 40 ml dark soy sauce
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 5 slices galangal
4 hard-boiled eggs and 2 blocks firm tofu puffs
400 g dried broad rice sheets (kway), broken into squares
steps: Bring the water, soy sauces, rock sugar and spices to a boil, add the pork belly and intestines, and simmer covered on low heat for 90 minutes until tender.
Add the eggs and tofu for the last 30 minutes.
Boil the rice sheets in salted water for 5 to 6 minutes until silky and curled, then serve in bowls with a ladle of thinned braising liquid.
Slice the pork, intestines, eggs and tofu and serve on a separate plate with the chili vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Salted Vegetable Duck Soup (Kiam Chye Ark)

ingredients: 1 duck (about 2 kg), cut into large pieces
300 g salted mustard greens (kiam chye), soaked 30 minutes and cut into chunks
steps: Blanch the duck pieces in boiling water for 5 minutes, then rinse off the scum.
Put the duck, water, ginger and salted vegetable in a pot and bring to a boil.
Add the tomatoes and sour plums and simmer covered on low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until the duck is fork tender.
Taste for salt, add the pepper and brandy, and serve hot with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg daikon radish (lo bak), cut into thick strips
steps: Toss the radish strips with the salt in a bowl, weigh down and leave overnight until they release a lot of liquid.
Squeeze dry and spread the strips on racks in full sun for 2 to 3 days, bringing them in at night, until shrunken and leathery.
Toss with the brown sugar and five-spice and pack tightly into a clean sterilised jar.
Store in a cool place for 1 week before using; rinse and chop before frying to serve with porridge or in chwee kueh.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 120 ml shallot oil or lard (traditional, gives the dish its richness)
150 g ginkgo nuts, shelled and cooked
steps: Steam the taro slices over high heat for 25 to 30 minutes until completely soft.
Mash to a fine paste while hot, pressing through a sieve if you want it very smooth.
In a wok on low heat, combine the taro, sugar, water and lard, and stir continuously for 8 to 10 minutes until glossy and smooth.
Simmer the ginkgo nuts in the syrup for 5 minutes until glazed.
Serve the paste warm, topped with the ginkgo nuts and a drizzle of coconut milk.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g split mung beans, soaked 2 hours
4 tbsp sweet potato starch mixed with 6 tbsp water
steps: Drain the soaked beans and steam on a cloth over high heat for 20 minutes until tender but whole.
Bring the water, rock sugar and pandan to a boil until the sugar dissolves, then remove the pandan.
Add the beans, return to a boil, and stir in the starch slurry until the soup turns clear and thick.
Serve hot topped with slices of crisp youtiao.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 g Phoenix Dancong oolong tea (Fenghuang Dancong)
1 small gaiwan or clay teapot and tiny cups
steps: Warm the teapot and cups by pouring boiling water over and into them, then discard the water.
Fill the pot about one third with the tea leaves, add boiling water and pour it off immediately to rinse and awaken the leaves.
Refill with water just off the boil, steep for 10 to 15 seconds, and pour in a circular motion across all cups so every cup gets an even strength.
Repeat for 6 to 8 infusions, lengthening each steep by a few seconds, and sip slowly, traditionally after a meal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp sand ginger powder (shajiang fen; substitute ground galangal)
3 slices ginger and 2 scallions, for the cavity
2 sheets greaseproof or sandwich paper, lightly oiled
1 tbsp sesame oil mixed with 1/2 tsp sand ginger powder and 3 tbsp peanut oil, for dipping
steps: Rub the chicken inside and out with sand ginger powder, salt and wine, stuff with ginger and scallions and leave to dry 1 hour.
Wrap the chicken tightly in two layers of oiled paper.
Heat the rock salt in a wok or heavy pot over high heat 15 minutes, stirring, until very hot and crackling.
Bury the chicken completely in the salt, cover and cook on low heat 50-60 minutes until the thigh juices run clear (75 C).
Unwrap, tear or chop into pieces and serve with the sand ginger dipping oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 squares firm tofu (about 600 g), each halved into triangles
100 g white fish paste (or minced mackerel)
3 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
1 tbsp dried shrimp, soaked and chopped
1 tbsp light soy, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp cornstarch, 1/4 tsp white pepper
1 tbsp oyster sauce and 150 ml chicken stock
2 tbsp peanut oil and 2 scallions, chopped
steps: Mix the pork, fish paste, mushrooms, dried shrimp and seasonings until sticky.
Cut a pocket into the long side of each tofu triangle, dust with cornstarch and pack in the filling.
Pan-fry the tofu meat-side down in oil over medium heat 3-4 minutes until golden, then brown the other sides.
Add oyster sauce and stock, cover and simmer 8-10 minutes until the filling is cooked through.
Scatter scallions and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Meicai Kourou (Pork Belly with Preserved Mustard)

ingredients: 800 g skin-on pork belly, one slab
150 g dried preserved mustard greens (mei cai), soaked and rinsed well
1 tbsp red fermented bean curd (nam yu)
steps: Boil the pork 30 minutes, then prick the skin, rub with dark soy and fry skin-side down in hot oil (covered) until blistered and brown.
Soak in cold water 10 minutes so the skin wrinkles, then cut into 1 cm slices.
Squeeze the mei cai dry, chop and stir-fry with garlic, sugar and half the soy 5 minutes.
Mix the remaining soy, nam yu, wine and five-spice, toss the pork slices in it and lay them skin-side down in a deep bowl, then pack mei cai on top.
Steam 2-2.5 hours until meltingly tender, invert onto a plate and serve with rice or steamed buns.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Hakka Rice Wine Chicken (Niang Jiu Ji)

ingredients: 1 kg chicken pieces on the bone
20 g dried wood ear mushrooms, soaked
400 ml Hakka glutinous rice wine (bought; substitute Shaoxing wine with 1 tsp sugar)
steps: Fry the ginger slowly in sesame oil over medium-low heat 5 minutes until dry and fragrant.
Add the chicken and fry 5-6 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in rice wine and water, add wood ear and red dates, and simmer covered 25-30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Season with salt and serve hot; this is the classic Hakka confinement dish for new mothers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
1 tbsp light soy and 1 tbsp oyster sauce
steps: Steam the taro 20 minutes until soft, mash while hot and knead with tapioca starch and salt into a smooth dough.
Roll into marble-sized balls and press a dent in each with a fingertip to make the abacus bead shape.
Boil them in batches until they float and turn slightly translucent, then 1 minute more; drain into cold water.
Stir-fry garlic, pork, mushrooms, dried shrimp and squid 4 minutes until the pork is cooked.
Add the abacus seeds, soy, oyster sauce and a splash of water and toss 2 minutes until chewy and glossy; finish with scallions and coriander.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g fresh thin Meizhou yanmian or alkaline egg noodles
3 tbsp lard (or peanut oil), plus 4 shallots, sliced
2 tsp fish sauce or light soy
150 g minced pork, cooked with 1 tsp soy
400 ml pork bone soup with 100 g pork liver and 100 g lean pork slices (san ji tang), to serve
steps: Fry the shallots in lard over medium heat until golden to make crispy shallots and shallot lard.
Boil the noodles 30-40 seconds until just tender and drain very well.
Toss the hot noodles with shallot lard, fish sauce and the crispy shallots.
Top with the cooked mince and scallions, and serve with a bowl of the pork soup on the side (see Hakka Three Delicacies Soup).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g pork intestine, cleaned and pre-boiled, or pork meatballs
1 tsp cornstarch and 1 tsp soy for the meat
1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp white pepper
steps: Soak the liver in cold water 10 minutes, then toss liver and lean pork with soy and cornstarch.
Bring the stock and ginger to a boil and add the intestine or meatballs for 3 minutes.
Add the lean pork and liver, simmer 2-3 minutes until just cooked through and no longer pink.
Add the greens for 30 seconds, season with salt and pepper and serve with fried shallots, alongside yanmian.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 40 g fresh Thai basil, mint and coriander leaves
20 g green tea leaves (or 2 tbsp matcha)
3 tbsp roasted peanuts and 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
600 g cooked brown or white rice
200 g firm tofu, diced and pan-fried
300 g mixed greens (long beans, cabbage, sweet potato leaves, chives), finely chopped
100 g preserved radish (chai poh), rinsed and chopped
steps: Pound the herbs, tea, peanuts, sesame and salt in a mortar (or blender) into a paste, then whisk in the hot water to make the green "thunder tea".
Stir-fry each vegetable separately in a little oil with a pinch of salt 1-2 minutes until just tender.
Fry the chai poh 2 minutes until fragrant.
Fill bowls with rice and arrange the vegetables, tofu and chai poh on top in sections.
Pour the tea over at the table or serve it alongside to drink as a soup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml Hakka glutinous rice wine (huangjiu style), bought from a licensed producer
steps: Hakka niang jiu is a sweet, amber rice wine brewed from glutinous rice; buy it from licensed producers or Chinese grocers rather than making it at home.
Serve it warmed: heat gently with ginger and sugar over low heat 5-10 minutes until steaming (do not boil), and pour into small cups.
It is drunk at festivals and weddings and is the cooking base of Hakka Rice Wine Chicken; serve to adults only.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Braised Sea Cucumber with Scallion (Congshao Haishen)

ingredients: 400 g ready-soaked sea cucumber (haishen), cut lengthwise into thick strips
6 thick Zhangqiu scallions (dacong), white parts only, cut into 6 cm lengths (sub: leeks or large spring onions)
300 ml clear pork or chicken stock
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Blanch the sea cucumber in boiling water with 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and a scallion knot for 3 minutes to remove any fishy smell, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-low heat and fry the scallion whites slowly for 8–10 minutes until deep golden and fragrant; lift out half the scallions and keep the scallion oil in the wok.
Add the remaining wine, stock, light and dark soy, oyster sauce and sugar, bring to a boil, add the sea cucumber and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes so it absorbs the sauce.
Return the fried scallions, then stir in the cornstarch slurry a little at a time until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the sea cucumber.
Drizzle with a spoonful of the scallion oil and serve hot with steamed rice or mantou.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Sweet and Sour Yellow River Carp (Tangcu Liyu)

ingredients: 1 whole carp (liyu), about 1 kg, scaled and gutted (sub: sea bass or snapper)
120 g potato starch mixed with 120 ml water to a thick batter
1 tbsp each minced ginger, garlic and scallion
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Score the fish deeply on both sides every 2 cm, cutting down to the bone, then rub with salt and Shaoxing wine and rest 10 minutes.

Coat the fish all over with the starch batter, getting it into the cuts, then hold it by the tail and lower it into oil heated to 180°C, bending the body so the head and tail curl upward; fry for 8–10 minutes, ladling oil over the top, until crisp and cooked through to the bone.
In a clean wok with 2 tbsp of the hot oil, fry the ginger, garlic and scallion for 30 seconds, then add sugar, vinegar, soy and water and boil until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the slurry until thick and glossy, then add 1 tbsp hot oil and stir until the sauce bubbles.
Set the fish upright on a platter and immediately pour the sizzling sauce over it; serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp honey mixed with 2 tbsp water
1 thumb ginger, sliced, and 3 scallions, knotted
spice bag: 2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 slices galangal (sub: extra ginger), 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, 1 black cardamom (caoguo), 3 cloves, 1 small piece dried tangerine peel
steps: Tuck the wings into the beak opening and fold the legs into the cavity so the bird sits compact, then brush all over with honey water and let dry 15 minutes.
Fry the chicken in oil heated to 170°C for 4–5 minutes, turning, until evenly deep amber; drain.

Put the chicken in a heavy pot with the spice bag, ginger, scallions, soy sauces, salt and water to cover, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over the lowest heat for 2.5–3 hours until the meat is falling-off-the-bone tender.
Lift out very carefully with two wide spatulas to keep it whole, and serve warm or at room temperature; the chicken should pull apart with chopsticks.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp salt and 2 tbsp flour, for cleaning
1 tbsp each minced ginger, garlic and scallion
0.5 tsp each ground cinnamon, white pepper and Sichuan pepper powder
steps: Turn the intestines inside out, scrub with salt and flour, rinse well several times, then blanch in boiling water for 5 minutes and rinse again.
Simmer in fresh water with ginger and scallion for 1.5 hours until tender, then cool and cut into 3 cm rings.
Pan-fry the rings in hot oil for 4–5 minutes until golden, then push aside, add the sugar and cook until it melts to a light caramel.
Add ginger, garlic and scallion, then the wine, vinegar, soy sauces and 150 ml water; braise over low heat for 15 minutes, turning, until the sauce reduces and coats the intestines.
Sprinkle with the ground spices, toss, garnish with coriander and serve; the taste should be sour, sweet, salty and slightly spicy all at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp minced ginger and 2 scallions, minced
1 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp white pepper
1 tsp dark soy sauce and 1 tsp sugar
steps: Mix the pork with water chestnuts, egg, cornstarch, ginger, scallion, 1 tbsp light soy, salt and pepper, stirring in one direction until sticky, then shape into 4 large balls, slapping each between your palms to firm it.
Fry the meatballs in oil at 170°C for 5–6 minutes until golden brown all over; drain.
Put them in a pot with 500 ml water, the remaining soy sauces, sugar and star anise, bring to a boil and simmer covered over low heat for 40 minutes until cooked through.
Arrange the meatballs on blanched bok choy, reduce the braising liquid until slightly thick and spoon it over; serve with rice for celebrations.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g pork loin, cut into thin shreds
1 tsp each light soy sauce, cornstarch and Shaoxing wine, for marinating
3 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
15 g dried wood ear mushrooms, soaked and shredded
30 g dried daylily buds (huanghua cai), soaked and knotted (optional)
steps: Marinate the pork with soy, cornstarch and wine for 10 minutes.
Scramble the eggs in 1 tbsp hot oil over medium heat into large soft curds that resemble osmanthus flowers, then remove.
Stir-fry the pork in the remaining oil over high heat for 1–2 minutes until it turns white and is cooked through.
Add wood ear, daylilies and scallion and stir-fry 1 minute, then add cucumber, the egg and soy sauce and toss 30 seconds.
Finish with sesame oil and serve hot with rice or rolled in thin pancakes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g pork stomach (the thick inner muscle, duren), cleaned
1 tbsp each minced garlic, ginger and scallion
steps: Peel off the tough skin of the stomach and gizzards, then score each piece in a fine crosshatch about two-thirds deep and cut into bite-size pieces.
Mix the stock, wine, soy, salt, sugar and cornstarch in a bowl as the finishing sauce.
Plunge the pieces into rapidly boiling water for 5 seconds, drain, then flash-fry in oil heated to 200°C for 10–15 seconds until they bloom open; drain immediately.

With 1 tbsp oil in the very hot wok, fry the aromatics for 5 seconds, add the offal and the sauce, toss for 10–15 seconds until glossy and serve at once; the pieces must stay crisp, not rubbery, and be fully opaque inside.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 large prawns (duixia), shell on, legs and veins removed
steps: Heat the oil over medium heat, add the prawns and press their heads with a spatula so the red coral oil runs out; fry 2 minutes per side.
Add ginger and scallion, then the wine, sugar, soy, salt and water, and bring to a boil.
Cover and braise over low heat for 4–5 minutes until the prawns are cooked through, then uncover and reduce the sauce until thick and bright red.
Arrange the prawns on a platter, pour the sauce over and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg skin-on pork belly, cut into 10 cm x 3 cm slabs
12 strips dried gourd or kitchen string, for tying
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 bay leaves
steps: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 5 minutes, rinse, then tie each slab tightly with a strip of soaked dried gourd or string.
Melt the rock sugar in the oil over low heat until amber, then add the pork and turn to coat.
Add soy sauces, wine, spices, ginger, scallions and hot water to cover, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over very low heat for 2 hours until the pork is meltingly soft.
Uncover and reduce the sauce for 10 minutes until it coats the pork; serve each slab with rice and a ladle of sauce, as at Jinan bazi rou stalls.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Sweet and Sour Pork Tenderloin (Tangcu Liji)

ingredients: 400 g pork tenderloin, cut into finger-thick strips
0.5 tsp salt and 1 tsp Shaoxing wine
80 g potato starch mixed with 70 ml water to a thick batter
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 60 ml water
steps: Marinate the pork with salt and wine for 10 minutes, then coat well in the batter.
Fry the strips in oil at 160°C for 3 minutes until set and cooked through, remove, raise the oil to 190°C and fry again for 1 minute until crisp and golden.
In a clean wok, simmer sugar, vinegar, soy, ketchup and the slurry over medium heat until thick and glossy.
Toss the pork quickly in the sauce, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve immediately while crisp.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g pork tenderloin, cut into finger-thick strips
1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns and 1 tbsp salt, toasted and ground (huajiao yan)
steps: Marinate the pork with soy, wine and salt for 15 minutes, then mix in the egg and cornstarch to a thick coating.
Fry the strips one by one in oil at 160°C for 3–4 minutes until pale golden and cooked through; drain.
Reheat the oil to 190°C and fry again for 1 minute until deeply crisp.
Serve hot with Sichuan pepper salt for dipping.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g pork belly or ribs, cut into large pieces
500 g kelp (haidai), soaked and cut into wide strips
4 small whole fish such as crucian carp, cleaned
400 g firm tofu, fried until golden
300 ml Chinese rice vinegar (or Shanxi aged vinegar)
150 ml light soy sauce and 2 tbsp dark soy sauce
steps: Line a large heavy pot with cabbage leaves, then layer kelp, fish, pork, lotus root, tofu and scallions, finishing with more cabbage.
Mix vinegar, sugar, soy sauces, salt and enough water to almost cover, pour in, bring to a boil and skim.
Cover and simmer over the lowest heat for 4–5 hours until the fish bones are soft and edible and the pork is very tender.
Cool completely in the pot, then refrigerate overnight; serve cold in slices as a New Year appetizer with the jellied juices.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg pork belly and pork offal (heart, intestine, liver), cleaned
3 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp dark soy sauce
spice bag: 3 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, 2 bay leaves
steps: Blanch the pork, offal and chicken in boiling water for 5 minutes and rinse.

Put them in a wide open pot with soy sauces, salt, spice bag, ginger and water to cover, bring to a boil and simmer uncovered over low heat for 2.5–3 hours, topping up water, until everything is tender.
Bring the open pot to the table on a burner so it stays hot, and slice the meats thinly as diners request.
Each person wraps slices of meat with scallion, cucumber and sweet bean sauce in a pancake and sips the rich broth on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Soak the clams in salted water for 2 hours to purge sand, scrub them, and discard any that are open and do not close when tapped.
Fry the garlic, ginger, dried chillies and bean paste in hot oil over medium heat for 30 seconds until red and fragrant.
Turn the heat to high, add the clams and wine, toss and cover for 2–3 minutes until the shells open.
Add green chillies, soy and scallions and toss 30 seconds; discard any clams that stay shut and serve with a cold Qingdao beer.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g pork bones and 1 chicken carcass
400 g napa cabbage hearts, cut into strips
50 g Jinhua ham or bacon, shredded
steps: Blanch the bones, then boil them hard with ginger and 2 l water over high heat for 1.5–2 hours, topping up with boiling water, until the stock turns milky white.
Strain the stock and keep 800 ml.
Heat the lard, briefly stir-fry the cabbage and ham for 1 minute, then pour in the milky stock and boil 5 minutes until the cabbage is tender.
Season with salt and white pepper and serve in a deep bowl.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 ml water with 1 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp alkaline water (jianshui, sub: baked baking soda)
steps: Knead the flour with the salted alkaline water into a smooth dough, then rest covered for 40 minutes.
Roll into a thick log, then stretch, fold and twist repeatedly until the dough is pliable; pull into thin strands by doubling and stretching 6–7 times, oiling lightly so they do not stick.
Fry the pork in oil until cooked, add shrimp and sweet bean sauce and cook 2 minutes; for the soup topping, season the stock with soy.
Boil the noodles for 1–2 minutes until just tender, then serve in hot broth topped with the pork-shrimp sauce, cucumber and scallion.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g plain flour mixed with 260 ml water, rested 30 minutes
500 g Spanish mackerel (bayu) fillet, skinned and boned
150 g pork fat or fatty pork mince
200 ml water infused with 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns and ginger, cooled
steps: Chop the fish and pork fat to a fine paste, then add the pepper-ginger water a spoonful at a time, stirring in one direction until it is absorbed and the filling is light and springy.
Season with salt and soy, then mix in the chives coated with sesame oil.
Roll the dough into thin rounds, fill each and pinch into large crescent dumplings.
Boil in plenty of water, adding a cup of cold water each time it returns to the boil, 3 times, until the dumplings float and the filling is cooked through; serve with black vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 crisp fried crackers (baocui) or wonton crisps
steps: Whisk the flours, salt and water into a thin, smooth batter and rest 10 minutes.
Heat a large flat griddle or nonstick pan over medium heat, wipe with oil, pour a ladle of batter and spread it very thin with a scraper; cook 1–2 minutes until dry and lightly crisp.
Flip, brush with sweet bean sauce and chilli sauce, scatter scallion and coriander, add a cracker and a whole scallion.
Fold and roll up firmly and eat hot, Shandong style, with the crunchy centre.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g extra flour, for kneading in
steps: Mix 500 g flour, yeast and water into a firm dough and let rise for 1.5 hours until doubled.
Knead hard while working in the extra flour a little at a time until the dough is very firm, smooth and silky; this gives the dense, chewy layers.
Divide into 8, shape each into a tall dome by tucking and rolling the dough between your palms, then rest covered for 30 minutes.
Steam over boiling water on high heat for 20–25 minutes, then turn off the heat and wait 5 minutes before lifting the lid so they do not collapse.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: natural food colouring (beet, spinach, pumpkin juice) for decoration
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and water into a firm dough, knead until very smooth and let rise for 1.5 hours.
Knead again thoroughly, divide into large and small pieces, and shape a large round base for each bun, pressing red dates into it in a flower pattern.
Shape small pieces of coloured dough into fish, flowers, and peaches and attach them on top with a dab of water, using the red bean paste for small details.
Rest for 30 minutes, then steam over high heat for 35–40 minutes and wait 5 minutes before lifting the lid; serve at weddings and New Year.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix flour, water, sugar and salt into a soft dough, knead 5 minutes and rest 30 minutes.
Divide into 20 tiny balls, press each into a thin round, then press one side into the sesame seeds and stretch with your fingertips until paper-thin and almost translucent.
Stick them to a hot oiled baking sheet sesame side up and bake at 180°C for 10–15 minutes until crisp and pale golden.
Cool completely so they turn shatteringly crisp, then store airtight.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g millet flour (or millet ground in a blender)
steps: Boil 1 l water with the peanuts, tofu, tofu skin and vermicelli for 10 minutes.
Whisk the millet flour with 200 ml cold water to a smooth paste and pour slowly into the pot, stirring constantly.
Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until thick and silky.
Add spinach, salt, pepper and ground ginger, cook 2 minutes and serve hot for breakfast with youtiao.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Toss the sweet potato with cornstarch and fry at 170°C for 6–8 minutes until golden and soft inside; drain.
In a clean wok with 1 tbsp oil and the water, cook the sugar over low heat, stirring, until it turns light amber and the bubbles become small.
Add the sweet potato and toss quickly to coat, sprinkle with sesame seeds and plate on an oiled dish.
Serve immediately with a bowl of cold water; pull a piece away so the caramel stretches into threads, then dip it to harden the sugar before eating.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 mandarin fish (guiyu), about 800 g, scaled and gutted (sub: sea bass)
1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
30 g pine nuts, toasted, and 30 g peas, blanched
steps: Cut off the head, then slice the fish along both sides of the backbone to the tail, leaving the two fillets attached at the tail; remove the spine and score the flesh diagonally in a crosshatch down to, but not through, the skin.
Rub with salt and wine, then coat thoroughly in potato starch, opening the cuts so every strand is dusted; dust the head as well.

Holding the tail, lower the fish into oil at 180°C, ladling oil over so the flesh curls into a 'fur' pattern, and fry 4–5 minutes until crisp and cooked through; fry the head too, then arrange both on a platter in the shape of a squirrel.
Simmer ketchup, sugar, vinegar and water, thicken with the slurry, add 1 tbsp hot oil, peas and pine nuts and stir until it sizzles.
Pour the hot sauce over the fish at the table so it crackles, and serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g pork belly or shoulder (70% lean, 30% fat), hand-chopped
1 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp white pepper
steps: Dice the pork finely by hand rather than mincing so the meatballs stay tender, then mix with water chestnuts, egg, cornstarch, wine, soy, salt, pepper and ginger-scallion water, stirring in one direction until sticky.
Shape into 4 large loose balls, tossing each between wet palms to firm the surface.
Line a clay pot with cabbage leaves, add the stock and bring to a gentle simmer, then lower in the meatballs and cover them with more leaves.
Simmer over the lowest heat for 1.5–2 hours (Yangzhou qingdun style, the clear-stewed version) until the meatballs are cooked through and so tender they can be eaten with a spoon; serve in the pot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g salt plus 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns, dry-roasted together
steps: Rub the duck inside and out with the hot pepper salt and refrigerate 8–10 hours to cure.
Rinse the duck, then make a brine by boiling the water with salt, ginger, scallion, star anise and wine.

Put a ginger-scallion bundle in the cavity, lower the duck into the barely simmering brine, fill the cavity with liquid, then cover and keep the heat just below a simmer (about 85°C) for 50–60 minutes, turning once, until the juices at the thigh run clear.
Cool in the brine, then chop into pieces and serve at room temperature with a spoon of brine; the skin should be white and the meat juicy and pink-tinged from the cure.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg pork spare ribs, cut into 6 cm pieces
1 tbsp red yeast rice (hongqu mi) in a spice bag, for colour (optional)
steps: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for 3 minutes and rinse.
Fry ginger and scallion in oil, add the ribs and sear 3 minutes, then add wine, soy sauces, rock sugar, spices, red yeast rice and hot water just to cover.
Bring to a boil, then simmer covered over low heat for 1 hour until tender but still on the bone.
Uncover and reduce over medium heat for 15 minutes, basting, until the sauce is thick, sticky and glossy; serve warm with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g rice-field eel (shanyu), cleaned and boned (sub: freshwater eel fillets)
steps: Blanch the eel briefly, cut into thin strips 6 cm long and pat completely dry.
Fry at 180°C for 4 minutes, remove, then fry again at 200°C for 2–3 minutes until very crisp and dry; drain.
In a clean wok cook ginger, soy sauces, sugar and wine over medium heat until syrupy.
Toss the eel in the syrup until glazed and dark, add sesame oil and seeds, and serve at room temperature as a crisp, sweet appetizer.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g rice-field eel (shanyu), cleaned and boned
1 tbsp salt and 1 tbsp vinegar, for blanching
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Blanch the eel in boiling salted, vinegared water for 2 minutes until it curls and is cooked through, then cut into 8 cm strips.
Fry half the garlic and the ginger in hot lard, add the eel and stir-fry 1 minute.
Add wine, soy sauces and sugar, toss, then thicken with the slurry until glossy.
Plate the eel, top with the remaining raw garlic and white pepper, and pour over 2 tbsp sizzling hot lard so the garlic crackles; serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp red yeast rice (hongqu mi) soaked in 100 ml water, strained (for colour)
steps: Blanch the pork 5 minutes, then cut into 1.5 cm cubes and score the skin side of each in a crosshatch so it looks like a cherry when cooked.
Sear the cubes in oil over medium heat for 3 minutes, then add ginger, scallion, wine, soy, red yeast water, rock sugar and water.
Bring to a boil and simmer covered over low heat for 1 hour until tender.
Uncover and reduce, turning the pieces, until the glossy cherry-red sauce coats each cube; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole wild duck or Muscovy duck, about 1 kg (sub: second small duck)
steps: Carefully debone each bird whole through the neck opening, keeping the skin intact, then blanch briefly and rinse.

Stuff the pigeon with some ham, mushrooms and bamboo shoots, place it inside the wild duck, then place the wild duck inside the domestic duck, filling gaps with the remaining ham, mushrooms and shoots.
Put in a large clay pot with ginger, scallion, wine and water to cover, bring to a boil and skim.
Simmer over the lowest heat for 3.5–4 hours until all three birds are fully cooked and tender, season with salt, and serve in the pot so diners can cut through the three layers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Braised Shredded Tofu (Da Zhu Gan Si)

ingredients: 4 sheets pressed dry tofu (baidoufu gan), sliced paper-thin and shredded as fine as threads
1 small bunch pea shoots or bok choy hearts
steps: Blanch the tofu shreds twice in boiling water with baking soda for 1 minute each time, then rinse well in cold water to remove the beany taste.
Bring the stock to a boil, add the tofu and simmer 10 minutes so it absorbs the flavour.
Add the bamboo shoots and shrimp and cook 2 minutes until the shrimp are pink, then add the pea shoots and salt.
Pour into a bowl and arrange the chicken and ham on top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook
