ingredients: 1 kg pork hock or trotter meat with skin, boned
Zhenjiang black vinegar and fine ginger shreds, to serve
steps: Rub the pork with salt and refrigerate 8–10 hours to cure, then rinse and soak in water for 1 hour.
Simmer with peppercorns, star anise, ginger, scallion, wine and water to cover over low heat for 2.5–3 hours until the meat is very soft and the stock is rich.
Pack the meat skin side down tightly into a dish, strain over enough stock to just cover, place a weight on top and refrigerate overnight until set into a clear jelly.
Slice and serve cold with Zhenjiang vinegar and ginger shreds, as eaten with morning tea in Zhenjiang.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 50 g cooked chicken breast, shredded hair-thin
2 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and shredded
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water (optional)
steps: Trim the tofu and slice it very thin with a wet knife, then cut into hair-fine threads and slide them into a bowl of water to separate.
Bring the stock to a simmer with the mushrooms, bamboo shoots, chicken and ham and cook 3 minutes.
Drain the tofu threads gently into the soup, stirring very gently, and bring just back to a simmer; season with salt and thicken lightly if desired.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot; the tofu should float in fine strands.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Duck Blood and Vermicelli Soup (Yaxue Fensi Tang)

ingredients: 1 l duck stock (from simmering duck bones)
300 g set duck blood (yaxue), cut into cubes
150 g cooked duck gizzards, liver and intestine, sliced
steps: Bring the duck stock to a boil and season with salt and pepper.
Blanch the vermicelli in boiling water for 1–2 minutes until soft, then divide among bowls.
Simmer the duck blood and tofu puffs in the stock for 3–4 minutes until heated through and the blood is firm throughout.
Ladle the stock, blood and tofu over the noodles, top with the duck offal, chilli oil and coriander, and serve hot in Nanjing style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole old hen or 1 kg chicken pieces
50 g plain flour mixed with 100 ml water
steps: Simmer the chicken, pork bones, ginger and barley in water over low heat for 1.5–2 hours, then remove the chicken and shred the meat.
Whisk the flour paste into the boiling broth and simmer 5 minutes until lightly thick.
Return the shredded chicken, season with salt and plenty of black pepper.
Drizzle in the beaten egg, stirring gently, so it sets in ribbons; serve hot with sesame oil for breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g cooked jasmine rice, chilled overnight
80 g ham or Chinese barbecued pork, diced
2 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
steps: Stir-fry the shrimp in 1 tbsp oil over high heat for 1 minute until pink, then remove.
Scramble the eggs in the remaining oil until just set, then add the rice and toss over high heat for 3–4 minutes, breaking up clumps, until every grain is separate and hot.
Add ham, chicken, mushrooms, bamboo shoots and peas and toss 2 minutes.
Return the shrimp, season with salt, add scallions and serve; the rice should be golden, loose and lightly salted without soy sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g blue carp or other firm white fish, cut into pieces
steps: Fry the fish in hot oil until crisp and golden, then braise briefly with wine, soy sauces and sugar until glazed; set aside the fish.
Fry the fish bones and trimmings with ginger, add the stock and simmer 20 minutes, then strain and combine with the fish braising juices for a rich, dark broth.
Boil the noodles for 1–2 minutes until just tender and drain.
Place the noodles in bowls, ladle over the hot broth, top with the fish and scallions and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g fresh wheat noodles (or hand-cut noodles)
200 g bok choy or pea shoots
steps: Bring a very large pot of water to a rolling boil and float a small wooden pot lid on top, as done in Zhenjiang, or simply cook in a wide pot.
Stir-fry the pork in oil until cooked through, then add 1 tbsp soy and set aside as a topping.
Boil the noodles for 2–3 minutes until tender, adding the greens for the last minute.
Mix soy, vinegar, lard and sugar in each bowl, add a ladle of cooking water, then the noodles and greens; top with pork, dried shrimp and scallions.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and water into a soft dough, knead until smooth and let rise for 1 hour.
Stir-fry the pork and chicken in oil until cooked, add bamboo shoots, sweet bean sauce, soy and sugar and cook 3 minutes, then thicken with cornstarch mixed with water and cool completely.
Divide the dough into 12, roll into rounds thicker in the centre, fill, and pleat closed with 30 pleats around the top; rest 20 minutes.
Steam over high heat for 15 minutes, then wait 3 minutes before lifting the lid; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Crab Roe Soup Dumplings (Xie Huang Tangbao)

ingredients: 150 g crab meat and roe from 3 steamed hairy crabs (sub: crab meat plus salted egg yolk)
300 g plain flour mixed with 150 ml hot water
Zhenjiang black vinegar with ginger shreds, for dipping
steps: Simmer the pork skin with ginger, scallion and 1.5 l water for 3 hours, strain, and refrigerate overnight to set into an aspic; dice finely.
Fry the crab meat and roe briefly in lard with a little ginger, cool, then mix with pork mince, soy, salt, sugar and plenty of diced aspic.
Roll the dough very thin into large rounds, fill each generously and pleat closed at the top.
Steam over high heat for 10–12 minutes until the filling is cooked and the aspic melts into soup; bite a small hole, sip the soup through a straw or spoon, then eat with vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp instant yeast (Wuxi dough is lightly leavened)
250 g pork skin aspic, finely diced
steps: Make the aspic a day ahead by simmering pork skin with ginger and water for 3 hours, straining and chilling overnight.
Mix the flour, yeast and water into a smooth dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the pork with soy, sugar, salt and ginger-scallion water in one direction until sticky, then fold in the aspic; the filling should taste noticeably sweet.
Roll small thin wrappers, fill and pleat into small round dumplings, rest 10 minutes, and steam over high heat for 8–10 minutes until cooked through; serve with vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g lard (for the flaky oil paste)
100 g extra flour (for the oil paste)
100 g pork belly, finely diced, or crispy pork lard bits (youzha)
1 tbsp honey mixed with 1 tbsp water
steps: Mix 400 g flour, yeast and water into a soft dough and rest 40 minutes; separately rub the lard and extra flour together into a paste.
Mix the pork, scallions and salt for the filling.
Roll the dough into a rectangle, spread with the lard paste, roll up into a log, cut into 12 pieces, flatten, fill with the pork mix and seal.
Press into flat ovals, brush with honey water, dip into sesame seeds and bake at 220°C for 15–20 minutes until puffed, flaky and golden and the filling is cooked through.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g lard, softened (sub: vegetable shortening, but lard is traditional)
100 g candied pork fat cubes (tang zhi ding) or extra lard
2 tbsp red and green candied fruit shreds
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and water into a soft dough and let rise for 1 hour.
Roll into a thin, long rectangle, spread with lard, sprinkle evenly with sugar and candied pork fat, fold into thirds, and roll out and fold again to make 16 layers or more.
Press into a square tin, decorate with candied fruit, rest 30 minutes, then steam over high heat for 25–30 minutes until cooked through.
Cool slightly and cut into diamonds; each piece should show fine translucent sweet layers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g plain flour, 60 g lard and 90 ml warm water, for the water dough
150 g plain flour and 75 g lard, for the oil dough
steps: Knead the water dough and oil dough separately until smooth, rest 30 minutes, then divide each into 12 pieces.
Mix the pork with soy, salt, sugar, ginger and sesame oil in one direction until sticky (the savoury xianrou yuebing eaten hot at Mid-Autumn).
Wrap each oil dough piece in a water dough piece, roll into a long tongue, roll up, turn 90 degrees, roll out and roll up again; flatten into rounds and wrap around the filling, sealing well.
Press each into a flat disc and pan-fry over low heat with a lid for 10–12 minutes per side, or bake at 200°C for 25 minutes, until flaky, golden and the pork is cooked through; serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g pork skin, cleaned, plus 1 thumb ginger and 2 scallions for the aspic
250 g plain flour mixed with 130 ml water
Zhenjiang black vinegar with fine ginger shreds, for dipping
steps: Simmer the pork skin with ginger, scallion and 1.5 l water for 3 hours, strain and refrigerate overnight until firmly set, then dice finely.
Mix the pork with soy, salt, sugar and wine, then beat in the ginger-scallion water a spoonful at a time, stirring in one direction until sticky; fold in 200 g of the aspic.
Knead the dough smooth, rest 30 minutes, divide into 30 small pieces and roll each into a thin round about 8 cm across with a thinner edge.
Place a spoonful of filling in the centre and pleat closed with 18 fine pleats; set on parchment or napa cabbage in a bamboo steamer.
Steam over high heat for 8 minutes until the wrappers are translucent and the filling is cooked through; lift gently into a spoon, nibble a hole, sip the soup and eat with vinegar and ginger.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g pork skin aspic, diced (made as for xiaolongbao)
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds and 2 scallions, chopped
steps: Make the dough with flour, yeast and water and let rise 45 minutes; mix the pork with soy, sugar and salt until sticky, then fold in the aspic.
Divide the dough into 16, roll into small rounds, fill and pleat closed, then place pleat side down in a heavy oiled frying pan.
Fry over medium heat for 2 minutes until the bottoms start to colour, then pour in 120 ml water, cover tightly and cook for 8 minutes until the water is gone.
Uncover, sprinkle with sesame and scallion, and fry 2 minutes more until the bottoms are deep golden and crisp; serve straight from the pan, biting carefully as the soup is very hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g shepherd's purse (jicai), blanched, squeezed dry and chopped (sub: spinach or bok choy)
1 l clear chicken or pork stock
2 tbsp dried tiny shrimp, 1 sheet laver (zicai), torn, and 2 scallions, chopped
steps: Mix the pork with soy, salt, sugar and ginger until sticky, then mix in the greens and sesame oil.
Place a large spoonful of filling on each wrapper, fold in half into a rectangle, then fold again and bring the two corners together to form a plump 'ingot' shape.
Boil the wontons in plenty of water for 5–6 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Put dried shrimp, laver and scallion in each bowl, add hot seasoned stock, then the wontons; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
steps: Steam the drained glutinous rice over high heat on a cloth for 20 minutes until cooked.
Stir-fry the pork in oil until cooked, add mushrooms, soy sauces, sugar, pepper and stock, then mix in the rice and toss until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is brown and glossy; cool.
Place a spoonful in the centre of each wrapper and gather the edges loosely around it into an open-topped flower shape, pressing the filling firmly in.
Steam over high heat for 8–10 minutes until the wrappers are translucent; serve hot for breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 chicken legs (or a 1.2 kg young chicken)
1 tsp salt plus 1 tbsp for the marinade
steps: Bring a pot of water with ginger, scallion and 1 tsp salt to the boil, add the chicken, bring back to a simmer, then cover and poach on the lowest heat for 20–25 minutes until the juices run clear and the internal temperature reaches 74°C.
Plunge the chicken into ice water for 10 minutes to firm the skin, then drain.
Mix the wine, cooled stock, remaining salt, sugar and goji berries.
Submerge the chicken in the wine mixture, cover and refrigerate at least 8 hours or overnight; cut into pieces and serve cold with a little of the marinade.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 live hairy crabs or blue crabs, scrubbed
2 tbsp Chinese brown sugar or rock sugar (optional)
steps: For safety at home, cook the crabs first: steam over high heat for 12–15 minutes until the shells turn bright orange and the meat is fully opaque (traditional raw-marinated crab carries a parasite risk).
Boil the soy sauce, 300 ml water, sugar, salt, ginger and spices for 5 minutes, then cool completely and stir in the wine.
Pack the cooled crabs in a clean container, pour over the marinade to cover, weigh down, and refrigerate for 8–24 hours.
Cut into halves and serve cold with ginger vinegar; eat within 2 days.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 live hairy crabs (dazha xie, Chinese mitten crab), about 200 g each
1 thumb ginger, sliced, plus 2 tbsp very finely shredded ginger
2 tbsp Shaoxing wine, warmed, to drink alongside (optional)
steps: Scrub the crabs under running water while still tied, and keep them tied so the legs do not fall off during cooking.
Lay them belly side up in a steamer on ginger slices and perilla leaves, and steam over high heat for 15–18 minutes until the shells are bright orange and the roe is set.
Mix the vinegar, sugar and ginger shreds as a dipping sauce.
Serve hot, opening the shell to eat the golden roe first, and dipping the meat into the ginger vinegar; drink warm ginger tea or Shaoxing wine with it in the autumn season.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g medium river or sea shrimp, shell on, legs and antennae trimmed
steps: Pat the shrimp completely dry.
Fry them in oil at 190°C for 1 minute, remove, reheat the oil and fry again for 30 seconds until the shells are crisp and the shrimp cooked through.
In a clean wok with 1 tbsp oil, fry ginger and scallion, then add wine, soy, sugar and vinegar and boil until syrupy.
Toss the shrimp in the sauce until glazed and serve at once; the shells should be crisp enough to eat.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g rice-field eel (shanyu), cleaned, boned and blanched until cooked, cut into strips
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Stir-fry the ginger in oil, add the eel and toss over high heat for 1 minute.
Add wine, soy sauces and sugar, cook 1 minute, then thicken with the slurry until glossy.
Spoon onto a plate, make a well in the centre and place the raw garlic and white pepper in it.
Heat the sesame oil until smoking and pour it over the garlic at the table so it sizzles; toss and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole duck, about 2 kg, deboned whole
6 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
50 g lotus seeds and 50 g chestnuts, cooked
3 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp dark soy sauce
steps: Rub the deboned duck inside with 1 tbsp soy and the wine.
Stir-fry all the stuffing ingredients in oil with the remaining soy and sugar for 5 minutes, then mix with the drained raw glutinous rice.
Stuff the duck loosely (the rice swells), sew up the opening, brush the skin with dark soy and fry briefly in hot oil to colour.
Place in a deep dish and steam over high heat for 3–3.5 hours, topping up water, until the duck is very tender and the rice inside is fully cooked.
Pour the juices into a pan, reduce to a glaze, brush over the duck and serve whole, cutting it open at the table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 pork loin chops, boneless, 1.5 cm thick
0.5 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp white pepper
Shanghai Worcester sauce (la jiangyou, sub: Worcestershire sauce), to serve
steps: Pound the chops with the back of a cleaver until thin and enlarged, scoring the edges so they stay flat.
Marinate with soy, wine, sugar, salt and pepper for 30 minutes.
Dip each chop in egg, then press into the breadcrumbs.
Fry in oil at 170°C for 3–4 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through; serve hot with a splash of Shanghai Worcester sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pork Chop with Rice Cakes (Paigu Niangao)

ingredients: 4 pork chops, pounded thin and marinated as for Shanghai fried pork chop
steps: Dust the marinated chops with cornstarch and fry at 175°C for 3–4 minutes until golden and cooked through.
In a clean wok with 1 tbsp oil, fry the scallions, then add soy sauces, sugar, wine and water and bring to a boil.
Add the rice cakes and simmer 5–6 minutes, stirring, until soft and coated in the thick brown sauce.
Add the pork chops, turn them in the sauce for 1 minute, and serve with the rice cakes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g Shanghai rice cake slices (niangao), soaked if dried
1 tsp each soy sauce and cornstarch, for the pork
200 g napa cabbage or bok choy, shredded
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
steps: Marinate the pork with soy and cornstarch for 10 minutes, then stir-fry in 1 tbsp oil until just cooked and remove.
Stir-fry the cabbage and mushrooms in the remaining oil for 2 minutes until wilted.
Add the rice cakes, soy sauces, sugar and water, cover and cook 3 minutes until the rice cakes are soft.
Return the pork and toss over high heat until the liquid is absorbed; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg grass carp or black carp steaks, cut 1.5 cm thick
2 star anise and 1 small cinnamon stick
steps: Marinate the fish with light soy, wine, ginger and scallion for 3–4 hours, then pat very dry.
Simmer the dark soy, rock sugar, spices and 300 ml water until slightly syrupy, then cool the sauce.
Fry the fish in oil at 190°C for 6–8 minutes until deep brown, crisp and cooked through.
Immediately drop the hot fish into the sauce, soak 2–3 minutes, then lift out; despite the name it is not smoked, and is served cold as a sweet, aromatic appetizer.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g kaofu (spongy wheat gluten), cut into chunks
20 g dried wood ear mushrooms, soaked
6 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked, liquid reserved
30 g dried daylily buds (huanghua cai), soaked
steps: Blanch the kaofu in boiling water for 3 minutes, then squeeze out the water thoroughly.
Fry the kaofu in oil over medium heat until lightly golden, then add all the mushrooms, daylilies and peanuts.
Add soy sauces, rock sugar, star anise and 300 ml mushroom soaking liquid, bring to a boil and braise covered for 20 minutes.
Uncover and reduce until the sauce is thick and glossy, finish with sesame oil, and serve cold or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Fry the scallions in the oil over medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes, stirring, until dark brown and crisp but not burnt.
Add the soy sauces and sugar to the oil, simmer 1 minute until bubbling and slightly syrupy, then turn off the heat.
Boil the noodles for 1–2 minutes until just tender and drain well.
Toss the hot noodles with several spoonfuls of the scallion oil sauce and top with crispy scallions.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp each soy sauce and cornstarch, for the pork
steps: Boil the noodles for 2 minutes, rinse in cold water and drain well.
Marinate the pork with soy and cornstarch, stir-fry in 1 tbsp oil until cooked through and remove.
Stir-fry the bok choy in the remaining oil for 1 minute, add the noodles, soy sauces and sugar and toss over high heat for 3 minutes until evenly brown.
Return the pork, add sesame oil, toss and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp peanut butter (or Chinese sesame paste) thinned with 3 tbsp water
200 g pork, shredded, stir-fried with bean sprouts (or crispy pork chop)
steps: Boil the noodles for 2 minutes until just tender, drain, toss with oil and fan them until cool so they stay separate.
Stir-fry the pork in a little oil until cooked through, add bean sprouts for 1 minute and season with soy.
Mix soy, vinegar and sugar into a sauce.
Pile noodles into plates, pour over the peanut sauce and soy-vinegar, add the pork topping and chilli oil, and mix well before eating on hot summer days.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 Chinese sausage (lap cheong) or 100 g cured pork (xianrou), diced
steps: Fry the sausage in lard for 2 minutes until the fat runs.
Add the bok choy stems and stir-fry 1 minute, then the leaves and salt.
Add the rice and stir to coat, then transfer to a rice cooker or pot, add water and cook covered over low heat for 20 minutes until tender.
Rest 10 minutes, fluff and serve; the crisp crust at the bottom of the pot is prized.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 youtiao (Chinese fried dough sticks), cut in half and re-crisped in the oven
50 g pickled mustard greens (zhacai), finely chopped
2 salted duck egg yolks, cooked and crumbled (optional)
2 tbsp sugar (for a sweet version, optional)
steps: Steam the drained glutinous rice on a cloth over high heat for 30 minutes until soft and sticky.
Spread a portion of hot rice into a thin rectangle on a damp cloth or plastic wrap.
Lay a piece of youtiao along the middle, scatter with pork floss, pickles and egg yolk.
Roll up tightly using the cloth, squeeze into a firm oval log, and eat warm for breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g plain flour and 60 ml vegetable oil, for the flaky paste
1 tbsp sugar (for a sweet version, optional)
2 tbsp malt syrup or honey mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and water into a soft dough and rest 30 minutes; cook the extra flour in the hot oil to a light paste and cool.
Roll the dough into a rectangle, spread with the oil paste, roll up into a log and cut into 12 pieces.
Flatten each, fill with salted scallion (vegetarian), seal, and roll into an oval about 1 cm thick.
Brush with syrup water, press into sesame seeds, and bake at 220°C for 15–18 minutes until puffed, flaky and golden like the colour of a cooked crab shell.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g fresh pork belly or ribs
300 g salted cured pork (xianrou) or Jinhua ham
500 g fresh spring bamboo shoots, peeled, blanched and cut into chunks (sub: canned bamboo shoots)
steps: Blanch the fresh pork and cured pork separately for 5 minutes and rinse.
Put both in a pot with ginger, scallion, wine and water, bring to a boil and simmer over low heat for 1.5 hours until the broth is milky and rich.
Add bamboo shoots and tofu knots and simmer 20–30 minutes.
Taste before seasoning, since the cured pork is salty; slice the meats and serve in the broth in spring.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g beef brisket or shank, cut into chunks
1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp sugar and 0.5 tsp black pepper
steps: Blanch the beef, then simmer in 2.5 l water for 1.5 hours until tender, keeping the broth.
Melt the butter, fry the onion until soft, add the tomato paste and fry 3 minutes until dark red, then stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes.
Add this roux to the broth with the potatoes, carrots, cabbage and tomatoes and simmer 30 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the soup is thick.
Season with salt, sugar and pepper and serve hot with buttered bread; this Russian-inspired version uses tomato, not beetroot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Osmanthus Lotus Root with Sticky Rice (Guihua Tang Ou)

ingredients: 2 sections fresh lotus root (lianou), about 800 g, peeled
100 g brown sugar or rock sugar
steps: Cut a 2 cm cap from the end of each lotus root and pack the drained rice into the holes, tapping with a chopstick until full.
Secure the caps back on with toothpicks.
Simmer the roots with sugar, red dates and water over low heat for 2–2.5 hours until the root turns rosy pink and the rice is cooked.
Cool, slice into rounds, and drizzle with reduced cooking syrup and osmanthus syrup; serve warm or cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Fermented Rice Soup with Rice Balls (Jiuniang Yuanzi)

ingredients: 200 g sweet fermented rice (jiuniang/laozao), bought ready-made
steps: Mix the rice flour and warm water into a smooth dough, roll into marble-sized balls.
Bring the water and sugar to a boil, add the rice balls and cook 3–4 minutes until they float and are soft.
Stir in the jiuniang and bring just back to a boil.
Ladle into bowls and drizzle with osmanthus syrup; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: West Lake Fish in Vinegar (Xihu Cuyu)

ingredients: 1 grass carp (caoyu), about 800 g, scaled and gutted
3 slices ginger, plus 1 tbsp finely chopped ginger
2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 4 tbsp water
300 ml water from poaching the fish
steps: Split the fish lengthways from the back into two connected halves and make a few shallow cuts on the thicker side so it cooks evenly.

Bring a wide pan of water to a boil with the ginger slices, scallions and Shaoxing wine, slide in the fish skin-side up, cover and poach at a bare simmer for 3-4 minutes until the flesh at the thickest point turns opaque and flakes.
Lift the fish carefully onto a warm platter and drain off any water; reserve 300 ml of the poaching liquid.
Simmer the reserved liquid with the soy sauce, sugar, vinegar and chopped ginger for 1 minute, then stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until glossy and lightly thickened.
Pour the sweet-sour sauce over the whole fish and serve at once with steamed rice; sea bass or tilapia work if grass carp is not available.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g skin-on pork belly, in one even slab
steps: Blanch the pork belly in boiling water for 5 minutes, rinse, scrape the skin clean and cut into 5 cm squares; tie each square with kitchen string so it holds its shape.
Line a heavy clay pot or casserole with the scallions and ginger and pack the pork in skin-side down.
Add the Shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, rock sugar and water, bring to a boil, then cover tightly and simmer on the lowest heat for 2 hours, turning the pieces skin-side up halfway.
Transfer the pork to small bowls skin-side up, spoon over the sauce and steam for 30 minutes until the fat is wobbly and the skin is meltingly soft.
Serve one square per person with steamed rice or plain steamed buns.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g fresh river shrimp or small prawns, peeled
1 tsp Longjing (Dragon Well) green tea leaves
80 ml boiling water, cooled to 80 C
steps: Rinse the shrimp, pat very dry and toss with the salt, egg white and cornstarch; chill for 15 minutes.
Steep the Longjing leaves in the 80 C water for 1 minute, then strain, keeping both the leaves and the tea.
Heat the oil over medium heat and slide in the shrimp, stirring gently for about 1 minute until they turn pink and white all through; drain off the excess oil.
Add the tea leaves, 2 tbsp of the tea and the Shaoxing wine, toss for 20 seconds over high heat and serve immediately; any good Chinese green tea can stand in for Longjing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
50 g Sichuan or Zhejiang preserved mustard greens (zhacai), diced
2 dried lotus leaves, soaked until pliable
1.5 kg salt-free flour dough (1 kg flour + about 550 ml water), or clay as traditionally used
steps: Rub the chicken inside and out with the wine, soy sauces and five-spice and marinate for 30 minutes.
Stir-fry the pork belly, mushrooms and preserved greens for 3 minutes until fragrant, then stuff them into the chicken cavity.
Wrap the chicken tightly in the lotus leaves, then in a layer of baking paper, and encase completely in the rolled-out dough, sealing all seams.
Bake at 220 C for 30 minutes, then lower to 180 C and bake for 2.5 hours more.
Crack open the crust at the table, unwrap the leaves and check the thigh juices run clear before serving with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Steamed Pork in Lotus Leaf (Heye Fenzheng Rou)

ingredients: 600 g skin-on pork belly, cut into 5 x 8 cm slices 1 cm thick
2 dried lotus leaves, soaked and cut into squares
steps: Marinate the pork slices with the soy sauces, wine, sweet bean sauce and sugar for 30 minutes.
Dry-toast the rice with the star anise in a wok over low heat for about 10 minutes until golden, then grind coarsely to make rice powder.
Coat each pork slice in the rice powder, wrap it in a square of lotus leaf and arrange the parcels in a steamer.
Steam over boiling water for 2 hours, topping up the water as needed, until the pork is very tender.
Serve the parcels unopened so each diner unwraps the fragrant leaf at the table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Braised Pork with Preserved Mustard (Meigan Cai Men Rou)

ingredients: 600 g skin-on pork belly, one piece
100 g meigan cai (dried preserved mustard greens), soaked 20 minutes and chopped
steps: Simmer the pork in water with the ginger for 20 minutes, then rub the skin with dark soy and pan-fry skin-side down in the oil until blistered and brown.
Cool slightly, slice into 1 cm thick slices and arrange skin-side down in a deep bowl.
Stir-fry the drained meigan cai with the sugar, light soy and wine for 3 minutes and pile it on top of the pork.
Steam the bowl over boiling water for 90 minutes until the pork is soft enough to cut with chopsticks.
Invert onto a plate so the pork sits on the greens and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 sheets dried tofu skin (doufu pi), about 20 cm square
sweet bean sauce and scallion strips, to serve
steps: Mix the pork with soy sauce, wine, salt, ginger and scallion and stir in one direction until sticky.
Lay out a tofu skin, spread a thin layer of filling along one edge, roll it up tightly and seal the end with egg yolk; cut each roll into 4 cm pieces.
Heat the oil to 170 C and fry the rolls in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden, crisp and the pork inside is fully cooked.
Drain and serve hot with sweet bean sauce and scallion strips for dipping.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g Jinhua ham (dry-cured ham), in one piece
200 g honey dates or lotus seeds (optional, for honey-glazed version)
steps: Scrub the ham skin, soak the piece in warm water for 2 hours if very salty, then simmer for 20 minutes and drain.
Slice thinly, arrange the slices in a heatproof bowl with the ginger and scallion, and sprinkle with rock sugar and Shaoxing wine.
Steam over boiling water for 40 minutes until the ham is soft and the sugar has formed a light syrup.
Serve the slices with the syrup alongside steamed lotus-leaf buns; prosciutto or Smithfield ham is the closest substitute.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g fresh spring bamboo shoots (chunsun), peeled
steps: Cut the shoots into 5 cm wedges and blanch for 3 minutes in boiling water to remove bitterness; drain well.
Heat the oil over medium-high heat and fry the shoots for 3 minutes until the edges turn light golden.
Add both soy sauces, the sugar and water, cover and braise on low heat for 6-8 minutes.
Uncover, raise the heat and reduce until the sauce glazes the shoots, then finish with sesame oil; vacuum-packed winter shoots can replace fresh spring ones.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Song Sao Fish Soup (Song Sao Yu Geng)

ingredients: 400 g mandarin fish or sea bass fillet
4 slices ginger, plus 1 tsp ginger strips
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and shredded
3 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 5 tbsp water
steps: Steam the fish with the ginger slices and 1 tbsp wine for 8 minutes until it flakes, then remove skin and bones and break the flesh into small flakes.
Bring the stock to a boil with the ham, mushrooms and bamboo shoots and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the fish, soy sauce and remaining wine, then stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer until the soup thickens.
Drizzle in the egg yolks in a thin stream, stir once so they set in golden threads, add the vinegar and ginger strips and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: West Lake Water Shield Soup (Xihu Chuncai Tang)

ingredients: 30 g cooked Jinhua ham, finely shredded
steps: Coat the chicken shreds with the egg white and cornstarch, then poach in simmering water for 1 minute until white and drain.
Blanch the water shield in boiling water for 30 seconds and divide it among serving bowls.
Bring the stock to a boil, season with salt and add the chicken shreds.
Ladle the hot stock over the water shield and top with the ham shreds; there is no real substitute, so look for jarred chuncai in Chinese supermarkets.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Yellow Croaker with Pickled Greens (Xuecai Dahuangyu)

ingredients: 100 g xuecai (pickled potherb mustard), rinsed and chopped
steps: Score the fish on both sides and pat dry.
Heat the lard in a wok and fry the fish with the ginger over medium-high heat for 2 minutes per side until lightly golden.
Splash in the wine, pour in the boiling water and boil hard for 8 minutes until the broth turns milky white.
Add the xuecai and bamboo shoots and simmer for 5 minutes more until the fish is cooked through at the bone.
Season with salt and white pepper and serve in a deep bowl; croaker can be replaced by sea bream.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g eel or white fish fillet (such as pike conger or cod), cut in strips
steps: Toss the fish strips with salt, wine and pepper and knead until sticky, then work in the starch so each strip is coated.
Bring the stock to a gentle boil and drop in the strips one by one; simmer for 4-5 minutes until they float and are opaque all through.
Add the vinegar and adjust salt to taste.
Ladle into bowls and finish with scallion and a few drops of sesame oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Heat the lard in a wok and stir-fry the pork over high heat for 1 minute until it changes colour.
Add the bamboo shoots and xuecai and stir-fry for 2 minutes more.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce and boil for 3 minutes; season with salt.
Cook the noodles separately in boiling water until just tender, divide among bowls and ladle the pork, pickle and bamboo soup over the top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
1 handful pea shoots or bok choy
steps: Mix the flour, water and salt into a firm dough, rest 20 minutes, then roll into thin ropes and pinch off pea-sized pieces.
Press each piece with your thumb and push it forward so it curls into a small cat-ear shape.
Bring the stock to a boil with the mushrooms, chicken and ham and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the cat ears and shrimp and cook for 4-5 minutes until the pasta floats and is tender and the shrimp are pink.
Add the greens for the last minute, season with salt and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g pork belly, cut into 8 chunks
24 dried bamboo leaves (zongye), soaked and blanched
steps: Marinate the pork overnight with half the light soy, the wine, sugar and salt.
Drain the rice and mix with the remaining light soy and the dark soy until evenly brown.
Overlap two bamboo leaves, fold into a cone, add a spoon of rice, a piece of pork and more rice, fold the leaves over into a rectangular pillow and tie tightly with string.
Submerge the zongzi in a large pot of water and boil for 3 hours, topping up with boiling water so they stay covered.
Unwrap and serve warm; they keep refrigerated for 3 days and reheat by steaming.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
400 ml hot pork or chicken broth
steps: Drain the rice, spread on a cloth in a steamer and steam over high heat for 30 minutes until translucent and tender.
Fry the pork in the lard for 5 minutes until browned, add the mushrooms, soy sauces and 100 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes into a rich meat sauce.
Scoop the sticky rice into bowls, spoon over the pork sauce and scatter with crushed youtiao and scallions.
Serve with a bowl of hot broth on the side, as Wenzhou breakfast stalls do.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 pieces ready-made stinky tofu (chou doufu), bought from a Chinese grocer
steps: Rinse the stinky tofu briefly and pat dry; traditional Shaoxing tofu is brined in a fermented vegetable liquor, which gives the famous aroma.
Heat the oil to 180 C and fry the tofu in batches for 4-5 minutes until puffed, deep golden and crisp.
Mix the chilli sauce, sweet bean sauce and water as a dip.
Drain the tofu, skewer or plate it and serve hot brushed with the sauce; firm tofu soaked in brine for a day is a mild substitute.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 80 g meigan cai (dried preserved mustard), soaked and finely chopped
120 g pork fat or fatty pork belly, finely diced
1 tbsp water mixed with 1 tsp sugar, for brushing
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and warm water into a soft dough and rest for 40 minutes.
Mix the meigan cai, pork fat, sugar and salt as the filling.
Divide the dough into 8, flatten each, fill with a spoon of filling, seal and roll into a thin round.
Brush with the sugar water and press the tops into sesame seeds.
Bake on a tray at 220 C for 12-15 minutes until puffed and golden, with the pork fat fully rendered; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp sweet osmanthus syrup (guihua jiang), optional
steps: Grind the toasted sesame finely, mix with the sugar and lard into a paste and chill for 20 minutes, then roll into 20 small balls.
Knead the rice flour with the warm water into a smooth dough like play-dough.
Pinch off a piece, flatten into a cup, enclose a sesame ball and roll smooth.
Drop into boiling water and simmer for 5-6 minutes until they float and then 1 minute more.
Serve in their cooking water with a drizzle of osmanthus syrup; butter can replace lard.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: West Lake Lotus Root Starch Soup (Xihu Oufen)

ingredients: 40 g West Lake lotus root starch (oufen)
steps: Stir the lotus root starch and sugar with the cold water in a heatproof bowl until smooth.
Pour in the boiling water in a steady stream, stirring hard all the time until it turns clear, glossy and thick like a jelly.
If it stays cloudy, microwave for 30 seconds and stir again.
Top with osmanthus syrup, walnuts and raisins and eat warm; arrowroot is the best substitute.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 bottle Shaoxing huangjiu (aged rice wine, e.g. Huadiao), bought from a licensed producer
2 dried plums (huamei) or 1 tbsp rock sugar, optional
steps: Shaoxing wine is an amber rice wine brewed from glutinous rice and wheat qu in Shaoxing, aged for years in clay jars; buy it from licensed producers and do not brew it at home.
To serve in the local style, pour into a small kettle or jug and warm in a water bath to about 40 C, optionally with a dried plum or ginger slice.
Pour into small cups and sip with salted broad beans (huixiang dou) or drunken chicken; drink responsibly and only if of legal age.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g pork knuckle, chopped and blanched
1 chicken (about 1.2 kg), cut into pieces and blanched
200 g fish maw or sea cucumber, rehydrated
100 g bamboo shoots and 8 slices ham
steps: Soak the dried scallops, mushrooms and fish maw overnight in cold water, changing the water once.
Fry the ginger and spring onions briefly, then layer the chicken, pork knuckle, ham, bamboo shoots, mushrooms and scallops in a large ceramic jar or casserole.
Add the stock and Shaoxing wine, cover tightly (traditionally sealed with a lotus leaf), and simmer or steam on very low heat for 3 hours.
Add the abalone, fish maw and quail eggs and cook a further 45 minutes until every ingredient is meltingly tender and the soup is rich.
Skim the fat, check for salt, and serve straight from the jar in small bowls.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g eel or Spanish mackerel fillet, skinned
200 g minced pork with some fat
1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil
1 tbsp chopped Chinese celery and a little white pepper
steps: Scrape and chop the fish into a fine paste, add salt, and beat by hand for 10 minutes, adding ice water and starch gradually, until bouncy.
Season the minced pork with soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil and roll into small marbles for the filling.
Wrap each pork ball in a spoonful of fish paste, squeezing out through your fist into cold water.
Bring the water slowly to a gentle simmer and cook 8 to 10 minutes until the balls float and the pork filling is cooked through.
Serve in hot broth with celery and white pepper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g pork tenderloin, cut into 2 cm thick slices
100 g water chestnuts, peeled and halved
3 tbsp red yeast rice wine lees (hongzao) or 1 tbsp ketchup for colour
3 tbsp Zhenjiang or white rice vinegar
steps: Score each pork slice in a fine crosshatch on one side, cut into 4 cm pieces, and marinate in soy sauce and egg white for 10 minutes.
Wrap each piece around half a water chestnut, scored side out, and coat in potato starch.
Deep-fry at 180°C for 3 to 4 minutes until the pieces curl into lychee shapes and are cooked through, then fry again for 30 seconds to crisp.
Stir the garlic, red lees, vinegar, sugar and 4 tbsp water in a wok until bubbling and thickened with a little starch slurry.
Toss the pork in the sweet-sour sauce and serve immediately with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g old ginger, sliced (preferably a pungent mature variety)
steps: Heat the sesame oil in a clay pot on medium-low heat and fry the ginger 8 to 10 minutes until edges curl and turn golden.
Add the duck and stir-fry on high heat 8 minutes until the skin renders and browns.
Pour in the wine, water, soy sauce, rock sugar and angelica, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 50 to 60 minutes until the duck is tender and the sauce reduced and glossy.
Serve hot from the clay pot with rice, traditionally as a warming winter dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg chicken pieces on the bone
4 tbsp red yeast rice wine lees (hongzao); substitute 2 tbsp red fermented bean curd plus 1 tbsp red yeast rice powder
steps: Fry the ginger and garlic in the oil on medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the red lees and fry 1 minute until the oil turns red and aromatic.
Add the chicken and stir-fry on high heat for 5 minutes until coated and lightly browned.
Pour in the wine, soy sauce, sugar and water, cover, and simmer 25 to 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce clings.
Serve hot with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g pork spare ribs, cut into 5 cm pieces
1 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
2 tbsp red yeast rice wine lees (hongzao) or ketchup
2 tbsp Shaoxing wine for the sauce
steps: Marinate the ribs in soy sauce, wine and egg for 20 minutes, then coat with potato starch.
Deep-fry at 170°C for 6 minutes until cooked through, then raise to 190°C and fry 1 minute until crisp.
Fry the garlic in a little oil, add the sugar, vinegar, red lees, wine and 3 tbsp water, and simmer until syrupy.
Toss the ribs quickly in the sauce until glazed and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g small fresh oysters, rinsed and drained
3 tbsp sweet chili sauce or tomato chili sauce for dipping
steps: Mix the oysters, sweet potato starch, water, spring onions and fish sauce into a loose batter.
Heat the lard in a flat pan over high heat, pour in the batter, and spread into a thin round.
Fry 2 to 3 minutes until crisp and golden underneath, pour the eggs over, and flip once the egg begins to set.
Fry another 2 minutes until the oysters are cooked through and the edges are crisp, then serve with the dipping sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g fresh sea worms (tusun, a peanut worm from the Fujian coast), cleaned
3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp minced garlic, 1 tbsp wasabi or chili sauce for dipping
steps: Squeeze the worms gently to clean out sand and rinse in several changes of water.
Boil with the ginger, wine and salt in the water, then simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until the liquid becomes gelatinous.
Divide the worms between small cups and pour the cooking liquid over.
Cool, then refrigerate at least 4 hours until set into firm jelly.
Unmould and serve cold with the dipping sauce, carrot and coriander.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 popiah skins (thin wheat crepes); buy fresh from Asian grocers
500 g jicama (yam bean), shredded; substitute cabbage
2 blocks firm tofu, cut into strips and fried
2 eggs, made into a thin omelette and shredded
50 g crushed peanuts mixed with 1 tbsp sugar
3 tbsp sweet bean sauce and 1 tbsp chili paste
2 tbsp vegetable oil and 2 cloves garlic, minced
steps: Fry the garlic and pork in oil until the pork is cooked, add the prawns and cook 2 minutes until pink.
Add the jicama and carrot and braise with 100 ml water on low heat for 30 minutes until soft and juicy, then drain off excess liquid.
Lay out a popiah skin, spread with sweet sauce and a little chili, and add lettuce, the filling, tofu, egg and peanut sugar.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly, then cut in half and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g lean pork, pounded to a paste
40 wonton wrappers, preferably very thin rouyan wrappers
1 tbsp fried garlic with its oil
1 tsp sesame oil and white pepper
steps: Beat the pork paste with salt, sugar and ice water until sticky and springy.
Place a small dab of filling on each wrapper corner and scrunch the wrapper loosely closed like a little flower.
Boil the wontons in plenty of water for 2 to 3 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Ladle into bowls of hot broth and finish with fried garlic, spring onion, sesame oil and pepper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g lean pork for filling, minced
30 rouyan skins (thin sheets made from pounded pork and sweet potato starch); substitute thin wonton wrappers
2 tbsp chopped spring onion and celery
steps: Mix the pork, prawns, water chestnuts, soy sauce and sesame oil into a filling.
Wrap a teaspoon of filling in each rouyan skin and pinch the top together into a swallow-tail shape.
Steam on oiled paper over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the filling is firm and cooked through.
Serve in hot broth with spring onion and celery.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g roast pork or char siu, diced
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and diced
1 tbsp dried scallops, soaked and shredded
400 ml chicken stock thickened with 2 tbsp cornstarch
1 tbsp oyster sauce and 1 tbsp light soy sauce
steps: Stir-fry the rice with the eggs in 2 tbsp oil over high heat for 4 minutes until dry and fluffy, then plate as a mound.
Fry the mushrooms and scallops in the remaining oil, add the chicken and prawns, and cook 3 minutes until cooked through.
Add the pork, bok choy, stock, oyster sauce and soy sauce, and simmer 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and turns glossy.
Pour the rich gravy over the fried rice and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g Fujian mian xian (thin wheat vermicelli)
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
2 tbsp red yeast rice wine or Shaoxing wine
steps: Fry the ginger in sesame oil on medium heat for 3 minutes, add the pork and mushrooms, and stir-fry until the pork is cooked.
Add the stock and wine and simmer 5 minutes.
Poach the eggs in the broth for 4 minutes until the whites set.
Boil the noodles in separate water for 1 to 2 minutes, drain and add to bowls, ladling over the broth, pork and egg; garnish with spring onion, traditionally for birthdays.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g pork liver or lean pork, sliced
4 tofu puffs and 50 g bean sprouts
1 tsp sugar and 1 tbsp fish sauce
steps: Simmer the stock with shacha sauce, peanut butter, sugar and fish sauce for 10 minutes until rich and orange.
Blanch the noodles and bean sprouts in boiling water for 1 minute and divide between bowls.
Cook the pork, squid, prawns and tofu puffs in the shacha broth for 2 to 3 minutes until just cooked through.
Ladle the toppings and broth over the noodles and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g mian xian (thin wheat vermicelli), broken into short lengths
1.2 litres pork bone or seafood stock
50 g dried oysters or fresh oysters
100 g pork intestine or pork, cooked and sliced
3 tbsp sweet potato starch mixed with 6 tbsp water
2 tbsp fried shallots, white pepper, vinegar
steps: Simmer the stock with the dried shrimp and oysters for 10 minutes.
Add the noodles and cook 3 minutes until soft.
Stir in the starch slurry and fish sauce and simmer until the broth turns into a thick paste.
Serve topped with pork, youtiao, fried shallots, pepper and a dash of vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g Putian thick wheat noodles or fresh yellow noodles
4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
2 tbsp lard or oil and 3 shallots, sliced
steps: Fry the shallots in lard until golden, add the pork and mushrooms, and stir-fry until the pork is cooked.
Add the seafood and cabbage and stir-fry 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce, bring to a boil, and add the noodles.
Cover and braise on medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the noodles absorb most of the broth and the seafood is fully cooked, then serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g Xinghua (Putian) fine rice vermicelli, soaked 10 minutes
steps: Fry the pork and mushrooms in lard until the pork is cooked, then add the prawns and cabbage and stir 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce and bring to a boil.
Add the drained vermicelli and toss with chopsticks over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the noodles absorb the liquid and become fluffy.
Scatter with peanuts and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp sweet potato starch mixed with 5 tbsp water
2 tbsp fried shallots and 1 tbsp black vinegar
steps: Bring the stock to a boil, add the pork and seafood, and simmer 3 minutes until cooked through.
Season with soy sauce, stir in the starch slurry, and simmer until thickened.
Drizzle in the beaten egg while stirring to form ribbons.
Blanch the noodles for 1 minute, place in bowls, and ladle the thick lu gravy over; finish with fried shallots and vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp smooth peanut butter or sesame paste
steps: Stir the peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and hot water into a smooth pourable sauce.
Boil the noodles for 2 to 3 minutes until just tender, then drain well.
Toss the hot noodles thoroughly in the peanut sauce and top with spring onion.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Grind the soaked rice with the water into a thin smooth batter.
Bring the stock to a rolling boil in a wide wok with the dried shrimp, clams, pork and cabbage, until the clams open and pork is cooked.
Lower the boil slightly and pour the batter in a thin ring around the hot wok sides above the liquid, cover, and cook 1 to 2 minutes until the batter sets into sheets.
Scrape the sheets into the soup, season with fish sauce, and serve with youtiao, shallots and celery.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g minced pork, seasoned with soy sauce and five-spice (optional filling)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, soda and water into a soft dough, knead 8 minutes, and prove 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 12 pieces, flatten, and place a little seasoned pork in the middle if using, then pinch closed and press flat.
Poke a hole through the centre of each, sprinkle with sesame, and rest 15 minutes.
Bake at 220°C for 15 to 20 minutes, or on the walls of a clay oven, until golden and crisp and the pork is cooked through.
Thread onto string and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g raw peeled peanuts, soaked overnight
steps: Drain the soaked peanuts, toss with the baking soda, rinse, and slip off any remaining red skins.
Bring to a boil in fresh water, then simmer covered on the lowest heat for 2 hours until the peanuts melt in the mouth.
Add the rock sugar and stir until dissolved.
Serve hot or cold, with youtiao for dipping.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 gaiwan or small teapot and small cups
steps: Warm the gaiwan and cups with boiling water and discard.
Add the tightly rolled leaves, pour over boiling water, and discard after 5 seconds to rinse.
Infuse for 20 to 30 seconds with water just off the boil, then pour off into cups.
Re-infuse 5 to 7 times, lengthening the steep slightly each time, enjoying the orchid fragrance.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g skin-on pork belly, cut into 3 cm cubes
steps: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 3 minutes, drain, and pat dry.
Stir-fry the pork in a dry wok on medium heat for 6 minutes until some fat renders and the edges turn golden, then remove.
Melt the rock sugar in the oil on low heat, stirring until it turns a deep amber caramel, return the pork and toss to coat.
Add the ginger, chilies, spices, wine, soy sauce and hot water, cover, and simmer on low for 60 to 75 minutes until the pork is meltingly tender.
Uncover and reduce on high heat, stirring, until the sauce becomes a sticky glossy glaze, then serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Steamed Fish Head with Chopped Chili (Duojiao Yutou)

ingredients: 1 large bighead carp head (about 1.2 kg), split in half and cleaned; substitute salmon head
steps: Rub the fish head with the salt and wine and leave 10 minutes, then lay it cut side up on a deep plate.
Mix the chopped chili with the ginger and half the garlic and spread thickly over the fish.
Steam over high heat for 12 to 15 minutes until the flesh behind the gills is opaque and comes away easily.
Scatter the remaining garlic and spring onions, pour over smoking hot oil to sizzle, and drizzle with soy sauce.
Serve with rice or noodles to mop up the juices.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g pork belly or pork shoulder with some fat, thinly sliced
200 g green Hangzhou or long green peppers, sliced diagonally
steps: Dry-fry the green peppers in a hot wok with a pinch of salt for 3 minutes until blistered, then remove.
Heat the oil and fry the pork on medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the fat renders, the edges curl and it is cooked through.
Add the garlic, chilies and fermented black beans and stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the peppers, add both soy sauces, and toss on high heat for 1 minute, then serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 dried red chilies, cut into pieces
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Simmer the whole chicken in water to cover for 10 minutes, turn off the heat, and leave covered 20 minutes until cooked through (juices run clear); reserve 100 ml stock.
Cool, debone, and cut the meat into finger-sized strips.
Fry the ginger, chilies and peppercorns in the oil on medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken, wine, vinegar, salt and reserved stock and toss on high heat for 2 minutes.
Thicken with the starch slurry, add spring onions, and serve hot with its tangy sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Steamed Smoked Meats (La Wei He Zheng)

ingredients: 150 g smoked chicken or smoked fish
2 tbsp chopped dried chili or chili flakes
steps: Soak the smoked meats in warm water for 20 minutes, scrub, then simmer 10 minutes to remove excess salt.
Slice thinly and arrange the meats overlapping in a heatproof bowl.
Scatter the black beans, chili, wine and sugar over.
Steam over high heat for 30 to 40 minutes until the fat turns translucent and the meats are soft and hot through.
Turn out onto a plate, garnish with spring onions, and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 duck (about 1.5 kg), chopped into small pieces
150 ml fresh duck blood, mixed with 1 tsp vinegar to stop clotting; substitute duck or pork blood tofu, crumbled
steps: Stir-fry the duck pieces in a hot dry wok for 5 minutes to render fat, then add the oil, ginger and garlic and fry 5 minutes until browned.
Add the wine, soy sauce, salt and 300 ml water, cover, and simmer 25 minutes until the duck is tender.
Add the chilies and cook uncovered on high heat until the liquid is almost gone.
Pour in the blood while stirring constantly over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until it coats every piece and turns dark and fully cooked.
Serve hot with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg live crayfish, scrubbed and cleaned with veins removed
1 head garlic, smashed and 30 g ginger, sliced
4 star anise, 2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick
1 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp light soy sauce
3 spring onions and a handful of perilla (zisu) leaves
steps: Blanch the crayfish in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
Fry the garlic, ginger, spices, chilies and peppercorns in the oil on medium heat for 2 minutes, then add the chili bean paste and fry until the oil turns red.
Add the crayfish and stir-fry on high heat 3 minutes.
Pour in the beer, soy sauce and sugar, cover, and simmer 10 to 12 minutes until the shells are bright red and the tail meat is opaque throughout.
Toss in the perilla and spring onions, reduce the sauce on high heat for 2 minutes, and serve as a late-night snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g loose-headed cauliflower, broken into small florets
8 dried red chilies, cut into segments
steps: Blanch the cauliflower in salted boiling water for 1 minute and drain well.
Fry the pork belly in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes until browned and the fat has rendered.
Add the garlic, chilies and chili bean paste and stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the cauliflower, soy sauce and sugar and stir-fry on high heat 4 to 5 minutes until charred at the edges and tender-crisp.
Transfer to a small dry pot over a burner, add spring onions, and serve sizzling.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg skin-on pork belly, cut into long strips 5 cm wide
200 g wood chips (cypress or tea wood) and 50 g rice, for smoking
steps: Toast the salt with the peppercorns until fragrant, cool, and rub with the wine and sugar all over the pork.
Cure in the refrigerator for 3 to 5 days in a covered dish, turning daily.
Rinse, pat dry, and hang in a cool airy place for 1 to 2 days until the surface is dry.
Hot-smoke over wood chips and rice in a covered smoker or foil-lined wok, at about 90°C, for 3 to 4 hours until deep brown and the internal temperature reaches 63°C.
Store in the fridge; before eating, soak, simmer 20 minutes, slice and stir-fry with garlic leaves and chilies or steam.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g fresh round rice noodles (Changde mifen); substitute thick dried round rice noodles, soaked
200 g beef or pork, braised in soy sauce and spices until tender, sliced
1 tbsp pickled mustard greens or sour beans
steps: Bring the broth to a boil and season with the braising liquid and lard.
Blanch the rice noodles in boiling water for 1 minute until heated through and soft.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle over the hot broth, and top with the braised meat.
Finish with pickles, chili oil and spring onions and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g lean pork, sliced and marinated in 1 tsp soy sauce and 1 tsp cornstarch
2 tbsp pickled long beans (suan doujiao) or pickled radish
steps: Stir-fry the pork in a little oil for 2 minutes until cooked through, splash with soy sauce, and set aside as the topping (matou).
Put lard and soy sauce into each bowl and pour over the boiling broth.
Blanch the noodles for 30 seconds in boiling water and add to the bowls.
Top with the pork, pickles, chili oil and spring onions.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 pieces black Changsha fermented stinky tofu (bought ready-brined from Asian grocers); substitute firm tofu soaked in fermented bean curd brine
2 tbsp warm water or vegetable stock
2 tbsp chopped coriander and spring onion
steps: Pat the tofu dry with paper towels.
Deep-fry at 180°C for 4 to 5 minutes until puffed and crisp, then drain.
Mix the garlic, chili oil, soy sauce and water into a sauce.
Poke a hole in the centre of each piece with a chopstick, spoon in the sauce, and top with coriander, spring onion and pickled radish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the glutinous rice flour with the warm water into a soft smooth dough and shape into 16 small flattened discs.
Fry the discs in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until lightly golden.
Add the brown sugar and water, and cook on low heat 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until the syrup thickens and coats the cakes, which become soft and chewy.
Sprinkle with sesame and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Lotus Seeds in Rock Sugar (Bingtang Xianglian)

steps: Soak the lotus seeds in warm water with the baking soda for 10 minutes, rinse well, and remove any remaining green cores.
Steam the lotus seeds in a bowl with a little water over high heat for 40 minutes until soft and creamy.
Boil the water with rock sugar and red dates until the sugar dissolves.
Add the lotus seeds, pineapple and goji berries and simmer 5 minutes, then serve warm or chilled.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg fresh red chilies, washed and completely dried
50 ml Chinese baijiu or vodka (for the jar, optional)
steps: Remove the stems and chop the chilies finely with a cleaver (keep everything dry so the ferment stays clean).
Mix with the salt, ginger, garlic and sugar.
Pack tightly into a sterilised jar, drizzle a little spirit on top, and seal, leaving 3 cm headspace.
Ferment at cool room temperature for 7 days until pleasantly sour, then refrigerate and use for steamed fish heads, stir-fries and dips.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 fresh mandarin fish (guiyu), about 800 g, scaled and gutted (sub: sea bass)
1 tbsp minced ginger and 3 cloves garlic, sliced
2 fresh red chillies, sliced, and 2 scallions, chopped
steps: Traditional cure: rub the fish lightly with salt, place in a clean covered container, press with a weight and refrigerate at 4°C for 3 days, turning daily, until the flesh is firm and has a mild pungent aroma (in Huizhou this is done in a cool wooden barrel); discard if slimy or sour-smelling.
Rinse and pat dry, score both sides, and pan-fry in hot oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Push the fish aside, fry the pork, ginger, garlic and bamboo shoots for 2 minutes, then add wine, soy, sugar and 300 ml water.

Braise covered over low heat for 15 minutes, basting, until the fish is cooked through to the bone and the sauce is reduced; scatter chillies and scallion and serve with rice; the flesh separates into firm garlic-clove flakes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g Chinese yam (shanyao), peeled and cut into chunks
50 g Jinhua ham or Huizhou cured ham, sliced
steps: Blanch the pigeons for 3 minutes and rinse.
Place in a clay pot with ham, mushrooms, ginger, scallion, wine, rock sugar and water, bring to a boil and skim.
Cover and simmer over very low heat for 1.5 hours.
Add the yam and simmer 20–30 minutes until the pigeon is very tender and the yam soft, season with salt, and serve in the pot as a nourishing Huizhou dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g squid, scored and cut into pieces
150 g fish maw or fish balls
1.5 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp white pepper
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
steps: Blanch the sea cucumber, squid and fish maw separately for 1 minute each and drain.
Bring the stock to a boil with the wine, mushrooms, bamboo shoots, ham and chicken and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the tofu, sea cucumber and fish maw and simmer 10 minutes, then add squid for the final 2 minutes until opaque and just cooked.
Season with salt and pepper, thicken lightly with the slurry, and serve in a large pot at the table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 star anise and 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns
200 g dried rice noodles or vermicelli, to serve
steps: Blanch the goose for 5 minutes, then rinse.
Put it in a large pot with the ginger, scallions, spices, wine, salt and water to cover, bring to a boil and skim.
Simmer over low heat for 3 hours until the goose is very tender and the broth is rich and clear.
Chop the goose into pieces and serve in bowls of the broth with soaked rice noodles, in the style of Hefei's Wushan town.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp honey or maltose mixed with 2 tbsp water
spice bag: 2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, 1 black cardamom (caoguo), 3 slices dried galangal, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp fennel seed
steps: Tuck the wings and legs to make a compact bird, brush with honey water and let dry 20 minutes.
Fry at 170°C for 4–5 minutes, turning, until evenly reddish-brown.

Simmer in a pot with soy sauces, salt, rock sugar, spice bag, ginger, scallions and water to cover over very low heat for 2 hours until the meat is extremely tender and the internal temperature exceeds 74°C.
Lift out carefully and serve warm or cool; the meat should fall from the bone with a shake, as in Fuliji, Suzhou (Anhui).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g hairy tofu (mao doufu), bought ready-fermented (sub: firm tofu, though the texture and flavour will differ)
steps: Hairy tofu is fermented with a white mould until fluffy; gently flatten the fuzz and cut into 4 cm pieces.
Pan-fry over medium heat in the oil for 3–4 minutes per side until both sides are golden and crisp.
Push to the side, fry the garlic and ginger, then add soy, sugar, chilli sauce and water.
Braise 3–4 minutes until the sauce reduces, sprinkle with scallion and serve hot in the Huizhou way, with extra chilli sauce for dipping.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Wenzheng Mountain Bamboo Shoots with Ham

ingredients: 500 g fresh spring bamboo shoots (Wenzheng shan dongsun), peeled (sub: canned bamboo shoots)
100 g Huizhou or Jinhua ham, sliced
steps: Cut the bamboo shoots into chunks and blanch for 5 minutes to remove bitterness.
Render the pork fat in a clay pot, add ginger, ham and mushrooms and fry 2 minutes.
Add the bamboo shoots, wine, rock sugar and stock, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes until the shoots are tender and full of flavour.
Taste before adding salt, since the ham is salty, and serve in the pot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg beef bones and 500 g beef shank
200 g beef tripe, cleaned and cooked
3 tbsp beef tallow (niuyou) or vegetable oil
spice bag: 3 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 black cardamom, 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp fennel seed
steps: Blanch the bones and shank, then simmer with ginger and the spice bag in 3 l water for 2.5 hours; remove the shank once tender, cool and slice thinly.
Heat the tallow, add chilli flakes off the heat to make a red spiced oil, and stir it into the broth with salt.
Blanch the vermicelli and tofu skin briefly in the boiling broth.
Fill bowls with vermicelli, tofu skin, sliced beef and tripe, ladle over the hot red broth and top with coriander; eat with sesame flatbread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g dried preserved mustard greens (meigancai), soaked and finely chopped
2 tbsp malt syrup mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Mix flour, salt and water into a soft dough and rest 30 minutes; mix pork fat, meigancai, chilli and sugar into a filling.
Divide the dough into 10, flatten each, spread with lard, roll up and coil into a spiral, then flatten again and fill with the meigancai mixture, sealing well.
Roll each into a thin round about 8 cm across, brush with syrup water, and press into sesame seeds.
Bake at 210°C for 18–20 minutes until crisp, golden and flaky and the pork fat has rendered into the filling; these crab-shell style cakes are the classic Huangshan travel snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole duck, about 2.2 kg, neck skin intact
1 cucumber and 6 scallions, cut in thin strips
steps: Rub the cavity with the salt and five-spice, then pour boiling water over the skin to tighten it and pat dry.
Dissolve the maltose and vinegar in the 200 ml boiling water, brush the skin all over, then hang or set the duck on a rack in the fridge, uncovered, for 12 hours to dry the skin.

Roast breast-up on a rack over a tray of water at 200 C for 30 minutes, turn breast-down for 20 minutes, then breast-up again at 220 C for 15-20 minutes until the skin is lacquered deep mahogany and the thigh reaches 75 C.
Rest for 10 minutes, then carve thin slices of crisp skin and meat.
Serve with warmed pancakes, sweet bean sauce, cucumber and scallion for each diner to wrap; boil the carcass into a soup to finish the meal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg lamb leg or shoulder, frozen and sliced paper-thin
500 g napa cabbage, glass noodles and frozen tofu
steps: Fill a copper hot pot or electric pot with water, add the ginger and scallions and bring to a rolling boil.
Thin the sesame paste with water until pourable and stir in the fermented tofu, chive flower sauce and soy sauce to make each person's dipping sauce.
At the table, swish each slice of lamb in the boiling water for 10-15 seconds until it changes colour completely, then dip in the sauce and eat.
Cook the cabbage, tofu and glass noodles in the enriched broth towards the end and serve with sesame flatbreads.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Shredded Pork in Beijing Sauce (Jingjiang Rousi)

ingredients: 300 g pork tenderloin, cut into fine shreds
8 thin tofu skin sheets (doufu pi) or pancakes, to wrap
steps: Mix the pork with the wine, egg white and cornstarch and rest 10 minutes.
Heat the oil to medium and stir-fry the pork for 1-2 minutes until white and separated, then remove.
In the remaining oil fry the sweet bean sauce, sugar and soy for 1 minute until fragrant and glossy.
Return the pork and toss over high heat for 30 seconds until coated and cooked through.
Pile the pork on a bed of scallion shreds and serve with tofu skins or pancakes to wrap.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 thick Chinese leeks or large scallions (dacong), sliced diagonally
steps: Marinate the lamb with the soy sauces, wine and cornstarch for 10 minutes.
Heat the wok until smoking, add the oil and stir-fry the lamb over the highest heat for 1 minute until no longer pink.
Add the scallions and garlic and toss for 1 minute until just wilted and fragrant.
Splash in the vinegar around the side of the wok, drizzle with sesame oil and serve immediately with rice or flatbread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g lamb or beef, thinly sliced
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds and cumin (optional)
steps: Marinate the meat with soy sauce, wine, sugar, sesame oil and ginger for 20 minutes.
Heat a large griddle or cast-iron pan until very hot and lightly oil it.
Spread out the onion and scallions, put the meat on top and stir and turn with long chopsticks for 3-4 minutes until the meat is cooked through and the onions caramelised.
Toss in the coriander and sesame, and serve straight from the griddle with sesame flatbreads and garlic cloves.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g pork intestines, cleaned and blanched (optional but traditional)
300 g pork lung or extra pork belly
4 plain huoshao flatbreads or other firm flatbreads
1 spice bag: star anise, cinnamon, Sichuan pepper, bay leaf
3 cloves garlic, mashed with 2 tbsp vinegar
steps: Blanch the meats and offal for 10 minutes, rinse, then simmer in 2.5 litres water with the spice bag and soy sauce for 2 hours until tender.
Add the fried tofu for the last 20 minutes and cut a cross into each huoshao and simmer them in the broth for 3 minutes until soft.
Lift out and chop the bread, meat, offal and tofu into bite pieces and put into bowls.
Ladle over hot broth and top with fermented tofu juice, chive flower sauce and the garlic vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g fresh hand-pulled or thick wheat noodles
300 g fatty pork belly, diced 1 cm
100 g bean sprouts and 100 g soybeans, blanched
steps: Fry the pork belly in the oil over medium heat for 6-8 minutes until the fat renders and edges brown.
Mix the two pastes with the water, add to the pan, lower the heat and simmer for 12-15 minutes, stirring, until thick and oil pools on the surface.
Stir in the scallions.
Boil the noodles until tender, rinse briefly in cold water if you like them firm, and divide among bowls.
Top each with a spoonful of sauce and arrange the cucumber, sprouts and soybeans around; mix well before eating.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/2 tsp Sichuan peppercorn water or ground pepper
150 ml water, added gradually to the meat
steps: Mix the flour and warm water into a very soft dough, oil it and rest for 30 minutes.
Stir the meat with soy, salt, ginger and pepper in one direction, adding the water little by little until juicy, then fold in the scallions.
Divide the dough into 8, flatten each into a thin round, top with filling, pleat closed and press gently into a flat pie about 1.5 cm thick.
Pan-fry in oil over medium-low heat, covered, for 5 minutes per side until deep golden and the filling is fully cooked.
Serve hot with vinegar and garlic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper and salt (jiaoyan)
1 tbsp water mixed with 1 tsp sugar
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and water into a soft dough and rise for 40 minutes.
Roll into a large thin rectangle, spread with the sesame paste mixed with oil, jiaoyan and sugar.
Roll up tightly, cut into 8 pieces, twist each cut side in and flatten into a round with spiral layers.
Brush tops with sugar water, dip into sesame seeds and bake at 210 C for 15-18 minutes until puffed and golden.
Serve warm with doufu nao or with hot pot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g cleaned lamb or beef tripe (baodu ren or san ban), cut in strips
steps: Wash the tripe thoroughly and soak in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Thin the sesame paste with water and mix in the fermented tofu, chive flower sauce, soy, vinegar and chilli oil to make the dip.
Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and blanch the tripe in small batches for 8-15 seconds until it curls and turns crisp; do not overcook or it becomes rubbery.
Drain, top with scallion and coriander and serve immediately with the sesame sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g pork intestines, cleaned and blanched
6 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 150 ml water
1 tsp MSG or salt to taste
steps: Simmer the cleaned intestines in the stock with the star anise for 45 minutes until tender, then cut into short rings.
Blanch the liver slices in boiling water for 1 minute and rinse.
Add both soy sauces to the stock, return the intestines and add the liver; simmer 3 minutes until the liver is cooked through.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until thick and glossy, then add half the garlic.
Ladle into bowls, top with the remaining garlic and eat with steamed baozi for breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp neutral oil, for the dough
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, soda and salt, add the water and oil and knead into a soft dough; cover and rest for 2 hours.
Roll into a 5 mm thick strip, cut into 4 x 10 cm pieces, stack two, press a slit through the middle and form into a ring.
Fry in oil at 160 C for 5-6 minutes, turning, until very crisp and golden brown.
Drain and serve with douzhi or wrapped in a sesame flatbread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp gypsum (calcium sulphate) or 1 tsp glucono-delta-lactone (GDL)
