10 g dried wood ear and 5 dried lily buds (jinzhen), soaked
3 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 5 tbsp water
2 tbsp mashed garlic, chilli oil and sesame paste, to serve
steps: Dissolve the coagulant in 3 tbsp cold water in a pot, heat the soy milk to 90 C and pour it in from a height; cover and leave undisturbed for 15 minutes until set.
Simmer the lamb, wood ear and lily buds in the water with the soy sauces for 10 minutes until the lamb is cooked.
Thicken with the cornstarch slurry into a dark, glossy gravy (dalu).
Scoop thin slices of tofu pudding into bowls, ladle over the lamb gravy and finish with garlic, chilli oil and sesame paste.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cut the cabbage into leaves about 10 cm wide and blanch in boiling water for 30 seconds until just wilted, then drain.
Mix the mustard powder with the warm water into a paste and leave 10 minutes to develop heat.
Stir the sugar, vinegar and salt into the mustard, then layer the cabbage in a container, brushing every layer with mustard dressing.
Cover tightly and refrigerate overnight; serve cold, cut into neat blocks, as a Lunar New Year side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Wash and dry the fruit well, remove stems and thread 5-6 pieces onto each skewer.
Heat the sugar and water in a small pan over medium heat without stirring until the syrup reaches 150 C, clear and pale amber.
Tilt the pan and roll each skewer quickly through the syrup to give a thin coat.
Set on an oiled tray or dip in ice water for 10 seconds so the sugar hardens to a glassy crunch, and eat the same day.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the rice flour and water into a batter, pour into an oiled dish and steam over high heat for 25 minutes until translucent.
Dry-toast the soybean flour in a pan over low heat for 5 minutes until golden and nutty.
Dust the work surface with soybean flour, tip out the warm rice dough and roll it into a rectangle 5 mm thick.
Spread with red bean paste, roll up tightly, coat the outside with more soybean flour and cut into 3 cm slices.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp hawthorn cake or candied fruit, diced
50 g cooked glutinous rice flour, for dusting
steps: Drain the rice and steam on a cloth for 30 minutes until fully tender, then mash slightly while hot so it becomes sticky.
Mix the sesame, walnuts, sugar and candied fruit as the filling.
With hands dusted in cooked rice flour, take a piece of rice, flatten, add filling and roll into a small ball.
Make a small dent on top, roll the ball in cooked rice flour and serve at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g dried split yellow peas, soaked overnight
steps: Drain the peas, simmer in the water for 45 minutes until completely soft, then blend to a smooth puree.
Return to the pan with the sugar and stir constantly over low heat for 15 minutes until thick enough that a spatula leaves a lasting trail.
Spread into a lined container 3 cm deep, smooth the top and cool, then chill for 4 hours.
Cut into neat rectangles and serve cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g poria powder (fuling fen), from a Chinese herbalist
steps: Whisk the poria powder, rice flour, plain flour and water into a thin batter and rest 10 minutes.
Brush a non-stick pan very lightly with oil and cook spoonfuls of batter over low heat for about 1 minute into paper-thin white wafers, without browning.
Warm the honey and stir in the nuts and candied fruit to make the filling.
Sandwich a thin layer of filling between two wafers, press gently and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 litre raw douzhi (fermented mung bean starch liquid), bought from a Beijing-style shop
pickled mustard tuber shreds (jiaosi xiancai), with chilli oil
steps: Douzhi is the sour, fermented liquid left from making mung bean starch; buy it fresh, as it is not made at home in Beijing either.
Bring the water to a boil in a pot, pour in the douzhi and stir constantly over low heat until it just comes back to a simmer and foams; do not boil hard or it separates.
Pour into bowls and drink hot with pickled mustard shreds and fried dough rings on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp plain live yogurt, as starter
steps: Heat the milk with the sugar to 90 C, stirring, then cool to 43 C.
Whisk in the yogurt starter and pour into the jars.
Cover and keep warm at about 40 C (an oven with the light on) for 8 hours until set firm.
Chill, cover the jar mouth with paper and a rubber band in the old Beijing way, and drink with a straw.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rinse the dried ingredients except the osmanthus and soak in the water for 30 minutes.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 50 minutes.
Add the rock sugar and osmanthus and simmer for 10 minutes more.
Strain, cool and chill; serve icy cold with summer meals or after hot pot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 ml cold pork stock, added gradually
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and water into a soft dough and leave to rise for 30 minutes (Tianjin baozi use a half-raised dough).
Beat the pork with soy, ginger, salt and sesame oil in one direction, adding the stock a little at a time until juicy, then stir in the scallions.
Divide the dough into 24, roll thin wrappers, fill each and pleat the top into at least 18 neat folds.
Rest 15 minutes, then steam over high heat for 12-15 minutes until the dough is springy and the filling fully cooked.
Serve hot with black vinegar and garlic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the mung bean flour, plain flour and water into a thin batter and rest for 10 minutes.
Heat a large lightly oiled griddle or pan over medium heat, pour in a ladle of batter and spread thinly into a round.
Crack an egg on top, spread it over, scatter with scallions and coriander and cook until set, about 1 minute; flip.
Brush with sweet bean sauce, fermented tofu and chilli sauce, lay a youtiao in the centre and fold the crepe around it.
Serve immediately while crisp, folded in a paper bag.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 thin mung bean crepes (guoba), cooked as for jianbing without egg
4 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 6 tbsp water
1 tbsp fermented tofu and coriander, to serve
steps: Cut the crepes into strips 1.5 cm wide.
Fry the star anise and garlic in the oil for 30 seconds, add the soy sauces and water and bring to a boil.
Thicken with the cornstarch slurry to a glossy brown gravy (lu), then remove the star anise.
Put the crepe strips in bowls and ladle the boiling gravy over so they soften slightly.
Top with sesame paste, fermented tofu and coriander and eat at once for breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 80 g mixed nuts, sesame and candied ginger, finely chopped
steps: Make a dough of half the flour with yeast and water and rest 30 minutes, then knead in the remaining flour, soda, sugar and oil.
Divide off a third of the dough and knead the nut and candied ginger mix into it.
Roll both doughs into thin ropes, combine several plain and filled ropes, twist them together tightly and fold back on themselves into a thick twist about 20 cm long.
Fry at 150 C for 15-20 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp right through.
Drain and cool completely before serving; they keep for weeks in an airtight tin.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the rice flour and water into a dough, steam in pieces for 20 minutes until translucent, then knead smooth while warm.
Divide into 12, flatten each, wrap a ball of red bean paste and press into a thick round.
Fry in oil at 170 C for 6-8 minutes until puffed, crisp and golden with a blistered surface.
Drain and sprinkle with sugar while hot; traditionally the rice is soaked and stone-ground overnight, which you can replace with rice flour as here.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g donkey meat (or beef shin as substitute), in large pieces
1 spice bag: star anise, cinnamon, bay leaf, Sichuan pepper, cloves
steps: Soak the meat in cold water for 1 hour, blanch for 10 minutes and rinse.
Simmer with the soy sauces, spice bag, ginger, salt and 2 litres water for 2 hours until tender, then cool in the liquid.
Make a firm dough with the flour and water, roll thin, spread with lard, roll up and form 4 rectangles; dry-fry them for 4 minutes per side then bake at 200 C for 8 minutes until crisp.
Chop the meat with a little jellied stock and green chilli, split the warm bread and stuff it generously.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: tofu, potato slices and cabbage, for the pot
steps: Blanch the chicken for 3 minutes and drain.
Fry the chillies, Sichuan pepper, star anise, ginger and garlic in oil for 1 minute, add the chilli bean paste and chicken and stir-fry 5 minutes until the skin colours.
Add the soy sauces and water, cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Transfer to a tabletop pot on a burner, eat the chicken first, then add water and cook tofu, potato and cabbage in the spicy broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the flour and water into a very soft dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the meat with soy, salt, ginger, sesame oil and five-spice and fold in the scallions.
Roll the dough into a large thin sheet, spread the filling over half, fold over and seal into a large thin pie about 1 cm thick.
Pan-fry in oil over medium-low heat, covered, for 6-8 minutes per side until crisp, golden and the filling is cooked.
Cut into wedges and serve hot with porridge.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Knead the flour, salt and water into a very stiff dough, rest 30 minutes and knead again until smooth; form into a log.
Brown the pork in oil, add the soy sauces, star anise and 500 ml water and simmer 45 minutes into a rich braise (dalu).
Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil, hold the dough over it and shave thick ribbons off with a sharp curved blade straight into the water.
Boil for 4-5 minutes until the noodles float and are chewy-tender, then drain into bowls.
Top with the pork braise and tomato and season with Shanxi vinegar at the table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Pour the boiling water over the oat flour, stir with chopsticks, then knead into a smooth dough while hot.

Pinch off small pieces, roll each very thin on a smooth stone or oiled board with your palm and curl it around your finger into a thin tube, standing them close together in a steamer like a honeycomb.
Steam over high heat for 8-10 minutes until cooked.
Fry the tomato in oil for 3 minutes, mix with garlic, soy, vinegar and chilli oil to make the sauce.
Serve the rolls with the tomato-vinegar dip and shredded cucumber; buckwheat or wholemeal flour can stand in for oat flour, though less authentic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g plain flour (or half sorghum flour)
steps: Mix the flour, salt and water into a soft, sticky dough, cover and rest 30 minutes.
Fry the pork in oil until browned, add the tomatoes and soy and simmer 5 minutes, then stir in the eggs until just set.
Bring a pot of water to a boil, put dough on a plate, tilt it over the pot and flick thin strips off the edge with a chopstick into the water.
Cook for 3 minutes until they float and are tender, then drain into bowls.
Top with the pork and tomato sauce and a splash of vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 small cucumber or 50 g bamboo shoots, sliced
300 ml neutral oil, for passing through
steps: Coat the pork slices with egg white and cornstarch.
Heat the oil to 150 C, slide in the pork and stir for 1 minute until white and cooked through, then drain, keeping 2 tbsp oil.
Stir-fry the garlic, wood ear and cucumber for 1 minute over high heat.
Add the pork, soy, sugar and a little cornstarch water, toss, then splash the Shanxi vinegar around the wok so it sizzles, and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg beef shin or brisket, in large pieces
1 tsp saltpetre-free curing salt or extra salt
steps: Rub the beef all over with the salt and cure in the fridge overnight, turning once.
Rinse and put into a pot with the spices, ginger, soy sauce and enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 3 hours until tender but firm enough to slice.
Cool completely in the liquid, then slice thinly against the grain and serve cold with garlic and vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g mutton (lamb) shoulder, in large chunks
80 g oat or wheat flour, toasted and mixed with 200 ml water
200 ml huangjiu (yellow rice wine) or Shaoxing wine
4 pickled garlic chives or pickled leeks, to serve
steps: Blanch the lamb, then simmer with the ginger and astragalus in 2 litres water for 2 hours until tender; discard the astragalus.
Add the lotus root and yam and simmer 15 minutes.
Whisk in the flour slurry and the wine and simmer, stirring, for 10 minutes until thick, smooth and cooked through.
Season with salt and serve in bowls with pickled leeks and toasted flatbreads (maozhu) dipped into it.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg mixed lamb offal (tripe, intestines, lung, heart, liver), thoroughly cleaned
steps: Soak and rinse the offal repeatedly, blanch for 10 minutes and rinse again.
Simmer the offal with the ginger, star anise and Sichuan pepper for 2 hours (add the liver only for the last 20 minutes) until everything is tender.
Lift out, slice into thin strips and return to the strained broth; season with salt and white pepper.
Bring back to a rolling boil and serve in bowls with plenty of coriander and chilli oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the buckwheat flour with 200 ml cold water to a smooth paste.
Bring the remaining water and salt to a boil, stir in the paste and cook on low heat, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes until very thick and glossy.
Pour into shallow bowls and steam for 15 minutes, then cool completely until set.
Turn out, slice into strips and dress with vinegar, soy, chilli oil, garlic and sesame paste; serve cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Dissolve the sugar and maltose in the water, then mix with the oil.
Sift in the flour, baking powder and soda and fold lightly into a soft dough without over-kneading; rest 20 minutes.
Divide into 10, roll into balls, flatten and press the tops into sesame seeds.
Bake at 180 C for 15-18 minutes until golden and crackled; cool before eating.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g glutinous millet flour (huangmi mian), or glutinous rice flour
250 g red bean paste or jujube paste
steps: Mix the millet flour with the water, leave covered overnight, then steam in a cloth for 25 minutes until golden and sticky.
Knead while hot with oiled hands until smooth and elastic.
Divide into 12, wrap each round a spoon of bean paste and flatten into small cakes.
Fry at 170 C for 5-6 minutes until the outside is crisp and blistered, drain and dust with sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 tbsp Shanxi aged vinegar (lao chencu), bought from a licensed producer
steps: Lao chencu is a dark, mellow vinegar fermented from sorghum and aged for years; buy it ready-made rather than making it.
Stir the garlic, soy and chilli oil into the vinegar to make the classic table dip for dumplings, noodles and cold dishes.
Use plain lao chencu at the table for noodles, or Zhenjiang black vinegar if it is unavailable.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g pork belly, skin on, in large pieces
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 bay leaves, 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, 2 slices ginger
1 green chilli and a handful of coriander, chopped
steps: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 5 minutes, rinse, then simmer it gently with the soy sauces, rock sugar, spices, ginger, wine and water to cover for 2 to 2.5 hours until a chopstick slides through easily.

Meanwhile mix the flour, yeast and warm water into a firm dough, knead 5 minutes and rest 30 minutes; divide into 8 balls, roll each into a long strip, roll it up like a snail, stand it on end and flatten into a 10 cm disc (this makes the layered baijimo bun).

Dry-fry the discs in a heavy pan over medium-low heat for about 4 minutes per side until pale-golden with the characteristic "tiger-back, chrysanthemum-heart" ring, then bake 5 minutes at 200 C to cook through.
Lift the pork out, chop it finely on a board together with a little of the fat, the chilli and coriander, moistening with 2 to 3 tbsp of the braising liquid.
Split each warm bun open on one side like a pocket, stuff generously with the chopped pork and spoon over a little more liquid; eat hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g high-protein plain or bread flour
2 tbsp neutral oil for coating the dough
2 tbsp Shaanxi chilli flakes (youpo lazi), or Korean gochugaru mixed with a pinch of cayenne
2 tbsp Chinese black vinegar and 1 tbsp light soy sauce
steps: Mix the flour, salt and water into a firm dough, knead 10 minutes until smooth, rest 30 minutes, knead again briefly, then cut into 6 pieces, roll each into a thick oval, oil well, cover and rest at least 1 hour (up to 2).

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil; flatten one piece with a rolling pin, press a groove down the middle with a chopstick, hold both ends and slap it on the counter while pulling to stretch it into a belt 1 m long and 5 cm wide, then tear it apart along the groove into a loop.
Drop the noodles into the boiling water and cook 1.5 to 2 minutes until they float and are chewy; blanch the bok choy in the same water for the last 30 seconds.
Place the noodles and greens in a wide bowl, add the soy sauce and vinegar, then pile the garlic, spring onion and chilli flakes on top.
Heat the oil until just smoking and pour it over the aromatics so they sizzle, then toss everything together and eat immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp Shaanxi chilli flakes, or gochugaru
2 tbsp light soy sauce and 2 tbsp Chinese black vinegar (Shanxi aged vinegar)
steps: Knead the flour, salt and water into a smooth firm dough, rest 30 minutes, then cut into fingers, oil them and rest covered for 1 hour.
Press each finger flat, then pull and stretch it into a long wide ribbon about 3 cm wide by gently slapping it against the counter.
Boil the noodles in plenty of water for 2 minutes until they float and turn chewy-tender, adding the sprouts and bok choy for the final 30 seconds; drain into bowls.
Season with soy sauce and vinegar, top with garlic, spring onion and chilli flakes.
Heat the rapeseed oil until smoking and splash it over the toppings so they crackle, then mix well and serve right away.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g wheat starch (cheng fen), or 150 g plain flour washed to extract starch plus 50 g tapioca starch
3 cloves garlic, pounded with 3 tbsp water
3 tbsp Chinese black vinegar, 2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar
steps: Whisk the starch, salt and water into a thin smooth batter.
Lightly oil a flat metal tray, pour in a thin layer of batter (about 2 mm), float the tray in a wok of boiling water, cover and steam 2 to 3 minutes until the sheet turns translucent and bubbles up.
Lift the tray into a basin of cold water to cool, peel off the sheet, brush with oil and stack; repeat with the remaining batter.
Cut the stacked sheets into 1.5 cm wide strips and pile into bowls with the cucumber, sprouts and gluten cubes.
Mix the garlic water, vinegar, soy sauce and sugar, pour over, add chilli oil, toss and serve cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g bean sprouts and 1 bunch Chinese chives (jiucai), blanched and cut short
3 cloves garlic, pounded with 3 tbsp water
3 tbsp Hanzhong-style chilli oil (with plenty of sediment)
2 tbsp rice vinegar or black vinegar
steps: Drain the soaked rice and blend it with the water and salt into a very fine milky batter; rest 20 minutes.
Oil a shallow steaming tray, pour in a thin layer of batter, and steam over high heat for 2 minutes until set, glossy and bubbling.
Cool the tray briefly in cold water, peel off the soft rice sheet, brush with oil and stack; repeat until the batter is used.
Cut the warm sheets into wide strips with a large knife and divide among bowls with the sprouts and chives.
Dress with the garlic water, vinegar, soy sauce and a generous spoon of chilli oil; toss and serve warm or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 120 ml Qishan rice vinegar or Chinese black vinegar (Shanxi aged vinegar as substitute)
1 carrot, 1 block firm tofu and 50 g wood ear mushrooms, all diced small
2 eggs, made into a thin omelette and diced
2 garlic shoots or spring onions, chopped
steps: Fry the pork in lard over medium heat for 10 minutes until the fat runs and the edges turn golden, add the chilli flakes and fry 30 seconds, then pour in half the vinegar and the soy sauce and simmer covered for 25 minutes to make the sour-hot saozi.
In a separate pot heat the water with the remaining vinegar and salt, add the carrot, tofu and wood ear and simmer 10 minutes; ladle in some of the red pork oil so the broth turns bright and tangy.
Boil the noodles 2 to 3 minutes until just tender and drain.
Put a small portion of noodles into each bowl (Qishan noodles are served in small bowls), top with the saozi meat, omelette and garlic shoots, and ladle over the hot sour broth; serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg bone-in lamb or mutton (leg or shoulder)
30 g mung bean glass noodles (fensi), soaked
20 g dried wood ear, soaked and shredded
2 slices ginger, 2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, 2 bay leaves
2 spring onions and a handful of coriander, chopped
pickled sweet garlic (tangsuan) and chilli sauce to serve
steps: Blanch the lamb 5 minutes, rinse, then simmer with the ginger and spices in 3 litres of water over low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is falling off the bone and the broth is milky; season with salt and slice the meat.
Mix the flour, yeast and water into a stiff dough, rest 20 minutes, shape into 4 flat discs (tuotuomo) and dry-cook in a heavy pan over low heat for 6 to 7 minutes per side until firm and pale.
Let each diner tear their bread into pea-sized pieces into a bowl — the traditional, leisurely part of the meal.
Bring 2 ladles of broth per bowl to a boil in a wok, add the bread, glass noodles, wood ear and sliced meat and boil 2 to 3 minutes until the bread absorbs the broth but stays chewy.
Serve topped with spring onion and coriander, with pickled sweet garlic and chilli sauce on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp flour and 2 tbsp salt for cleaning
300 g plain flour made into 4 tuotuomo flatbreads as for yangrou paomo
2 slices ginger, 2 star anise, 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, 1 tsp fennel seed
chilli oil and pickled garlic to serve
steps: Rub the intestine with flour and salt, turn inside out, rinse very thoroughly under running water and trim excess fat; blanch it 5 minutes with ginger and rinse again.

Simmer the bones and intestine with the spices in 3 litres of water for 2.5 to 3 hours until the intestine is very tender and the broth is rich; remove, slice the intestine into rings and season the broth with salt.
Tear the flatbread into small pieces and place in bowls.

Pour boiling broth over the bread, drain it back into the pot and repeat twice so the bread is heated through (the "tang" method), then add the intestine, chicken and glass noodles and top up with very hot broth.
Finish with spring onion and coriander and serve with chilli oil and pickled garlic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 egg white, 1 tbsp cornflour, 1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper, 1 tsp salt
1 carrot, 1/4 cabbage and 100 g cauliflower, cut in pieces
3 tbsp potato starch mixed with 6 tbsp water
1 tsp ground white pepper and 1 tsp ground black pepper
flatbread or steamed buns to serve
steps: Mix the beef with egg white, cornflour, Sichuan pepper, salt and 3 tbsp water, stirring in one direction until sticky; roll into walnut-sized balls.
Bring the stock to a simmer, drop in the meatballs and cook 8 minutes until firm and cooked through.
Add the potatoes and carrot and simmer 12 minutes, then the cabbage and cauliflower for 6 minutes more until all are tender.
Season with the peppers and five-spice, then stir in the starch slurry and simmer 2 minutes until the soup becomes thick and glossy (the "hula" texture).
Ladle into bowls, drizzle with chilli oil and serve with flatbread for breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 small whole chicken (about 1.2 kg), trussed tightly
3 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp salt
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 slices ginger, 2 spring onions
spiced salt (jiaoyan: 2 tsp salt toasted with 1 tsp Sichuan pepper) and sweet bean sauce to serve
steps: Simmer the trussed chicken in stock with soy sauce, sugar, salt, wine, spices and aromatics for 40 minutes until cooked through (juices run clear at the thigh).
Transfer the chicken in a deep bowl with a ladle of the stock and steam over high heat for 40 minutes until very tender but still holding its gourd shape; drain and pat completely dry.
Heat the oil to 190 C and lower the chicken in, ladling hot oil over the top, for 3 to 4 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Drain and present whole, pulling the meat apart at the table, with spiced salt and sweet bean sauce for dipping.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g pork skin and 500 ml water, for aspic
400 g minced beef (or lamb, as served in Xi'an's Muslim Quarter)
2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper
1 tbsp grated ginger and 2 spring onions, minced
black vinegar and chilli oil to serve
steps: Blanch and scrape the pork skin, simmer it in the water for 2 hours until it melts, strain and chill 3 hours until set; dice the jelly finely. (For an all-halal version use beef bone broth set with gelatine.)
Mix the beef with soy, salt, pepper, ginger, spring onion, sesame oil and 4 tbsp water, stirring until sticky, then fold in the diced jelly.
Knead the flour and warm water into a soft dough, rest 20 minutes, divide into 30 pieces and roll each into a thin 8 cm wrapper with thinner edges.
Place a spoon of filling in each wrapper and pleat closed into a small bun with 18 or more folds.

Steam on lined baskets over vigorously boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes until the wrappers are translucent and the filling is cooked through; serve at once with vinegar and chilli oil, sipping the soup first.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1/4 tsp baking soda dissolved in 1 tbsp water
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and water into a very stiff dough; knead hard (traditionally pressed with a wooden pole) for 10 minutes, rest 30 minutes, then knead in the soda water until smooth.
Rest the dough 45 minutes, then shape into a large round disc about 3 cm thick and 25 cm wide, pressing a pattern on top with a fork or wooden stamp.

Brush a heavy cast-iron pan with oil and bake the disc over very low heat, covered, for 15 to 20 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until both faces are pale golden and it sounds hollow when tapped.
Cool completely before cutting into wedges; the dense, dry bread keeps for a week and is eaten with tea or broken into soups.

ingredients: 1 tsp sweet osmanthus (gui hua) jam, optional
steps: Scoop the persimmon flesh into a bowl, mash it, then mix in both flours to make a soft, non-sticky orange dough, adding more flour if needed.
Combine the brown sugar, walnuts, sesame and osmanthus as the filling.
Divide the dough into 12 balls, flatten each, fill with a spoon of sugar mix, seal and press into 1 cm thick cakes.
Pan-fry in oil over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden, puffed and the filling has melted; serve warm, taking care with the hot syrup.

ingredients: 2 tbsp coloured sugar sprinkles or crushed dried rose petals
steps: Drain the soaked rice and grind it to a coarse damp flour in a food processor.
Pack the rice flour loosely into small greased round moulds (about 5 cm wide, 1 cm deep), leveling the top.
Steam over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the cakes set into translucent white discs like little mirrors.
Turn each out, insert a skewer, and press one side onto a plate of sugar mixed with sesame and sprinkles, brushing a little osmanthus jam on top; eat warm.

ingredients: 300 g dried red dates (jujubes), soaked 1 hour
50 g sugar or honey to serve
1 tsp neutral oil for the tin
steps: Drain the rice; oil a deep heatproof bowl or steamer tin.
Layer a third of the dates, then a third of the rice, repeating to make three layers and finishing with dates pressed on top.
Steam over medium heat, covered, for 2 to 2.5 hours, sprinkling a little hot water over the surface twice, until the rice is completely soft and stained purple-red by the dates.
Scoop or slice into portions while hot and serve sprinkled with sugar or drizzled with honey and osmanthus, as a Xi'an breakfast sweet.

ingredients: 1 kg lamb bones and 400 g lamb shoulder
500 g plain flour, 260 ml water, 1/2 tsp salt
1 spice bag: star anise, cinnamon, Sichuan pepper, fennel seed
20 g dried kelp (haidai), soaked and shredded
chilli oil and sugar-garlic, to serve
steps: Simmer the bones and lamb with the spice bag and ginger in 3 litres water for 2.5 hours into a milky broth; slice the meat.
Knead the flour, salt and water into a soft dough, oil it, form into thick strips and rest 30 minutes.
Bring the broth to a boil, add the kelp and glass noodles, then stretch each strip into a wide ribbon and drop it straight in.
Cook for 3-4 minutes until the noodles are tender, add the lamb and quail eggs and season with salt.
Serve with coriander, chilli oil and pickled garlic.

ingredients: 10 g dried wood ear, soaked and shredded
50 g dried tofu skin and glass noodles, soaked
5 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 8 tbsp water
1 tsp black vinegar and sesame oil, to serve
steps: Simmer the beef in the stock for 1 hour until tender.
Add the wood ear, tofu skin, gluten and glass noodles and simmer 10 minutes.
Season with both peppers and soy, then stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until thick and glossy.
Ladle into bowls with a few drops of vinegar and sesame oil, and serve with fried buns or youtiao for breakfast.

ingredients: 2 tbsp maltose or honey, thinned with water
1 spice bag: star anise, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf, cardamom, fennel, tangerine peel, nutmeg
steps: Fold the wings and legs into the cavity to make a compact shape, then brush with maltose and leave 20 minutes to dry.
Fry at 170 C for 3-4 minutes until the skin is deep red-gold.
Put the chicken in a pot with the spice bag, soy, salt, ginger, sugar and water to cover, bring to a boil and simmer very gently for 2.5 hours until the meat slips off the bone.
Lift out carefully, cool slightly and serve warm or at room temperature, torn by hand.

ingredients: 1 Yellow River carp, about 800 g, cleaned and scored
1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
150 g very thin dried wheat noodles (dragon whisker noodles)
steps: Rub the carp with salt and wine, coat thickly with cornstarch, then fry at 180 C for 6-8 minutes, holding it curved, until crisp and cooked through.
Briefly blanch the noodles, drain, then fry in the oil for 1 minute until crisp and golden as a fluffy nest.
Simmer the sugar, vinegar, tomato paste, soy and water and thicken with 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed in a little water.
Pour the sweet-sour sauce over the carp and pile the crisp noodles over the top; serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g white daikon radish, very finely shredded
6 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and shredded
50 g sea cucumber or squid, shredded and blanched
1 egg, made into a thin omelette and shredded
1 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp black vinegar
2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
steps: Soak the radish shreds in cold water for 15 minutes, drain well, coat lightly in mung bean starch and steam for 5 minutes until they turn translucent like bird's nest.
Bring the stock to a boil with the mushrooms, ham and seafood and simmer 5 minutes until the seafood is cooked.
Season with soy, vinegar and pepper and thicken with the cornstarch slurry.
Put the radish in a large bowl, ladle the soup over and arrange the egg shreds on top like a peony flower.

ingredients: black vinegar and ginger shreds, to serve
steps: Simmer the cleaned pork skin in 1.2 litres water for 2 hours, blend, strain and chill overnight to set into a firm aspic; dice finely.
Mix the pork with soy, ginger, salt and sesame oil, then fold in an equal volume of diced aspic.
Make a dough of the flour and water, rest 20 minutes, divide into 30 and roll very thin wrappers.
Fill each, pleat into a small bun with many folds and steam over high heat for 8-10 minutes until the filling is cooked and the aspic has melted into soup.
Lift carefully, bite a small hole, sip the soup and eat with vinegar and ginger.

ingredients: 500 g mung bean jelly (liangfen), in 2 cm cubes
1 tbsp fermented black bean or sweet bean sauce
steps: Heat the oil in a flat pan and fry the pork over medium-high heat for 3 minutes until fully cooked and crumbly.
Add the bean jelly cubes and fry without stirring too much for 6-8 minutes until a golden crust forms on the bottom.
Add the bean sauce, soy sauces, garlic and chilli and toss gently to coat.
Cook 2 minutes more until the edges are crisp and caramelised, scatter with scallion and serve hot from the pan.

ingredients: 250 g fresh alkaline wheat noodles (jianshui mian), or thick ramen noodles
1 tbsp sesame oil plus 1 tsp for tossing
3 tbsp Chinese sesame paste (zhimajiang), or tahini mixed with 1 tsp toasted sesame oil
2 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp dark soy sauce
2 tbsp pickled radish cubes (luobo ding) or Sichuan zhacai, finely diced
2 tbsp chopped pickled long beans (suan doujiao)
steps: Boil the noodles 2 to 3 minutes until just al dente, drain, toss with sesame oil and spread out under a fan to cool and dry (the traditional pre-cooking step).
Loosen the sesame paste with the soy sauces, vinegar and 2 to 3 tbsp warm water until it flows like thick cream.
To serve, plunge the noodles into boiling water for 15 seconds to reheat, then shake very dry and place in bowls.
Spoon over the sesame sauce, top with pickled radish, long beans, spring onion and chilli oil, and mix thoroughly so every strand is coated; eat at once for breakfast.

ingredients: 1 whole Wuchang bream (tuantou fang), about 800 g, scaled and gutted, or any bream or sea bass
4 slices ginger plus 1 thumb ginger, julienned
3 spring onions, 1 in sections and 2 julienned
30 g cured ham or shiitake slices, optional garnish
steps: Score the fish 3 times on each side, rub with wine and salt and lay on a plate over the ginger slices and spring onion sections, tucking ginger into the cuts and arranging ham or shiitake on top if using.
Steam over vigorously boiling water for 9 to 11 minutes until the flesh flakes away from the bone at the thickest point and the eyes turn white.
Pour off the steaming liquid, discard the cooked aromatics, and scatter the julienned ginger and spring onion over the fish.
Pour the soy sauce around the fish, then heat the oil until smoking and pour it over the aromatics so they sizzle; serve immediately with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper
1 tsp grated ginger and 1 spring onion, minced
steps: Drain the soaked rice well and spread it on a tray.
Mix the pork with the water chestnuts, egg, soy, salt, pepper, wine, ginger, spring onion, cornflour and sesame oil, stirring in one direction until sticky.
Roll the mixture into balls the size of a walnut and roll each over the rice, pressing so it is fully coated.
Arrange on a lined steamer with gaps between them and steam over high heat for 25 to 30 minutes until the rice grains are translucent like pearls and the pork is cooked through; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g freshwater fish fillet (grass carp), cut in pieces
300 g taro, peeled and cut in chunks, or pumpkin
200 g mixed-grain rice flour (mifen: rice toasted with star anise and ground coarsely), or ready-made steamed-pork rice powder
3 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp fermented bean curd juice
steps: Marinate the pork and fish separately for 15 minutes each with soy sauce, bean curd juice, wine, ginger and pepper.
Coat the pork, fish and taro each evenly in the rice powder, adding a little water so it clings, and drizzle with melted lard.
Layer the taro in the bottom of a bamboo steamer, the pork in another and the fish in a third basket.
Steam over high heat: the pork and taro for 60 minutes until the pork is meltingly tender, adding the fish basket for the last 15 minutes until cooked through.
Serve all three in their baskets scattered with spring onion, in the Hubei "no banquet without steaming" tradition.

ingredients: 500 g boneless white fish (grass carp or silver carp), skinned
1.5 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp white pepper
1 tbsp ginger-spring onion water (grated ginger and spring onion soaked in 100 ml water, strained)
steps: Blend the fish with the fat, salt, pepper and ginger-spring onion water to a smooth paste, then beat in the egg whites and starch and stir hard in one direction until elastic and fluffy.
Spread the paste 4 cm thick in an oiled tray, smooth the top and steam over medium-high heat for 30 minutes until set and cooked through.
Brush the surface with beaten yolk and steam another 3 to 5 minutes until the yellow top is set.
Cool slightly, cut into rectangular slices and serve warm or simmer them in broth with spring onion for the classic Jingzhou "fish without bones" dish.

ingredients: 2 kg live crayfish, purged in clean water and scrubbed
20 dried red chillies and 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns
1 head garlic, cloves smashed, and 50 g ginger, sliced
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 bay leaves
2 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp sugar
1 bunch spring onions and coriander, cut long
steps: Remove the central tail vein of each crayfish, rinse and drain; blanch them in boiling water for 1 minute until bright red.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, fry the garlic, ginger and whole spices 1 minute, then the bean paste, chillies and peppercorns for 1 minute until red and fragrant.
Add the crayfish and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes, then pour in the beer, soy sauce and sugar.
Cover and simmer 12 to 15 minutes until the meat is opaque and firm, then uncover and reduce the sauce for 3 minutes.
Toss in the spring onion and coriander and serve heaped on a platter with gloves and cold drinks.

dishes.name: Doupi (Wuhan Tofu Skin with Sticky Rice)

ingredients: 300 g glutinous rice, soaked overnight and steamed 30 minutes
100 g mung beans and 50 g long-grain rice, soaked overnight
4 dried shiitake, soaked and diced, and 50 g bamboo shoot, diced
2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp dark soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar
steps: Fry the pork in 1 tbsp lard until golden, add the shiitake, bamboo shoot and tofu, season with soy sauces and sugar and a splash of mushroom water, and cook 5 minutes until glossy.
Blend the soaked mung beans and rice with 300 ml water into a thin batter.
Heat a large flat pan with 1 tbsp lard, pour in a thin even layer of batter and cook over medium heat 1 minute until set; beat the eggs and spread them over the top.
Flip the sheet, spread the steamed sticky rice over in an even layer, then the pork filling, and drizzle the rest of the lard around the edge; fry 4 to 5 minutes until the base is crisp and golden.
Cut into squares in the pan, flip each so the crisp skin is on top, scatter spring onion and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Blend the drained rice and soybeans with about 200 ml water into a smooth, thick batter, then stir in the sugar, salt, baking powder and spring onion.
Heat the oil to 180 C and warm a mianwo ladle (a flat, ring-shaped ladle with a raised centre) or a small round ladle in the oil.
Spread a thin layer of batter in the ladle so the centre is thin and the rim thick, lower it into the oil and fry until it releases, about 1 minute.
Continue frying, turning once, for 2 to 3 minutes until golden-brown with a crisp thin middle and a soft thick edge; drain and eat hot with soy milk.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp dark soy sauce, 1/2 tsp white pepper
200 g plain flour, 100 ml boiling water and cornflour for dusting
steps: Steam the drained rice for 30 minutes until tender.
Fry the pork in lard until golden, add the shiitake, soy sauces, pepper and 100 ml mushroom water, then stir in the steamed rice and spring onion until evenly brown and moist.
Make a hot-water dough with the flour and boiling water, rest 15 minutes, divide into 20 pieces and roll each very thin, pressing the edges with cornflour into frilly "lotus-leaf" rims.
Place a spoon of rice in each wrapper, gather the sides around it leaving the top open, and steam over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the skins are translucent; serve hot.

dishes.name: Lotus Root and Pork Rib Soup (Paigu Ou Tang)

ingredients: 800 g pork spare ribs, cut in pieces
2 sections Hubei lotus root (about 600 g), the starchy "fen ou" type, peeled and cut in chunks
steps: Blanch the ribs in boiling water with the wine for 5 minutes, then rinse.
Put the ribs and ginger into a clay pot (wei guan) with 2.5 litres of water, bring to a boil and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the lotus root, cutting it with a rough break rather than a clean slice so it releases starch, and simmer 1.5 hours more until it is soft, powdery and pulls into threads.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with the spring onion scattered on top.

ingredients: 1 kg duck necks, trimmed of fat
3 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tbsp dark soy sauce
30 dried red chillies and 2 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns
3 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 bay leaves, 1 tsp fennel seed, 2 pieces dried tangerine peel
1 tbsp chilli oil and 1 tsp sesame oil to finish
steps: Rinse the necks, marinate with wine, ginger and 1 tsp salt for 3 hours, then blanch 3 minutes and rinse.
Bring 2 litres of water to a boil with the soy sauces, rock sugar, chillies, peppercorns and spices and simmer 20 minutes to make a spicy brine (lu shui).
Add the necks and simmer 35 to 40 minutes until cooked through, then turn off the heat and let them soak in the brine for 2 hours to absorb the flavour.
Drain, brush with chilli oil and sesame oil, and air-dry 20 minutes or dry in a 120 C oven for 15 minutes; chop into sections and serve cold as a snack.

ingredients: 400 g ready-made Xiaogan mijiu (sweet fermented glutinous rice, jiuniang), bought from a licensed producer or Chinese grocer
100 g small glutinous rice balls (xiaoyuanzi), bought frozen or homemade
steps: Xiaogan mijiu is a famous Hubei sweet, lightly alcoholic fermented glutinous rice made by specialist local producers; buy it ready-made rather than fermenting at home.
Bring the water to a boil, drop in the rice balls and cook 3 to 4 minutes until they float and are soft.
Stir in the mijiu and sugar and heat just until it returns to a simmer so the sweet aroma rises.
Ladle into bowls, top with osmanthus, and serve hot as a breakfast or dessert; it can also be served chilled straight from the jar in summer.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g bone-in chicken thighs, chopped into pieces
60 ml rice wine (Jiangxi mijiu or Shaoxing wine)
steps: Heat the sesame oil in a clay pot on medium heat and fry the ginger and garlic for 3 minutes until golden.
Add the chicken and stir-fry 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in the wine, soy sauce and rock sugar, cover, and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Uncover and cook on high, stirring, until the sauce reduces to a sticky glaze.
Add the chilies and basil, cover for 1 minute to wilt, and serve sizzling with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Steamed Pork with Rice Flour (Fenzheng Rou)

ingredients: 500 g skin-on pork belly, cut into 5 mm slices
1 star anise and 1/2 tsp Sichuan peppercorns
1 tbsp Pixian chili bean paste or fermented bean curd
1 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp dark soy sauce
300 g sweet potato or pumpkin, cut into chunks
steps: Toast the rice with the star anise and peppercorns in a dry pan on low heat for 10 minutes until golden, then grind coarsely.
Marinate the pork with the bean paste, soy sauces, wine, sugar and ginger for 30 minutes.
Toss the pork in the ground rice with 2 tbsp water until evenly coated.
Line a bowl with sweet potato, lay the pork on top, and steam over high heat for 60 minutes until the pork is meltingly tender.
Garnish with spring onions and serve.

ingredients: 500 g grass carp fillet, sliced into thin strips
1 small bunch perilla or spring onions
steps: Marinate the fish with salt, egg white and cornstarch for 10 minutes.
Slide the fish into warm oil over medium heat and cook 1 minute until white, then remove.
Fry the ginger and chilies in the same oil on high heat for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the fish, add the wine and vinegar, and toss gently 1 to 2 minutes until the fish is cooked through and flakes, then add perilla and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g fresh thick round rice noodles (Nanchang banfen); substitute dried round rice noodles, cooked
100 g braised pork or char siu, sliced
2 tbsp chopped pickled radish or pickled cowpeas
steps: Blanch the noodles in boiling water for 20 to 30 seconds until hot and soft, then drain well.
Toss with the soy sauce, chili oil and sesame oil until evenly coated.
Top with the pork, pickles, peanuts and spring onions and serve with a cup of clay jar soup.

ingredients: 300 g fresh or soaked dried round rice noodles
2 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp dark soy sauce
steps: Scramble the eggs in 1 tbsp lard until just set and remove.
Stir-fry the pork in the remaining lard on high heat for 2 minutes until cooked, add the cabbage and bean sprouts, and fry 1 minute.
Add the noodles, soy sauces and chili sauce and toss with chopsticks over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until evenly coloured and slightly charred.
Return the eggs, add spring onions, and serve hot.

dishes.name: Nanchang Clay Jar Soup (Wa Guan Tang)

ingredients: 400 g pork ribs or minced pork, or 1 small chicken, cut up
steps: Blanch the meat in boiling water for 3 minutes and rinse.
Divide the meat, dates, goji, ginger and mushrooms between 4 small clay jars and fill with water, covering with lids.
Set the jars in a large pot with water halfway up their sides, or in a slow cooker, and steam-simmer gently for 3 to 4 hours until the meat is falling off the bone and the broth is clear and rich.
Season with salt and serve each jar with Nanchang banfen.

ingredients: 500 g river snails (field snails), purged in water for a day and scrubbed; substitute clams
3 tbsp vegetable oil and 30 g ginger, sliced
2 tbsp perilla (zisu) and 2 star anise, 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns
400 g dried luosifen rice noodles, soaked 2 hours
150 g sour bamboo shoots (suan sun), shredded; buy fermented in jars
100 g dried tofu skin, fried, and 50 g roasted peanuts
50 g wood ear fungus, soaked and sliced
steps: Fry the ginger, perilla and spices in the oil for 1 minute, add the snails and stir-fry on high heat 5 minutes.
Add the pork bones and 3 litres water, bring to a boil, and simmer 2.5 to 3 hours to a rich broth; strain.
Fry the sour bamboo shoots in a little oil for 3 minutes until fragrant and pungent.
Boil the noodles 8 to 10 minutes until tender, and blanch the greens.
Place the noodles in bowls, ladle the boiling broth over, and top with sour bamboo, pickled beans, wood ear, tofu skin, peanuts, greens and chili oil.

ingredients: 300 g fresh round Guilin rice noodles; substitute dried round rice noodles
150 g Guilin braised beef or pork (lu niurou), thinly sliced
100 ml Guilin lu shui (spiced soy braising brine)
2 tbsp crispy fried pork rind or fried peanuts
steps: Blanch the noodles in boiling water for 30 seconds until hot and soft and drain into bowls.
Spoon the lu shui over and toss so every strand is coated.
Top with the braised meat, crispy pork, peanuts, pickled beans and spring onions.
Add chili sauce to taste and a little broth if you like it soupy, then eat at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g fresh thin rice noodles or wheat noodles
steps: Fry the garlic, black beans, bird's eye chilies and sour bamboo in the lard on high heat for 2 minutes until very fragrant.
Add the pork and stir-fry 2 minutes until cooked.
Pour in the stock and bring to a rolling boil.
Add the noodles and cook 1 to 2 minutes, then serve topped with pickled chilies and spring onions.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 dried shiitake mushrooms and 30 g wood ear, soaked and chopped
200 ml warm bone broth seasoned with soy sauce, for dipping
steps: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch and water into a thin batter and rest 10 minutes.
Stir-fry the pork, mushrooms and wood ear in the oil for 4 minutes until the pork is cooked, and season with soy sauce.
Steam a thin layer of batter on an oiled tray for 2 to 3 minutes until translucent.
Spread with filling and roll up into a tube, then cut into lengths.
Serve dipped in the warm seasoned broth with fried shallots.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 carp or Li River fish (about 1 kg), cleaned and cut into large pieces on the bone
2 green peppers and 2 red chilies, sliced
30 g ginger, sliced and 6 cloves garlic
steps: Pat the fish dry and pan-fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Add the ginger, garlic, chili bean paste and peppers and fry 1 minute.
Pour in the beer, soy sauce, sugar and salt, add the tomatoes, and simmer covered for 10 to 12 minutes until the fish flakes at the bone.
Reduce the sauce uncovered for 3 minutes, scatter spring onions, and serve in the pan.

ingredients: 4 pickled lemons (suan ningmeng), chopped; substitute preserved salted lemons
4 tbsp pickled chilies and 2 tbsp pickled ginger, chopped
2 tbsp sour plum sauce or 2 sour plums
steps: Stir-fry the duck in a hot dry wok for 8 minutes until the fat renders and the skin browns; pour off excess fat.
Add the oil, garlic, pickled lemon, chilies, ginger and sour plum and stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, sugar and water, cover, and simmer 30 to 35 minutes until the duck is tender.
Uncover and reduce on high heat until the sauce clings, then serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g skin-on pork belly in one piece
600 g Lipu taro, peeled and sliced to match the pork
2 tbsp red fermented bean curd (nan ru), mashed
2 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp dark soy sauce
steps: Boil the pork for 25 minutes until cooked through, prick the skin, rub with dark soy sauce, and deep-fry skin side down at 180°C for 4 minutes until blistered (cover the pot, it spatters).
Fry the taro slices 3 minutes until golden at the edges.
Slice the pork 1 cm thick, mix the bean curd, soy sauces, wine, sugar, five-spice and garlic, and coat both pork and taro.
Arrange alternating slices of pork and taro skin side down in a deep bowl and steam on high heat for 90 minutes until the taro is floury and the pork is tender.
Invert onto a plate, pour the juices over, and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg glutinous rice, divided into 5 portions
50 g red maple-like plant leaves (fengye) for black; substitute butterfly pea for blue/purple
30 g turmeric or gardenia for yellow
50 g purple-red blue grass (hongnan cao) leaves for red and purple; substitute beetroot juice
2 tbsp sugar or sesame for serving (optional)
steps: Steep each plant dye in hot water for several hours to extract colour (overnight for maple leaves), then strain.
Soak four portions of rice in the different dye waters and one in plain water overnight, until evenly coloured.
Drain and steam each colour in separate sections on a cloth over high heat for 35 to 40 minutes until tender and chewy.
Pile the colours together on a plate or in banana leaves and serve, traditionally for the Sanyuesan festival.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g mung beans, skinned and soaked overnight
500 g pork belly, cut into large strips
2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp five-spice, 1 tsp salt
15 large dried zongzi leaves (bamboo or dong leaves), soaked; plus string
steps: Marinate the pork with soy sauce, five-spice and salt for 2 hours.
Drain the rice and mix with oil and a little salt; drain the mung beans.
Overlap leaves into a large cone, add a layer of rice, a layer of mung beans, the pork, more mung beans, and finish with rice.
Fold the leaves over to form a large pillow shape and tie tightly with string.
Submerge in a large pot of water and boil for 6 to 8 hours, topping up with boiling water, until the rice is fully cooked and the pork tender, then slice to serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 50 g guiling gao herbal jelly powder (herbal blend; this vegetarian version uses no turtle shell)
4 tbsp honey or condensed milk to serve
steps: Whisk the jelly powder into 250 ml cold water until smooth.
Bring the remaining 750 ml water to a boil, pour in the slurry while stirring, and boil 2 to 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Pour into bowls, cool, and refrigerate 2 hours until set.
Serve chilled, drizzled with honey or condensed milk.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g fresh red chilies, stemmed and dried
steps: Mince the chilies and garlic finely, keeping everything dry.
Mix with the black beans, salt and sugar, pack into a sterilised jar, and leave sealed at room temperature for 1 day to mellow.
Heat the oil until shimmering and fry the mixture on low heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.
Cool, jar, and keep refrigerated, serving with Guilin rice noodles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 30 g green tea leaves, soaked briefly
2 tbsp tea seed oil (camellia oil); substitute peanut oil
50 g puffed rice, fried peanuts and spring onion, to serve
steps: Heat the tea seed oil in a wok, add the ginger and garlic, and fry on medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the tea leaves and pound them in the wok with a wooden mallet for 3 minutes until fragrant and slightly bitter.
Pour in the water and salt and boil 5 minutes until dark, then strain.
Serve hot in small bowls with puffed rice, peanuts and spring onion floating on top; refill several times.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole fresh carp or catfish (about 1 kg), cut into thick steaks
400 g red sour soup base (hong suantang), made from fermented wild tomatoes and chilies, or 6 ripe tomatoes plus 2 tbsp rice vinegar
1 tbsp fermented chili paste (zao lajiao) or pickled chilies
15 g ginger, sliced, and 3 garlic cloves
3 sprigs mujiangzi (litsea) oil or a few drops, or omit
100 g bean sprouts or water spinach
1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp vegetable oil
2 sprigs fresh mint or Chinese celery, and ciba lajiao dipping sauce
steps: Fry the ginger, garlic and chili paste in the oil 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the sour soup base and fry 2 minutes, then add the water and boil 10 minutes until the broth is bright red and tangy.
Add the fish steaks and simmer 8 minutes until the flesh is opaque and cooked through, adding the bean sprouts for the final 2 minutes.
Season with salt and a few drops of mujiangzi oil, add mint, and serve in a pot at the table with rice and a dip of ciba lajiao, as served by the Miao people of Kaili.

ingredients: 1 kg free-range chicken, chopped into small pieces
150 g ciba lajiao (Guizhou glutinous chili paste)
15 g ginger and 6 garlic cloves, sliced
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and 1 tbsp light soy
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken 6 minutes until the moisture evaporates and the skin is lightly browned.
Add ginger, garlic and peppercorns and fry 1 minute, then add the ciba lajiao and fry over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Add wine, soy, sugar, salt and water, cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Add spring onions and serve in a pot with rice; leftover sauce is often used to cook vegetables or noodles.

ingredients: 400 g fresh alkaline egg wheat noodles
300 g pork large intestines, cleaned with flour and salt
200 g cooked pork blood curd, sliced
2 tbsp light soy and 1 tsp Sichuan pepper
4 slices ginger, 2 star anise, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
steps: Blanch the intestines, then simmer with ginger, star anise and wine for 1.5 to 2 hours until tender; slice.
Fry the diced pork belly over low heat until crisp and golden to make the sizao topping.
Bring the stock to a boil and heat the blood curd slices in it for 3 minutes.
Boil the noodles until springy, about 2 minutes, and divide into bowls with chili oil, soy and Sichuan pepper.
Ladle in stock, top with intestines (chang), blood curd (wang) and crispy pork, and garnish with spring onions and coriander.

ingredients: 4 slices ginger, 2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 bay leaves, 1 tsp fennel
2 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp salt
150 g Guizhou sour pickled radish or sour cabbage, chopped
steps: Blanch the beef 5 minutes, rinse, then simmer in the stock with ginger, spices, soy and salt for 2 hours until tender.
Remove the beef, cool slightly and slice thinly; keep the broth hot.
Blanch the rice noodles in boiling water for 1 minute and divide into bowls.
Top with beef slices, ladle over the boiling broth, and serve with sour pickles, chili oil, coriander and celery to add at the table.

ingredients: 1 kg bone-in mutton or lamb (leg or breast)
20 g ginger, sliced and 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns
4 tbsp Zunyi chili oil (made with toasted chili flakes and mutton fat, or regular chili oil)
2 tbsp Chinese celery and 2 tbsp mint leaves
steps: Blanch the mutton 5 minutes, rinse, then simmer in 2.5 litres of water with ginger, peppercorns and star anise for 2 hours until tender and the broth is milky.
Lift out the mutton, cool and slice thinly; season the broth with salt.
Blanch the rice noodles 1 minute and divide among bowls.
Top with mutton slices, ladle over boiling broth and add chili oil, Sichuan pepper, celery, mint and spring onions.

ingredients: 200 g plain flour and 150 ml water (for thin wrappers), or 30 store-bought spring roll skins
80 g soybean sprouts and 80 g kelp, blanched and shredded
80 g pickled radish or sour cabbage and 50 g fried soybeans or peanuts
50 g fish-mint root (zheergen / houttuynia), cut short (optional)
sour dipping broth: 300 ml vegetable stock, 3 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp ciba lajiao, chopped coriander
steps: Mix flour and water into a soft, wet dough, rest 20 minutes, then rub thin circles onto a hot ungreased pan and cook 30 seconds until they lift off as palm-size, paper-thin wrappers.
Arrange all the vegetables and toppings in small separate dishes.
Warm the dipping broth ingredients together and pour into small bowls.
Each diner fills a wrapper with a few vegetables, folds it into a little cone like a swaddled baby (siwawa), spoons in the sour broth and eats it in one or two bites.

ingredients: 600 g Guizhou fermented-style tofu or firm tofu, cut into 3 x 4 cm squares
1/2 tsp baking soda dissolved in 500 ml water (to make the tofu puff)
dip: 3 tbsp chili flakes toasted in 2 tbsp oil, 2 tbsp light soy, 1 tbsp black vinegar
2 garlic cloves, minced, and 2 spring onions, sliced
1/2 tsp ground Sichuan pepper and salt to taste
steps: Soak the tofu squares in the baking soda water for 2 hours, then drain and pat dry.
Grill the squares on an oiled griddle or charcoal over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until puffed and golden with crisp skin.
Mix all the dip ingredients with fish-mint, garlic, spring onions and Sichuan pepper.
Slit each tofu square open along one side and stuff with a spoonful of the dip; eat hot, as couples did at Guiyang street stalls during the war years.

ingredients: 1 tsp food-grade limewater powder (edible lime) or 1/2 tsp baking soda
2 tbsp light soy and 1 tbsp black vinegar
50 g crispy fried soybeans and 50 g sour pickled radish, chopped
chopped coriander, spring onion and fish-mint (zheergen)
steps: Blend the soaked rice with the water until very smooth.
Dissolve the lime in a little water, add to the rice milk and cook in a pot over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 20 to 25 minutes until very thick and glossy.
Pour into an oiled tray, smooth the top and leave 2 hours to set firm.
Cut into strips or cubes, top with chili oil, soy, vinegar, soybeans, pickles and herbs, and serve cold.

ingredients: 100 g dried Guizhou chilies (Huaxi or Zunyi chaotianjiao), or a mix of mild and hot dried chilies
steps: Snip the chili stems, rinse, and soak in warm water for 30 to 60 minutes until soft and pliable; drain.
Pound the chilies with ginger, garlic and peppercorns in a large stone mortar (or pulse in a food processor) into a thick, sticky, coarse paste like glutinous rice cake (ciba).
Mix in salt and sugar.
Store in a clean jar in the fridge up to 2 weeks; fry in oil before use for chili-paste chicken, or use raw as a dip for sour fish soup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 old hen (about 1.5 kg) and 500 g pork bones, for stock
400 g fresh round rice noodles (mixian), or dried rice vermicelli soaked
150 g raw chicken breast and 100 g pork loin, sliced paper-thin
100 g raw prawns, peeled and sliced; or thin fish slices
50 g Xuanwei ham, thinly sliced, or prosciutto
100 g pea shoots, 50 g chives and bean sprouts
steps: Blanch the hen and bones, then simmer in 4 litres of water for 3 to 4 hours, skimming, until rich; season with salt.
Warm 4 large deep bowls in a hot oven or with boiling water; arrange the raw meats, prawns, quail eggs, ham, vegetables and noodles on separate small plates.
Bring the stock to a hard rolling boil, put 1 tbsp chicken fat in each hot bowl and ladle in the boiling stock so the oil forms an insulating layer — it must be near 100 C.
At the table, slide in the meats and prawns first and stir for 1 to 2 minutes until fully cooked and opaque, crack in the quail egg, then add the ham, vegetables and finally the noodles.
Season to taste with chilli oil and eat carefully as the soup stays very hot under the oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 50 g garlic chives, cut in 3 cm lengths
1 tbsp chilli oil and 1 tsp minced garlic
steps: Mix the pork with soy sauce and a splash of stock.
In a small copper or clay pot bring the stock to a boil, crumble in the pork and cook 3 minutes until fully cooked and the foam rises; skim.
Add the noodles, tomato and pickled greens and boil 2 minutes until the noodles are hot through.
Toss in the chives and cook 30 seconds, season with salt, garlic and chilli oil, and serve bubbling in the pot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 free-range chicken (about 1.3 kg), chopped into pieces
10 g sanchi (panax notoginseng) slices, optional, or 6 goji berries and 4 dried shiitake
steps: Blanch the chicken pieces 3 minutes, rinse, then pack them into a Jianshui clay steam pot (a lidded pot with a central spout) with the ginger, spring onion, wine and sanchi or shiitake; add no water.
Seat the steam pot over a pot of boiling water so steam rises through the spout, sealing the joint with a damp cloth.
Steam for 3 hours over steady high heat, topping up the lower pot with boiling water, until the steam has condensed into a clear, intensely flavoured broth and the chicken is falling off the bone.
Season with salt and serve straight from the pot. (Without a steam pot, steam the chicken in a covered bowl inside a large steamer for the same time.)
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg mixed fresh wild mushrooms from a trusted seller (porcini/jianshou jun, chanterelle/jiyou jun, morel, matsutake, or cultivated king oyster and shiitake as substitutes)
6 slices ginger and 4 cloves garlic, smashed
300 g leafy greens, tofu and rice noodles to cook in the pot
dip: 2 tbsp chopped coriander, 1 tsp chilli flakes, 2 tbsp light soy sauce
steps: Blanch the chicken, rinse, then fry it in the fat with ginger and garlic for 5 minutes and add the water; simmer 30 minutes for a light stock.
Clean the mushrooms carefully with a brush and slice them thickly; only use varieties identified as edible by a reliable seller.

Add the mushrooms to the boiling broth, season with salt, cover and cook for at least 15 to 20 minutes at a full boil — Yunnan wild mushrooms must be thoroughly cooked and should not be eaten before the timer is up.
Drink the broth first, then eat the mushrooms and chicken with the dip, and cook greens, tofu and noodles in the remaining broth.

ingredients: 1 whole tilapia or carp (about 800 g), cleaned and butterflied
4 cloves garlic, 2 shallots and 3 bird's eye chillies, minced
1 bunch sawtooth coriander (culantro) and 1 bunch coriander, chopped
1 tbsp fish sauce or light soy sauce
steps: Pound the garlic, shallots, chillies, herbs, spring onion, salt and fish sauce together into a coarse, wet stuffing.
Score the fish, rub the stuffing inside and over it, then close it up and tie it into a bundle with 2 lemongrass stalks; lay the remaining stalks along each side and tie with kitchen string.
Clamp in a fish grill basket and grill over medium charcoal for 10 to 12 minutes per side until the skin is charred and the flesh flakes easily at the backbone.
Untie, squeeze over lime and serve with sticky rice in the Dai (Xishuangbanna) style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 Erhai carp or grass carp (about 1 kg), cut into thick pieces
100 g Xuanwei ham, sliced, or prosciutto
50 g wood ear and 4 shiitake, soaked and sliced
1 piece rubing goat cheese or 50 g tofu skin, optional
1.5 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp white pepper
steps: Pat the fish dry and pan-fry it in lard over medium-high heat for 2 minutes per side until lightly golden.
Line a clay pot with the cabbage, tofu, mushrooms and ham, lay the fish on top with ginger and spring onion, and pour in the stock.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, then simmer covered for 15 to 20 minutes until the fish is cooked through and the broth tastes rich.
Season with salt and pepper and serve bubbling in the clay pot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g Yunnan erkuai (pounded rice cake slices), or Korean or Shanghai rice cake sliced thin
150 g Chinese broccoli or pea shoots, cut short
2 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp sweet soy sauce (or 1 tsp sugar)
steps: Soak the erkuai slices in warm water 10 minutes so they are pliable, then drain.
Stir-fry the pork in oil over high heat for 2 minutes until cooked through, add the garlic and pickled greens and fry 30 seconds.
Add the erkuai, tomato and soy sauces and toss for 3 to 4 minutes, splashing in a little water, until the cakes are soft and glossy.
Add the greens and stir-fry 1 minute until wilted, then serve hot. (In Kunming this is called "Da Jiu Jia", Great Rescue of the Emperor.)
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g Xuanwei ham (Yunnan dry-cured ham bought ready cured), or Jinhua ham or a thick piece of prosciutto
steps: Scrub the rind of the ham and soak the piece in warm water for 2 hours to draw out excess salt (included in prep time when soaking ahead), then drain.
Place in a bowl with the ginger, sugar and wine and steam over high heat for 45 to 60 minutes until the fat turns translucent and the meat is tender.
Cool slightly, then slice thinly across the grain and serve fanned on a plate as a cold or warm dish, or stir-fry with the chilli for 1 minute.

ingredients: 300 g Yunnan rubing (fresh pressed goat cheese, Sani and Shilin specialty), or firm paneer or halloumi
1 tbsp ground Sichuan pepper and salt mix (jiaoyan)
steps: Cut the rubing into slices 1 cm thick and pat dry.
Pan-fry over medium heat in the oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden-brown and crisp at the edges but still soft inside (rubing does not melt).
Sprinkle with the pepper-salt and chilli flakes, or with sugar for the sweet version, and serve hot.

ingredients: 800 g floury yellow potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks
2 spring onions and a handful of mint, chopped
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until completely soft, drain and lightly mash so they are broken but still chunky.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and fry the chillies, garlic and pickled greens for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and stir-fry, pressing them against the wok, for 6 to 8 minutes until golden crusty bits form.
Season with salt and Sichuan pepper, toss through spring onion and mint, and serve hot.

ingredients: 4 sheets Dali rushan (dried cow's milk "fans", a Bai specialty), or thin strips of halloumi as a loose substitute
2 tbsp rose petal jam (meigui tang) or condensed milk
steps: Wrap each rushan sheet around a chopstick or snap it in half for easy handling.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the sheets 20 to 30 seconds per side until they puff, blister and turn pale golden — do not let them burn.
Brush with rose jam or drizzle with condensed milk, sprinkle with sugar and eat immediately while crisp.

ingredients: 800 g Jianshui fermented tofu cubes, or firm tofu cut in 3 cm squares
dip 1: 2 tbsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper, 1 tsp salt
dip 2: 2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tbsp chopped coriander, 1 tsp minced garlic and 1 tbsp chilli oil
steps: If using fresh firm tofu, toss it with the salt, wrap each piece in muslin and leave in a cool place overnight so it lightly ferments and develops a soft centre (traditional Jianshui method).
Brush a charcoal grill rack with oil and grill the tofu squares over gentle coals for 10 to 15 minutes, turning, until they puff up like little pillows and the skin is golden.
Serve straight from the grill with both dips on the side, eating them one at a time and counting with corn kernels as Jianshui vendors do.

ingredients: 300 g glutinous rice (black or white), soaked 4 hours
steps: Halve the pineapple lengthwise, scoop out the flesh leaving a 1 cm shell and dice 200 g of the flesh.
Steam the drained rice over high heat for 25 minutes until just tender.
Mix the rice with diced pineapple, sugar, salt, raisins and coconut milk and pack it into the pineapple shells.
Steam the filled shells for 20 minutes until fragrant and the rice is soft and glossy; serve in the shell.

ingredients: 80 g Xuanwei ham or cured pork, finely minced (for the savoury version)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and water into a soft dough, knead 5 minutes and rest 30 minutes.
Roll into a thin large rectangle, spread with lard and scatter with ham and spring onion, then roll up tightly into a rope and coil into a snail; cut into 6 pieces.
Press each coil into a 1.5 cm thick round flatbread.

Cook in an oiled heavy pan over low heat, covered, for 12 to 15 minutes, turning every few minutes, until the layers are flaky, the outside golden and the inside cooked through; serve hot with butter tea or soy milk.

ingredients: 250 g plain flour for the water dough plus 150 g for the oil dough
80 g lard plus 75 g lard for the oil dough
200 g fresh edible rose petals (Dianhong rose), from an unsprayed source, or 150 g rose petal jam
steps: If using fresh petals, rub them with the sugar and honey until juicy and dark, then mix in the toasted rice flour to make a sticky filling.
Make a water dough from 250 g flour, 80 g lard and the water, and an oil dough from 150 g flour and 75 g lard; rest both 20 minutes.
Divide each into 12, wrap each oil-dough ball in a water-dough ball, roll out and roll up twice to create layers, then flatten and wrap around a spoon of filling, sealing well.
Flatten to 1.5 cm cakes and bake at 180 C for 20 to 25 minutes until the pastry is flaky and just golden on top; cool before eating.

ingredients: 8 g Pu'er tea, ripe (shou) or raw (sheng), broken from a cake
small teapot or gaiwan and small cups
steps: Put the tea in the pot, cover with boiling water and immediately pour it off to rinse and awaken the leaves.
Fill with boiling water (95 C for raw, 100 C for ripe) and steep 10 to 15 seconds for the first infusion, pouring all the tea into a pitcher.
Repeat 8 to 10 times, lengthening each steep by a few seconds, and serve in small cups; ripe Pu'er should taste earthy and smooth, raw Pu'er bright and slightly astringent.

ingredients: 1 whole Wenchang or free-range chicken, about 1.5 kg
4 litres water with 5 slices ginger, 2 scallions and 1 tbsp salt
3 tbsp light soy sauce and 2 tbsp of the poaching stock
steps: Bring the water with ginger, scallions and salt to a boil, dip the chicken three times, then submerge.
Simmer at the barest bubble 15 minutes, turn off the heat, cover and steep 25 minutes until the thigh reaches 75 C.
Plunge into ice water 10 minutes so the yellow skin turns firm and smooth.
Mix garlic, ginger, calamansi juice, chillies, soy and stock for the Hainan dipping sauce.
Chop and serve at room temperature with the sauce and rice cooked in chicken stock and fat.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 Jiaji (Muscovy) duck, about 2 kg (substitute any duck)
4 litres water with 5 slices ginger and 1 tbsp salt
3 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp sugar
steps: Stuff the duck with scallions, bring the water to a boil and dip the duck in and out three times.
Submerge and simmer gently 20 minutes, then cover off the heat and steep 25-30 minutes until the thigh juices run clear (75 C).
Plunge into ice water 10 minutes, then drain.
Mix garlic, calamansi, chillies, soy, sugar and a ladle of stock for the dip.
Chop and serve with the dip and steamed rice.

ingredients: 1 kg bone-in goat meat (Dongshan black goat), skin on, in large pieces
2 tbsp fermented bean curd (nam yu), mashed
1 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp light soy and 1 tbsp sesame oil
steps: Blanch the goat in boiling water with ginger and wine 5 minutes; rinse.
Simmer in fresh water with the rest of the ginger, scallions and salt 90 minutes until tender.
Drain, pat dry and either sear in hot oil 3-4 minutes per side until crisp and golden, or chop and serve plain as white-cut.
Mix nam yu, sugar, soy, sesame oil and a little goat stock as the dipping sauce.
Serve with coriander and chilli, and the goat broth as soup.

ingredients: 2 live Hele mud crabs, about 1.2 kg total (substitute any mud or Dungeness crab)
3 tbsp Zhenjiang black vinegar or rice vinegar
steps: Chill the crabs in the freezer 20 minutes to dull them and scrub them clean; tie the claws.
Steam belly-side up with the ginger slices and scallion over rapidly boiling water 15-18 minutes until the shells are bright red and the meat is opaque.
Mix the minced ginger, garlic, vinegar, soy and sugar as the dip.
Crack the claws and serve whole with the ginger vinegar; Hele crabs are prized for their full roe.

ingredients: 1 kg Wenchang or free-range chicken, chopped into small pieces
4 young green coconuts (water about 1.2 litres, plus the soft flesh, sliced)
4 garlic cloves, minced; 2 calamansi limes; 2 red chillies; 3 tbsp light soy (dip)
300 g vegetables to dip (corn, taro, lettuce, rice noodles)
steps: Pour the coconut water into a hot pot with the coconut flesh, ginger and red dates and bring to a boil.
Add the chicken, skim, and simmer 10-12 minutes until just cooked through.
Mix garlic, calamansi juice, chilli and soy for the dip.
Eat the chicken first with the dip, season the broth with salt to drink, then cook vegetables and noodles in the broth.

ingredients: 600 g fresh thin round rice noodles (Hainan fen)
200 g lean pork or beef, cooked and thinly sliced
50 g pickled sour bamboo shoots or sour mustard greens
3 tbsp roasted peanuts and 2 tbsp fried shallots
4 tbsp thick sauce: 2 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tbsp sweet potato starch, 200 ml stock, simmered thick
1 tbsp garlic oil and Hainan yellow chilli sauce
steps: Simmer the thick sauce ingredients 2-3 minutes until glossy like gravy.
Blanch the noodles 30 seconds and drain.
Toss the noodles with garlic oil and the thick sauce.
Top with meat, bean sprouts, pickles, peanuts, shallots and sesame, and serve with yellow chilli sauce and a cup of clear soup.
