ingredients: 600 g thick round rice noodles (baoluo fen)
100 g pickled sour bamboo shoots or sour mustard greens
3 tbsp roasted peanuts and 2 tbsp fried shallots
1 tsp salt, chilli sauce and coriander
steps: Blanch the bones and beef, then simmer with ginger and star anise 2 hours until the broth is rich; slice the beef.
Season the broth with salt and keep at a rolling boil.
Blanch the noodles 1 minute until soft and slippery, and divide between bowls.
Top with beef, braised pork, pickles, peanuts and shallots, ladle over boiling broth and finish with coriander and chilli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 mature coconuts with a lid cut off (water reserved)
200 ml coconut water or coconut milk
steps: Drain the rice and mix with sugar, salt and enough coconut water to come just below the rice level.
Fill each coconut two-thirds full with the rice mix and replace the lid.
Stand the coconuts upright in a steamer and steam over high heat 60 minutes until the rice is soft and has soaked up the coconut flavour.
Cut the coconuts into wedges so each piece has rice attached to the white flesh, and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 50 g red beans and 50 g mung beans, soaked 2 hours
50 g lotus seeds and 20 g dried longan
50 g sago pearls or tapioca jelly
steps: Simmer the red beans, mung beans, barley and lotus seeds separately in water 30-45 minutes until tender but whole.
Boil the sago 10 minutes until translucent and rinse in cold water.
Dissolve rock sugar in 200 ml hot water to make syrup and cool.
Fill glasses with the beans, barley, lotus seeds, longan, sago and fruit, add crushed ice, syrup and coconut milk.
Serve ice-cold as the classic Haikou street dessert.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g pork tenderloin, sliced 5 mm thick into large thin pieces
1/2 tsp salt and 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
150 g potato starch soaked in 150 ml water until it settles (pour off the clear water to use the wet starch)
4 tbsp sugar and 4 tbsp white rice vinegar
1 small carrot and 1 thumb ginger, finely julienned
2 spring onions, julienned, and a few coriander sprigs
steps: Marinate the pork slices with salt and wine for 10 minutes, then coat each slice thickly in the wet potato starch.
Heat the oil to 170 C and fry the slices a few at a time for 2 to 3 minutes until set and pale, then remove; raise the oil to 190 C and fry again for 1 minute until golden and very crisp.
Mix the sugar, vinegar, soy sauce and 2 tbsp water in a wok and bubble over medium heat for 1 minute until syrupy; add the carrot, ginger and spring onion.
Toss the crisp pork in the sauce for 10 seconds until coated, scatter with coriander and serve immediately while it crackles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges
2 green bell peppers, torn into pieces
2 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp dark soy sauce
1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 100 ml water
steps: Fry the potato wedges in hot oil (170 C) for 6 to 7 minutes until golden and cooked through; remove.
Toss the eggplant in a dusting of cornflour and fry 3 minutes until golden and soft; fry the peppers 20 seconds; drain.
Leave 1 tbsp oil in the wok, fry the garlic 15 seconds, then add the soy sauces, sugar, salt and the cornflour water and simmer until glossy.
Return all the vegetables, toss over high heat for 1 minute until coated, and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g skin-on pork belly in one piece
600 g Dongbei suancai (fermented napa cabbage), or rinsed German sauerkraut
4 slices ginger, 2 spring onions, 1 star anise
1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp white pepper
dip: 2 tbsp fermented bean curd, 1 tbsp garlic paste, 1 tbsp chilli oil, 1 tsp sesame oil
steps: Simmer the pork belly with ginger, spring onion and star anise in 2 litres of water for 40 minutes until cooked through; remove, cool and slice thinly, reserving the stock.
Rinse the suancai, squeeze dry and shred very finely; fry it in lard for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the suancai to the stock and simmer 30 minutes until the broth is pleasantly sour.
Lay the pork slices on top, add the vermicelli and simmer 10 minutes until the noodles are soft; season with salt and pepper.
Serve in the pot with the bean curd and garlic dip on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pork Stewed with Vermicelli (Zhurou Dun Fentiao)

ingredients: 600 g pork belly or ribs, cut into chunks
150 g sweet potato vermicelli (fentiao), soaked 30 minutes
3 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp dark soy sauce
1 tbsp Dongbei soybean paste (dajiang) or yellow bean paste
steps: Blanch the pork 3 minutes and drain.
Melt the sugar in the oil over medium heat until amber, add the pork and stir to coat, then add the ginger, star anise, spring onion and soybean paste and fry 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauces and water to cover by 3 cm and simmer covered for 50 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the vermicelli and simmer 10 to 15 minutes until it has soaked up most of the sauce and is soft and slippery; season with salt and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Chicken Stewed with Mushrooms (Xiaoji Dun Mogu)

ingredients: 1 young free-range chicken (about 1.2 kg), chopped into pieces
80 g dried hazel mushrooms (zhenmo), or dried shiitake and oyster mushrooms, soaked 30 minutes
4 slices ginger, 3 cloves garlic, 2 star anise
2 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp dark soy sauce
steps: Blanch the chicken 3 minutes and drain; rinse the soaked mushrooms several times to remove grit, reserving the clean soaking water.
Fry the ginger, garlic and star anise in oil, add the chicken and stir-fry over high heat for 5 minutes until browned.
Add the wine, soy sauces, sugar and enough water plus mushroom water to cover, bring to a boil and add the mushrooms.

Simmer covered for 45 minutes until the chicken is very tender and the mushrooms have absorbed the sauce; reduce for a few minutes, season and garnish with spring onion. (Traditionally the stew is served with corn flatbreads stuck to the side of the pot.)
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g green beans, broken in half
200 g napa cabbage, cut in pieces
2 tbsp Dongbei soybean paste (dajiang) and 2 tbsp light soy sauce
3 cloves garlic, 2 slices ginger, 2 spring onions
2 tbsp neutral oil and 1 tsp salt
steps: Fry the pork in oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until the fat renders, add the garlic, ginger, spring onion and soybean paste and fry 1 minute.
Add the green beans, potatoes and corn, stir to coat and pour in water to come halfway up the vegetables.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes, then add the eggplant, tomato and cabbage and cook 12 to 15 minutes more until everything is soft and the green beans are fully cooked (no longer squeaky).
Season with soy sauce and salt and serve in a big bowl with rice or steamed buns.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg pork ribs or goose pieces, cut in chunks
2 potatoes and 1 corn cob, cut in chunks
3 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp sugar
3 star anise, 6 slices ginger, 4 spring onions
300 g plain cornmeal and 200 g plain flour mixed with 300 ml warm water, for the pot-side flatbreads (tiebingzi)
steps: Blanch the meat and drain; in a large cast-iron pot fry it in oil with the ginger, star anise, spring onion and soybean paste for 5 minutes.
Add soy sauce, sugar and water to cover, and simmer covered for 40 minutes.
Add the potatoes, corn and green beans and simmer 10 minutes more.

Shape the cornmeal dough into palm-sized ovals and press them onto the hot inside walls of the pot above the liquid; add the vermicelli, cover tightly and cook 20 minutes until the flatbreads are cooked through with crisp bottoms and the beans are tender.
Serve straight from the iron pot at the table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg pork spine bones (dagu) with plenty of meat
3 tbsp light soy sauce and 2 tbsp dark soy sauce
3 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 bay leaves, 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns, 2 dried chillies
disposable gloves and straws for the marrow
steps: Soak the bones in cold water for 2 hours, changing it twice, to draw out blood; blanch 5 minutes and rinse.
In a large pot combine the bones with all seasonings and water to cover, bring to a boil and skim.
Simmer gently, covered, for 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat falls from the bones and the sauce is dark and fragrant.
Serve piled high in a bowl with gloves for picking off the meat, and straws for sucking out the marrow.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 egg white and 2 tbsp potato starch
2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar
1 tsp cornflour mixed with 50 ml water
steps: Coat the pork in egg white and starch and fry in oil at 170 C for 1.5 minutes until just cooked and lightly golden; drain.
Leave 1 tbsp oil in the wok and fry the garlic, wood ear and carrot over high heat for 1 minute, then add the cucumber.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and cornflour water, stir until glossy, then return the pork and toss for 30 seconds until coated and heated through; serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g wide sweet potato or mung bean sheet noodles (fenpi), soaked
2 eggs, made into a thin omelette and shredded
1 cucumber, 1 carrot and 1/4 purple cabbage, julienned
3 tbsp sesame paste loosened with 3 tbsp water
3 cloves garlic, minced, 2 tbsp black vinegar, 2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar
1 tbsp chilli oil and 1 tbsp neutral oil
steps: Stir-fry the pork in oil over high heat with 1 tsp soy sauce for 2 minutes until cooked through.
Blanch the sheet noodles 1 minute, refresh in cold water and drain well.
Arrange the noodles in the centre of a large platter with neat piles of cucumber, carrot, cabbage, sprouts, egg, coriander and the hot pork around them.
Mix the sesame paste, garlic, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar and chilli oil, pour over at the table and toss everything together.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Dipping Vegetables with Soybean Paste (Dajiang Zhan Cai)

ingredients: 100 g Dongbei fermented soybean paste (dajiang), or Korean doenjang
1 bunch spring onions or Chinese green onions (dacong), whole
1 bunch radishes and a few mild green chillies
steps: Heat the oil in a pan over low heat, fry the chopped spring onion 30 seconds, then add the soybean paste, sugar and 3 tbsp water.
Stir constantly for 5 to 8 minutes until the paste darkens slightly and becomes glossy and fragrant; cool.
Wash and dry the raw vegetables and arrange them on a platter with the bowl of paste for dipping, eating them by hand alongside rice or corn porridge.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg pork shoulder (lean) and 200 g pork back fat
2 m pork or natural sausage casings, soaked
18 g salt and 1 tsp curing salt (Prague powder no.1), measured exactly
1 tsp ground coriander and 1 tsp black pepper
1/2 tsp red food colouring or 1 tbsp paprika, optional
hardwood chips and 2 tbsp sugar for smoking
steps: Dice the lean pork, mix with the salt, curing salt and sugar, and chill 1 hour; dice the fat into 5 mm cubes.
Mince the pork coarsely, then mix in the fat, starch, garlic, spices, colouring and 100 ml ice water until sticky.
Stuff loosely into the casings, twist into 20 cm links and prick any air bubbles.
Hang in a 70 C oven for 30 minutes to dry, then poach in 80 C water for 30 to 35 minutes until the internal temperature reaches 71 C.
Smoke over smouldering hardwood chips and sugar for 15 minutes until reddish-brown, cool and slice to eat cold with Dalieba bread and beer, the way it is served in Harbin.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 litre fresh pork blood from a butcher, with anticoagulant salt added at slaughter
2 m cleaned pork small intestine casings
1 tsp ground Sichuan pepper and 1/2 tsp five-spice
2 spring onions and 1 thumb ginger, minced
steps: Strain the blood, then mix it with the cooled stock, fat, salt, spices, spring onion, ginger and sesame oil.
Tie one end of the casing, funnel in the blood mixture until two-thirds full, and tie off in 30 cm links.
Lower into water held just below a simmer (about 85 C) and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, pricking with a needle to release air; it is done when no red liquid comes out of the pinpricks.
Lift out, slice into rounds and serve in suancai and pork stew or with a garlic soy dip.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g Dongbei suancai (fermented napa cabbage), or rinsed sauerkraut
2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp five-spice
1 tbsp grated ginger and 3 spring onions, minced
3 tbsp neutral oil and 1 tbsp sesame oil
500 g plain flour mixed with 250 ml water
black vinegar and garlic for dipping
steps: Rinse the suancai, chop finely and squeeze out as much water as possible.
Mix the pork with soy sauce, salt, five-spice, ginger and 4 tbsp water until sticky, then fold in the suancai, spring onion and both oils.
Rest the dough 20 minutes, roll into ropes, cut into 50 pieces and roll each into an 8 cm wrapper; fill and pinch into crescent dumplings.
Boil in batches in a large pot, adding a cup of cold water each time it returns to the boil, three times, about 8 minutes in all, until the dumplings float and the filling is cooked through.
Serve with black vinegar and crushed garlic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g lard, melted, and 200 ml hot pork bone stock
200 ml pork bone stock, cooled, beaten in for the filling
300 g Chinese cabbage or zucchini, finely chopped, salted and squeezed
2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp ground Sichuan pepper
1 tbsp grated ginger and 2 spring onions, minced
steps: Stir the hot stock and melted lard into the flour to make a soft, scalded dough (the Laobian "tangmian" method), knead smooth and rest 30 minutes.
Beat the cooled stock into the pork a little at a time until absorbed, then mix in the seasonings and finally the vegetable and sesame oil.
Divide the dough into 40 pieces, roll into wrappers, fill and pleat closed.
Steam over high heat for 12 to 15 minutes until the wrappers are translucent and the filling cooked through, or pan-fry the bottoms after steaming; serve hot with vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 sheets ready-made kaolengmian sheets (dried cold noodle sheets from Chinese grocers), or 2 large thin wheat tortillas
2 tbsp sweet bean sauce mixed with 1 tbsp chilli sauce and 1 tsp sugar
2 spring onions and a handful of coriander, chopped
steps: Heat a griddle or large flat pan over medium heat with 1 tbsp oil and lay a noodle sheet on it, sprinkling a little water to soften it.
Crack an egg on top, break the yolk and spread it over the sheet; flip once the egg sets, about 1 minute, then flip back.
Brush with the bean-chilli sauce, sprinkle with onion, spring onion, coriander and a splash of vinegar, and cook 1 minute more.
Roll or fold the sheet into a log, cut into pieces and serve hot in a paper tray. (Vegetarian/egg version; omit sausage often added by vendors.)
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix 300 g flour with the starter and 300 ml water and leave covered overnight (about 12 hours) until bubbly and sour-smelling.
Add the remaining flour, water, salt, sugar and yeast, knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, and rise 1.5 hours until doubled.
Shape into one very large round loaf (or two), place on an oiled tray and prove 1 hour.
Score the top and bake at 220 C with a tray of water in the oven for 15 minutes, then at 190 C for 40 to 45 minutes until deep brown and hollow when tapped.
Cool completely and slice thickly with hongchang sausage; the crust is chewy and the crumb mildly sour.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g yellow glutinous millet flour (dahuangmi) or glutinous rice flour
250 g red adzuki beans, soaked overnight
corn husks or baking paper squares
steps: Simmer the soaked beans in water for 1 hour until very soft, drain, and mash with the sugar and oil over low heat until a thick paste forms; cool and roll into balls.
Mix the flour, yeast and warm water into a soft dough and leave in a warm place for 2 to 3 hours until slightly sour and puffy.
Wet your hands, flatten a portion of dough, wrap a bean ball inside and roll smooth; place each bun on a corn husk.
Steam over high heat for 20 to 25 minutes until golden, glossy and chewy; eat warm, or freeze them outdoors in winter as Dongbei families do and steam again to serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 Qiuzi or other hard autumn pears (or Bosc pears)
steps: Freeze the whole pears outdoors in Dongbei winter or in a freezer for at least 24 hours until they turn black and rock-hard.
To eat, submerge them in a bowl of cold water for 20 to 30 minutes; a shell of ice forms on the outside as the pear thaws from within.
Crack off the ice and check the pear is soft all the way through; if not, soak 10 minutes more.
Bite a small hole and suck out the icy, sweet-tart juice, then eat the soft flesh; it is a traditional Spring Festival treat and cure for greasy food.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Simmer the beef in the water with a little salt over low heat for 1.5–2 hours until tender, skim the scum, then cool the meat and slice it thin.
Strain the broth, season it with vinegar, sugar and soy sauce, then chill it in the fridge or over ice until very cold (a thin crust of ice is traditional).
Boil the noodles for 3–4 minutes until chewy, rinse hard under cold water and squeeze dry; buckwheat-starch noodles are the Yanbian norm, Korean naengmyeon is the closest substitute.
Place a nest of noodles in each bowl, ladle in the icy broth, then top with sliced beef, pear, cucumber, kimchi, half an egg and sesame seeds.
Serve immediately with extra vinegar and mustard or chilli paste on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g fernbrake (gosari) or shiitake, soaked and sliced
steps: Stir-fry the beef with soy sauce and a little sesame oil over high heat for 5 minutes until browned and fully cooked.
Blanch the bean sprouts for 3 minutes and the spinach for 30 seconds, squeeze dry and season each with sesame oil and salt; quickly sauté the carrot and fernbrake separately for 2 minutes each.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in a lightly oiled pan until the whites are set.
Divide hot rice into bowls (stone bowls heated on the stove for 5 minutes give a crisp crust), arrange the vegetables and beef in sections, and top with an egg.
Add a spoon of gochujang and a drizzle of sesame oil, and mix everything together at the table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp fish sauce or salted shrimp (saeujeot)
2 tbsp glutinous rice flour cooked into 150 ml paste
4 spring onions, cut in 3 cm lengths
steps: Sprinkle salt between the cabbage leaves and leave for 6–8 hours, turning once, until the leaves bend without snapping.
Rinse the cabbage three times in cold water and drain cut-side down for 1 hour.
Mix the cooled rice paste with chilli flakes, garlic, ginger, fish sauce and sugar, then fold in the radish and spring onions.
Wearing gloves, smear the paste between every leaf, fold each quarter and pack tightly into a clean jar, pressing out air.
Leave at room temperature for 1–2 days until it smells pleasantly sour, then refrigerate; it is best after a week and keeps for months.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 m cleaned pork casings, soaked in salted water
500 ml fresh pork blood (from a licensed butcher)
100 g sweet potato glass noodles (dangmyeon), soaked and chopped
100 g napa cabbage, blanched and chopped
steps: Steam the soaked glutinous rice for 20 minutes until half-cooked, then cool.
Mix the rice, noodles, pork fat, cabbage, spring onion, garlic, pepper and salt, then stir in the blood to make a loose filling.
Tie one end of the casing, funnel in the filling until two-thirds full, and tie into 20 cm links, leaving room for expansion.
Simmer the sausages in barely bubbling water for 40–50 minutes, pricking any air bubbles, until firm and no red liquid shows when pierced (internal 72°C).
Rest 10 minutes, slice thick and serve warm with salt mixed with chilli powder and some kimchi.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Drain the soaked rice, mix in the salt and steam it over a cloth for 35–40 minutes until completely soft and translucent.
Tip the hot rice onto a wet board or into a stand mixer and pound with a wet wooden mallet (dagao means "beaten cake") for 10–15 minutes until smooth and stretchy.
Mix the soybean flour with the sugar and spread half on a tray.
Press the pounded rice onto the tray, cover with the remaining flour and cut into bite-sized pieces with a floured knife.
Serve the same day, ideally still slightly warm, with honey or extra sugar on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole young lamb, 12–15 kg, cleaned (from a butcher)
4 tbsp wheat flour mixed with 2 egg yolks for glaze
steps: Score the thick parts of the lamb and rub inside and out with salt, Sichuan pepper, cumin and grated onion mixed with water; marinate in a cool place overnight.
Brush the outside with the egg-flour glaze so the skin turns a lacquered gold.
Hang or spit-roast the lamb in a large wood or charcoal oven at about 180°C for 3–4 hours, turning or rotating so it colours evenly, until the thigh reaches 70°C and juices run clear.
Brush with sesame oil for the last 15 minutes to crisp the skin.
Present the whole lamb at the table, carve it in front of guests and serve with salt, chilli and cumin dips and milk tea, in Mongolian banquet style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 kg bone-in lamb ribs and leg, cut into large chunks
3 tbsp light soy sauce for dip
steps: Soak the lamb in cold water for 1 hour to draw out blood, then place in a pot with fresh cold water.
Bring to the boil, skim off all the foam, then add onion and ginger.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for 60–75 minutes until the meat is tender but still firmly attached to the bone; add salt in the last 15 minutes.
Mix the garlic, soy sauce and chilli oil into a dip.
Lift the lamb onto a large platter and eat by hand, cutting meat off the bone with a small knife, with the dip and a bowl of the hot broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix flour and hot water into a firm dough, rest 30 minutes, then roll into a log and cut into 30 pieces.
Stir the lamb with soy sauce, salt, pepper and ginger in one direction, adding the cold water gradually until sticky, then fold in the spring onion.
Dust each dough piece with cornstarch and roll very thin, then press the edges with a rolling pin to make ruffled "flower petal" wrappers.
Place a spoon of filling in the centre and gather the wrapper loosely so the top stays open like a pouch.
Steam over high heat for 10–12 minutes until the wrappers are translucent and the lamb is cooked, and serve with brick tea and vinegar, as Hohhot breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg lean beef round, cut into finger-thick strips along the grain
steps: Toss the beef strips with salt, soy sauce and spices and marinate in the fridge overnight.
Hang the strips in a cool, dry, airy place (or on racks in front of a fan in a fridge) for 2–4 days until firm and dark on the outside.
For safety, finish by baking the strips at 120°C for 25–30 minutes, or steaming for 30 minutes, until the meat is fully cooked through.
Cool, then tear into thin shreds along the grain.
Store sealed in a cool place and eat as a chewy snack with milk tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 litres whole milk (cow, traditionally also mare or goat)
500 ml plain yogurt or soured milk
steps: Leave the milk with the yogurt at warm room temperature for 4–6 hours until it sours and thickens slightly, then skim off any cream.
Heat over low heat, stirring, until the curds separate from the yellowish whey, about 15 minutes.
Drain off the whey, then knead the curds in the pot over low heat for 15–20 minutes until they turn smooth and stretchy; add sugar now if you like.
Press the hot curd firmly into a wooden mould or dish and let it set for 2 hours.
Unmould, slice and serve fresh, or dry the slices on racks for several days to make hard milk tofu for snacking with milk tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 tbsp ghee or clarified butter (shar tos)
500 ml hot milk tea or milk to serve
steps: Soak the millet overnight, then steam or boil for 10 minutes until the grains just swell, and drain well.
Toast the millet in a dry heavy pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 15–20 minutes until crisp, dry and golden-brown with a nutty smell.
Cool completely and store in an airtight jar; it keeps for months.
To serve, put a handful of chaomi in a bowl with a spoon of ghee and sugar, then pour hot milk tea over and eat as it softens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil the water with the tea for 5 minutes until deep orange; loose black tea is a substitute for brick tea.
Strain out the leaves and return the tea to the pot.
Pour in the milk and use a ladle to scoop and pour the tea from height repeatedly for 2–3 minutes while it returns to a simmer, to aerate it.
Season with salt, add butter if using, and serve hot in bowls with fried millet, milk tofu or air-dried beef.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 litre kumis (airag), bought from a licensed producer
100 g dried milk tofu or air-dried beef to accompany
steps: Kumis is mare's milk naturally fermented in leather bags; it is tangy, faintly fizzy and lightly alcoholic (usually 1–3% ABV), so buy it ready-made from a licensed dairy or producer rather than making it.
Chill it lightly and shake or stir before pouring, since it separates as it stands.
Serve in small bowls offered with both hands, traditionally to guests on arrival or at the Naadam summer festival, with dairy snacks or dried beef.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg beef shank plus 500 g beef bones
1 tsp each star anise, Sichuan peppercorn, fennel seed, cumin and 2 bay leaves (in a spice bag)
270 ml water with 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp penghui (alkaline ash water) or 1 tsp baked baking soda
1 handful coriander and garlic chives, chopped
steps: Soak the beef and bones in cold water for 1 hour, then simmer in fresh water with the spice bag and ginger for 2.5–3 hours, skimming often, until the broth is clear and fragrant; remove the beef, cool and slice thin.
Add the radish to the broth for the last 20 minutes and season with salt.
Knead the flour with the alkaline salted water into a smooth dough, rest 1 hour, then roll into ropes, oil them and pull by hand into thin noodles (or use fresh alkaline ramen noodles).
Boil the noodles for 1–2 minutes until just tender and lift into bowls.
Ladle over the hot clear broth, top with beef slices and radish, then add the "red" chilli oil and "green" coriander and garlic chives, and serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 garlic cloves, mashed with 3 tbsp water
1 tbsp sesame paste thinned with water
steps: Knead the flour and 300 ml water into a dough, rest 30 minutes, then knead it in a bowl of water until the water turns milky; repeat until only a lump of gluten remains.
Steam the gluten lump for 20 minutes and cut into cubes; let the starch water settle for 2 hours, pour off the clear top and stir the baking soda into the starch batter.
Pour a thin layer of batter into an oiled tray, steam over boiling water for 2–3 minutes until it bubbles and turns translucent, cool the tray in cold water, peel the sheet and repeat.
Cut the sheets into wide ribbons and toss with the gluten cubes, cucumber, vinegar, soy sauce, garlic water, sesame paste and chilli oil.
Serve cold as a summer lunch or snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml jiangshui (fermented vegetable starter water from celery or cabbage)
steps: To start jiangshui, blanch celery, pack it in a clean jar, cover with cooled noodle-cooking water and a spoon of old jiangshui (or a little plain yogurt whey), and leave 2–3 days until pleasantly sour.
Heat the oil until shimmering, fry the dried chillies and onion for 1 minute, then pour in the jiangshui with some of the soured celery; it should sizzle loudly.
Bring to a brief boil, season with salt and let it cool.
Boil the noodles for 2–3 minutes, rinse in cold water and drain.
Serve the noodles in bowls topped with the cool sour broth, celery and a little chilli oil, as a refreshing summer dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g lamb or beef, thinly sliced
steps: Knead the flour and salted water into a soft dough, rest 30 minutes, roll into flat strips and oil them.
Stir-fry the meat in hot oil for 3 minutes until browned, add tomato, potato and pepper and fry 3 minutes more, then add soy sauce.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil and simmer 8 minutes until the potato is tender.
Stretch each dough strip and pinch off thumbnail-sized pieces straight into the boiling soup; cook 3 minutes until they float and are tender.
Season with salt and vinegar and serve hot with chilli oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 kg lamb ribs and leg, bone-in, from Tan sheep if possible
steps: Soak the lamb in cold water for 1 hour, then put it in a pot of cold water and bring slowly to the boil, skimming thoroughly.
Add ginger and Sichuan pepper and simmer gently for 1–1.5 hours until tender but still on the bone; add salt in the last 20 minutes.
Mix a dip of salt, chilli powder and cumin, and a second one of garlic in a little broth and vinegar.
Lift the lamb onto a platter, cut between the ribs, and eat by hand with the dips, raw garlic and a bowl of broth, in Hui halal tradition.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix flour, yeast, soda, sugar and salt, then knead with warm water and honey into a soft dough; cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 12 pieces and roll each into a round 1 cm thick; make two small slits in the centre.
Heat the oil to 170°C and fry each round for 2–3 minutes per side until puffed and golden-brown.
Drain on paper and serve warm; youxiang is made for Eid, weddings and family gatherings among Hui Muslims, served with tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g dried pea beans (wandou) or dried green peas
1 tsp penghui (alkaline ash) or 1/2 tsp baking soda
steps: Soak the peas overnight and drain.
Simmer the peas in fresh water with the alkali for 1 hour; the alkali turns them grey-brown and soft.
Add the dates and rock sugar and simmer 20–30 minutes more, stirring, until the peas break down into a thick sweet soup.
Stir in osmanthus syrup if using and serve hot in winter or chilled in summer, as a Lanzhou street sweet.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp plain live yogurt as starter
steps: Bring the milk to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes and stir in the sugar.
Cool to 42°C, stir in the starter and pour into small bowls.
Cover with a cloth and keep in a warm place (40–45°C oven with light on) for 6–8 hours until set firm with a thick skin on top.
Chill 2 hours and serve sprinkled with sugar; it should be thick enough to hold an upturned spoon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tsp green tea (traditionally spring green tea)
steps: Divide the ingredients between two lidded gaiwan tea bowls (the Hui "three-piece" sanpaotai set).
Pour in boiling water, cover and steep for 5 minutes.
Sip by tilting the lid to strain, and keep refilling with hot water; the tea grows sweeter as the dates and rock sugar dissolve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 ml butter tea or salted milk tea
steps: If you can't buy tsampa, toast barley flour in a dry pan over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until golden and nutty.
Put a little hot butter tea in a bowl with the butter, then heap the tsampa on top.
Stir with a finger while turning the bowl, adding cheese and sugar, then knead into a dough ball (pa) with your hand.
Eat the pa in bites with the remaining butter tea, as a Tibetan breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g minced yak or beef with some fat
steps: Knead flour and water into a firm dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the meat with onion, ginger, garlic, coriander, soy sauce, salt and water until juicy.
Roll small rounds of dough thin at the edges, place a spoon of filling in the centre and pleat into round or crescent shapes.
Steam on oiled racks over high heat for 12–15 minutes until the wrappers are glossy and the filling is cooked through.
Serve hot with tomato-chilli sauce (sepen) and a bowl of broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g yak or beef, thinly sliced
steps: Fry the onion in oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, add garlic, ginger and tomato and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Add the meat and stir-fry 3 minutes until browned, then pour in the broth and simmer 20 minutes until tender.
Add the noodles and cook 3–4 minutes, then the greens for the last minute.
Season with salt and serve hot with chilli sauce on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g lamb or yak, thinly sliced
3 garlic cloves and 15 g ginger, minced
steps: Knead flour and water into a smooth dough, rest 30 minutes, then roll into long oiled flat strips.
Fry the meat in oil 3 minutes, add onion, garlic, ginger, tomato and radish and cook 5 minutes.
Pour in the broth and simmer 15 minutes.
Stretch each strip thin and pinch off pieces straight into the boiling soup ("then" = pull, "thuk" = noodle); cook 3 minutes until they float.
Add spinach, season with salt and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 15 g ginger and 2 garlic cloves, minced
steps: Knead flour and water into a firm dough and rest 20 minutes.
Mix the meat with onion, cabbage, ginger, garlic, soy sauce and salt.
Roll the dough into 10 cm rounds, top one round with filling, cover with another and crimp the edges (or fold into half-moons).
Fry in oil at 170°C for 4–5 minutes per side until golden and the filling is cooked through.
Drain and serve hot with chilli sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg lean yak or beef, cut into long strips
steps: Rub the strips with salt, chilli and pepper and marinate in the fridge overnight.
Hang in a cold, dry, windy place or a fridge with a fan for 3–5 days until dark and hard, as Tibetans dry meat in the cold highland winter.
For safety, bake the strips at 120°C for 25–30 minutes until cooked through, then cool.
Tear into pieces and eat as a snack, or crumble into chilli sauce and tsampa.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml fresh sheep or yak blood (from a licensed butcher)
200 g lamb fat or minced lamb
steps: Mix the blood with lamb, tsampa, garlic, pepper and salt into a loose filling.
Tie one end of the casing, funnel in the filling until two-thirds full and tie off in links.
Simmer in barely bubbling water for 40–45 minutes, pricking air bubbles, until firm and no red liquid shows (internal 72°C).
Slice and serve warm, or cool and pan-fry in slices, with chilli sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 80 g droma (small wild sweet potato-like roots) or 100 g raisins
steps: Cook the rice in the water, covered, on low heat for 15 minutes until tender, then fluff.
Boil the droma for 10 minutes if using (dried raisins and dates are a common substitute).
Melt the butter in a pan, add the rice, sugar, droma, raisins, dates and cashews and stir 5 minutes until glossy.
Serve warm at Losar (Tibetan New Year) and celebrations, often with a spoon of yogurt.

ingredients: 3 garlic cloves, mashed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Whisk the starch with 300 ml water until smooth; boil the remaining 600 ml water with the turmeric.
Pour the slurry into the boiling water, whisking constantly, and cook 5 minutes until thick and translucent.
Pour into an oiled dish and cool for 2 hours until set firm.
Cut into thick strips and toss with chilli oil, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic water and spring onion; serve cold as street food.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 litre yak or full-fat cow milk
3 tbsp plain live yogurt as starter
steps: Boil the milk for 5 minutes and cool to about 42°C.
Stir in the starter, cover and keep warm (wrapped in a blanket or in a 40°C oven) for 6–8 hours until set thick.
Chill and serve with sugar, often with tsampa or droma dresil; the Shoton (Yogurt) Festival in Lhasa celebrates it each summer.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 15 g Tibetan brick tea (pu-erh or strong black tea as substitute)
3 tbsp yak butter or unsalted butter
steps: Boil the tea in the water for 10 minutes until very dark, then strain.
Pour the hot tea into a churn (chandong) or blender with the butter, salt and milk.
Churn or blend for 1–2 minutes until creamy and emulsified.
Reheat gently without boiling and serve in small bowls, topping up the guest's bowl after every sip.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil the water with the tea for 5 minutes until strong.
Add the milk and sugar and bring back to a gentle boil, stirring.
Strain into a flask and serve hot, as in Lhasa's sweet tea houses, with a bowl of noodles or momo.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 litre chang, bought from a licensed producer
1 bowl tsampa or dried yak meat to accompany
steps: Chang is a mild, cloudy, slightly sweet-sour Tibetan beer brewed from highland barley; buy it from licensed producers rather than brewing it at home.
Serve at room temperature or warmed in winter, poured into small bowls.
It is offered at Losar, weddings and festivals in three sips: the host refills after each sip and the guest finishes the bowl on the third, while dabbing a drop to the air as an offering.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g bone-in lamb, cut into large pieces
120 ml vegetable oil or lamb fat
800 g yellow carrots, cut into thick matchsticks (orange carrots as substitute)
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot (kazan) until very hot, brown the lamb on all sides for 8 minutes, then add the onion and fry 5 minutes until golden.
Add the carrots, cumin and salt and stir-fry 5 minutes until the carrots soften.
Add hot water to just cover and simmer 20 minutes until the lamb is nearly tender.
Spread the drained rice evenly over the top without stirring, add raisins, and add water to come 1 cm above the rice.

Cook on medium until the water is absorbed, then poke a few holes, cover tightly and steam on the lowest heat for 30 minutes; mound on a platter with the lamb on top and serve with achchiq-chuchuk salad.

ingredients: 100 g green beans or celery, cut short
steps: Knead the flour and salted water into a smooth soft dough, rest 30 minutes, roll into finger-thick ropes, coat in oil and rest another 30 minutes.
Stretch the ropes by hand, wrapping and pulling them into long thin noodles; boil 2–3 minutes and rinse in cold water.

Stir-fry the lamb in hot oil for 3 minutes, add onion, garlic and tomato paste and fry 2 minutes, then add peppers, beans and tomatoes with 150 ml water and cook 5 minutes into a saucy topping (leghmen säy).
Season with salt, pile the noodles on plates and spoon the topping over, with black vinegar and garlic on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Make the dough as for laghman, roll into oiled ropes, stretch thin and break into 2 cm pieces.
Boil the pieces 2 minutes, rinse in cold water and drain.
Stir-fry the lamb in hot oil 3 minutes, add onion, garlic and peppers and cook 2 minutes, then tomato and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Add the noodle pieces and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes until coated and lightly charred; season with salt and serve with vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg chicken, chopped into bone-in pieces
30 g ginger and 6 garlic cloves, sliced
2 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp dark soy sauce
steps: Heat the oil, fry chillies, Sichuan pepper and star anise for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the chicken and stir-fry over high heat 8 minutes until browned.
Add ginger, garlic, soy sauces and sugar, then 700 ml water, and simmer covered 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook 15 minutes until tender and the chicken is cooked through, then add peppers for 3 minutes.
Boil the wide noodles 3 minutes and lay them on a large platter.
Pour the chicken and its plentiful sauce over the noodles and serve family-style.

ingredients: 1 whole lamb leg and shoulder (4–5 kg) or half a young lamb
steps: Score the meat deeply and rub with salt, cumin, chilli and grated onion; marinate in the fridge overnight.
Whisk the egg yolks, flour and turmeric into a thick paste and brush all over the lamb.
Hang the lamb on a hook inside a hot clay tonur (or roast on a rack in a 180°C oven), seal, and roast for 2.5–3 hours until the crust is golden and the thickest part reaches 70°C.
Rest 15 minutes and carve, serving with fresh nan and onion salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g lamb leg, cut into 2 cm cubes
150 g lamb tail fat, cut into small cubes (or fattier shoulder)
steps: Mix the lamb with grated onion, salt and egg white and marinate 1 hour.
Thread onto metal or red willow skewers, alternating 4 pieces of lean with 1 piece of fat.
Grill over hot charcoal for 8–10 minutes, turning often, until the fat sizzles and the meat is browned and cooked through.
Sprinkle generously with cumin and chilli in the last 2 minutes and serve with nan.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp butter or lamb fat, softened
100 g lamb tail fat, finely diced
steps: Knead flour and salted water into a firm dough, rest 30 minutes, roll thin, spread with soft fat, roll up tightly and cut into 12 pieces.
Mix the lamb, fat, onion, cumin, pepper and salt.
Roll each piece into a square, add filling and fold into a parcel; brush with yolk.
Bake in a very hot tonur or at 220°C for 20–25 minutes until deeply golden and the filling is cooked through, and serve hot with tea.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Knead flour and water into a soft dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb with onion, cumin, pepper, salt and water.
Wrap the filling in rounds of dough like a dumpling, pinch closed and flatten into 2 cm thick discs.
Pan-fry in oil over medium-low heat, covered, for 6–8 minutes per side until crisp, golden and cooked through; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g lamb, finely diced by hand
steps: Knead flour and water into a firm dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb, fat, onion and spices.
Roll thin rounds of about 12 cm, place filling in the centre and pinch the edges up into a pleated, slightly open top.
Steam over high heat for 20–25 minutes until the meat is cooked through and the juices bubble; serve with black vinegar and chilli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Knead flour and water into a firm dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb with onion, pepper and salt.
Roll the dough thin, cut into 5 cm squares, fill each with a little meat, fold into triangles and join the corners into small hat shapes.
Bring the broth to a boil with the tomato, add the dumplings and simmer 8–10 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked.
Serve in bowls with coriander, black pepper and vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 set fresh lamb lungs with windpipe (from a halal butcher)
150 g lamb liver and fat, finely diced
steps: Mix the flour, water, a little oil and salt into a thin batter and pour it through the windpipe into the lungs until they swell; tie the windpipe.
Mix the rice with liver, fat, cumin, pepper and salt, fill the intestine loosely and tie the ends.
Simmer the lungs and sausage gently for 50–60 minutes until the lungs are firm and the rice is fully cooked (prick to release air).
Slice both and serve hot with chilli-vinegar sauce, as at Kashgar night markets.

ingredients: 1 green chilli or green pepper, sliced
steps: Soak the onion in cold water for 10 minutes to soften its bite, then drain.
Toss the tomatoes, onion and chilli with salt and vinegar.
Scatter with coriander and serve at once alongside polo or kawap.

ingredients: 300 ml warm milk and water mixed
steps: Knead the flour, yeast, salt, sugar, liquid and oil into a soft dough and rise 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 4 balls, flatten each into a 20 cm round with a thicker rim and a thin centre.
Prick the centre in a pattern with a fork or nan stamp (dukchak), then scatter onion, sesame and nigella and brush with salted water.
Bake in a hot tonur or on a pizza stone at 250°C for 10–12 minutes until golden with a crisp rim, and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Knead flour, water and salt into a soft dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb with onion, cumin, pepper and salt.
Divide dough into 4, roll each into two thin rounds, spread filling on one, cover with the other and seal into 1 cm thick pies.
Pan-fry in oil over medium-low heat, covered, for 8–10 minutes per side until golden and the meat is cooked through, then cut into wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp vegetable oil for the dough
steps: Mix the flour, oil, salt, sugar, pepper and sesame with water into a firm dough, knead smooth and rest 30 minutes in oil.
Roll into thin ropes and stretch them into very fine strands, wrapping them around two chopsticks into loops.
Fry each coil in oil at 170°C for 2–3 minutes, holding the chopsticks apart, until golden and crisp.
Drain and stack; sangza is made for Eid (Rozi Heyt and Qurban Heyt) and served with tea.
